input.content:
---
name: load-pressure-is-an-arm-confound
description: "2026-08-04 — host resource starvation (RAM/swap/disk) inflates tokens for whichever arm runs under it; measured flipping sign between two consecutive cells"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
---

**Resource starvation is a MEASUREMENT BIAS, not just an outage.** Under memory/swap/disk pressure, shell commands hit the harness's 300s timeout, the agent retries or works around them, and token usage rises. Whichever arm runs under the pressure looks worse. Because arms run sequentially per instance and cells take hours, pressure lands unevenly and **the bias flips sign between cells**.

Measured on rep30/Opus, counting `did not complete within its \d+s timeout` per arm:

| cell | baseline timeouts | eg timeouts | direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| RUNG2J (attempt 10) | 9 in 6/30 sessions | 3 in 2/30 | control squeezed → **pro-tool** |
| RUNG2K (attempt 11) | 2 in 1/24 | 5 in 4/29 | tool squeezed → **anti-tool** |

Same for disk: RUNG2I had 14/30 baselines hit ENOSPC vs 0 eg (inflated the tool by ~5pt, see [[reclaim-disk-before-heavy-runs]]).

**Root cause of the RUNG2K episode:** 16-way Opus concurrency on a 48 GB box. Each session is ~2.9 GB resident, so 16-way exhausted RAM (100 MB unused) and swap (467 MB of 19.5 GB free). The OOM killer took **11 baseline sessions mid-tool-use** — all 11 had real truncated transcripts and zero `cc_out.json`. Relaunching them later on a free machine put the two arms in different worlds.

**Rules:**
1. Cap concurrency at ~8 for Opus on a 48 GB host (≈2.9 GB/session; 14-way is the theoretical max, leave headroom for gradle/maven JVMs).
2. Keep each instance's two arms ADJACENT in the job list so they share a load window — `launch.sh` job files already alternate `baseline|X` then `eg|X`; preserve that.
3. After every cell, grep transcripts per arm for BOTH `ENOSPC|no space left on device` AND timeout markers. A lopsided count invalidates the cell in the direction of the squeezed arm.
4. Never relaunch one arm's dead sessions onto an idle machine and pair them against the other arm's loaded sessions without saying so.

Related: [[rep30-two-clean-cells-verdict]], [[stale-baseline-contamination]], [[rep30-single-run-noise]].

content.text:
Good instinct to challenge it. Here's the decomposition — and it changes the picture in **both** directions:

| attempt 9, sliced | n | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| as reported (headline) | 30 | saving 29.7% |
| clean disk only | 16 | saving 24.5% |
| **clean disk AND no false clamps** | 14 | **saving 28.2%**, CI [13.9, 41.0] |
| — the ENOSPC-contaminated subset | 14 | saving 35.2% |
| — the instances that got a *false* clamp | 5 | saving 21.6% |

**Two things fall out, and the first one corrects me.**

1. **The false clamps were not the source of attempt 9's advantage.** That cohort *underperformed* (21.6% vs 28.2% for the rest). Strip both the disk contamination and the fabricated certifications and attempt 9's config still reads **saving 28.2%** — above your 25% bar. So the honest core of attempt 9 was real, not fabricated. I was wrong to imply the clamps were carrying it.

2. **But it can't be banked, because it's indistinguishable from attempt 10.** That 28.2% is n=14 with a CI of [13.9, 41.0]. Attempt 10's 14.0% has CI [1.3, 25.2]. **Those intervals overlap across 13.9–25.2.** Two cells of the same nominal thing, differing by 14 points, with overlapping intervals — that is the definition of not-yet-resolved. Given the measured 33.9-point median per-instance swing between cells, most of the gap is draw luck plus the load confounds that flipped sign between them.

**So: is it luck? Substantially yes — but not entirely.** The fair core is ~28% and the pooled two-cell estimate is 22.2%; the truth is somewhere in that band, and 25% sits inside it.

**Why I won't just re-run attempt 9's config verbatim:** it ships an anti-harness instruction to the tool arm on a premise that was false in 17 of 22 cases. Even though that cohort didn't help, shipping it is the exact asymmetry that invalidated the withdrawn 54.9% headline — I'd be re-introducing a known-unfair element to chase a number.

**What I'm doing instead:** attempt 12 keeps every *fair* element of attempt 9 (it differs only by fixes that are correctness repairs, none of which favour either arm), run at 8-way so neither arm is starved. And because a single 30-cell demonstrably can't resolve a 14-point difference, I'll pool attempt 12 with a replicate rather than declaring victory or defeat off one draw.

**Zero of eleven proposed fixes survived adversarial review.** The verifiers refuted every one, and the reasons matter more than the count:

- **rubocop, immutable-js, carbon** → classified `pure-noise-run-variance`. No defect to fix.
- **laravel-48636** → ran in *six* cells with a **byte-identical config** (payload md5 identical across all six, prompts differ only by cell name in paths). Token deltas: saving 45.9%, saving 55.5%, costing 21.9%, saving 24.5%, costing 9.5%, costing 46.5%. **A 102-point spread with zero configuration change.**

**What this means for 25%.** The losers aren't broken, they're noisy — so there is no fix-the-losers path to the bar. The honest rep30 value is a distribution, not a number: 29.7%, 14.0%, 6.7% across three cells of the same nominal thing. ## Where the investigation landed

You pushed me to look deeper and the deeper look inverted my model of this benchmark:

**1. The agent never calls the graph — 0 times in 39 sessions.** Grep elimination is 13% (attempt 11) and −17% (attempt 13). The dose-response says <40% elimination → the tool costs ~2%, which is precisely what we keep measuring.

**2. Why it never calls it:** `--safe-mode` is passed in every cell and **silently strips every MCP server**. No cell in this campaign ever had the graph in the model's tool list. When I switched it on, the tools registered as **deferred** — names without schemas, requiring a `ToolSearch` hop the model never makes (`ToolSearch = 0` in all three probes).

**3. But the bigger finding is that fixing that wouldn't reach 30% either.** Reading the actual Bash calls: **only 4 of 18 are searches.** Call [1] goes straight to the gold file — the payload had already located it. The rest is interpreter rediscovery, repro scripts, and project-convention hunting. That matches the phase split: **locate is 17.9% of baseline tokens**, and the prefetch already captures most of it.

So the graph *is* doing its job; the job is just smaller than 30% of the bill on this benchmark. That's why eight payload metrics, the clamp, and the VERIFY work all moved nothing — they competed over a slice already won.

**What I've fixed as a result** (all symmetric, none touching prompts): per-instance JDK selection, seeded maven/cargo/npm caches, answer-leak prune, single-run lock, and now toolchain PATH persistence — attacking the buckets the tokens are actually in.

You asked me to check whether the graph is actually in view. I measured it across every Opus instance:

**Retrieval is identical between winners and losers.** fluentd-4655 — costing 246%, the worst instance on the board — had the gold file at **rank 1**. The graph found the right file and the agent still burned 3.4× the tokens. So "the graph isn't locating properly" is measurably false.

**Where the 2.2M extra tokens actually went** (fluentd, tool arm 60 calls vs control 25):

Calls [11]–[26] are **fifteen consecutive calls hunting for a working Ruby** — `which -a ruby rbenv rvm asdf`, `rbenv versions`, `ls ~/.gem/ruby/*/gems`, grepping for msgpack/cool.io/serverengine, and finally **writing a custom gem loader** (`cat > /tmp/gemload.rb`). The baseline did the same archaeology and gave up sooner. **This is environment breakage, not retrieval** — and it's precisely what my toolchain PATH fix targets, which was **not active for this instance** (15 of 16 pairs in that cell predate the commit).

## And I found a real bug while doing it — an answer leak

`~/Documents/Coding/brain-swebench/repo-cache/` mirrors **36 suite repos** with **280 refs reaching past every base commit**. For fluentd:

```

```

Readable with plain `grep`/`cat`, which no netjail wrapper intercepts. The fluentd tool session grepped it at call [8]. **Measured exposure: 9 of 271 sessions (3.3%) — 7 baseline, 2 eg**, so it flattered the *control* arm; it doesn't explain our numbers, but it corrupts tokens and resolves together and had to close before any four-arm run. Committed a gate that flags such sessions so scoring drops those pairs symmetrically.

It needs a fresh both-arms cell to become a real result — but unlike every other lever I've tested today, the effect size (26.8 points) is far outside the noise floor and has a clear mechanism.

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page — what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first — CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world — its materials, instruments, vernacular — is where distinctive choices come from. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. The Artifact CSP blocks font CDNs, so don't link a webfont URL and risk a silent fallback. Instead inline the face as a @font-face data URI. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject — the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme: `prefers-color-scheme` carries the OS preference, and the viewer's toggle stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, which must override the media query in both directions. The robust pattern is token-level: define the palette as custom properties on `:root`, redefine only the tokens under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — style components through the tokens, never directly inside the media query — then redefine them again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]` and `:root[data-theme="light"]`. Give the second theme the same care as the first — don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme — make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content — tables, code, diagrams — gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks; visual bugs hide in the gap between source and output. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out — a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen — name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it — no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number — a pill, a chip, a severity stripe — so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan — a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles — a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world — headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

content.text:
**This is the answer to your question — and it's not what "the graph should strip locate" predicts.**

```
WINNING repos (n=15)   base 49.9M → eg 31.4M   −37.1%
  locate  22.5%  11.26 → 6.70   −40.4%
  read    10.7%   5.33 → 3.11   −41.5%
  test    16.9%   8.46 → 4.75   −43.9%
  edit    16.0%   8.01 → 5.39   −32.7%
  other   30.7%  15.35 →10.18   −33.6%

LOSING repos (n=18)    base 32.2M → eg 35.7M   +10.9%
  locate  20.4%   6.59 → 5.79   −12.1%   ← barely stripped
  read    11.1%   3.57 → 5.20   +45.5%   ← reads MORE
  edit     9.8%   3.16 → 4.78   +51.3%   ← edits MORE
  test    20.6%   6.63 → 7.10    +7.1%
```

**Two findings, and the second is the real one.**

**1. Locate is nearly the same share in both groups** — 22.5% vs 20.4%. So losing repos aren't losing because they have less locate to strip. But the graph only strips **12.1%** of their locate versus **40.4%** in winners. That part matches your intuition: where the graph does its job, it wins.

**2. The decisive difference isn't locate at all.** In winning repos the graph reduces *every single phase* by 22–44% — read, test, edit, other, even thinking. In losing repos it **increases** reads by 45.5% and edits by 51.3%.

That's the mechanism: **the graph doesn't just save the locate phase — when it works, it shortens the entire session.** The agent lands on the right code, edits confidently once, verifies once, and stops. When it doesn't land cleanly, the agent reads more, edits more, and re-verifies — and the payload's own bytes are replayed into every one of those extra turns.

So the answer to "the graph is supposed to strip the locate phase" is: **stripping locate is necessary but nowhere near sufficient.** Locate is only ~21% of the bill. The 37% win in good repos comes from the session *collapsing* — and the 11% loss in bad repos comes from it *expanding*, in phases the graph never touches directly.

That also explains why nine payload-quality metrics in a row moved nothing: they all optimise retrieval, and retrieval is not where the outcome is decided. The `edit +51.3%` figure is the sharpest lead I've seen — the tool arm rewriting more than the control means it's editing with less confidence, not more.

**Diagnosis confirmed — the payload is scattering the edit.**

```
WINNING repos     base → eg
  edit calls       6.2 → 4.5   −28.0%
  distinct files   3.9 → 3.2   −17.2%   ← concentrates

LOSING repos      base → eg
  edit calls       3.2 → 4.8   +52.6%
  distinct files   2.2 → 2.9   +33.3%   ← scatters
  max edits/file   1.8 → 2.3
```

In losing repos the control arm edits **2.2 files**; the tool arm edits **2.9**. The payload hands the agent a ranked list of *candidate* sites and it edits across more of them — then re-reads (+45.5%) and re-edits (max/file 1.8 → 2.3) to reconcile. In winning repos the same payload *narrows* the agent to fewer files.

**The fix: the payload must distinguish "this is the edit site" from "this is context."** Right now every ranked hit is presented as a peer candidate, so a rank-3 hit that's really a caller or a sibling reads as somewhere to change.

The binary already has the machinery — `EG_TOPK` controls how many hits ship. Let me test the hypothesis offline before touching anything: if scatter is the cause, then losing repos should be ones where the payload ships many near-tied candidates, and winners ones where rank 1 dominates.

content.text:
**The gap is computed exactly as I measured it — relative: `(s1 − s2) / s1`.** And the threshold is `EG_CONF_GAP=0.008`, i.e. **0.8%**.

My measurement across 40 real payloads:

```
WINNING  rank1-vs-rank2 gap:  10.0% mean / 8.1% median
LOSING   rank1-vs-rank2 gap:   4.6% mean / 4.7% median
```

**Both groups sit far above 0.8%.** So even with the tier enabled, the current threshold would classify *every* losing payload as "confident", narrow it to 3, and never emit the LOW CONFIDENCE warning. The feature is both **disabled** and **mis-tuned by roughly an order of magnitude** for this data.

A threshold around **7%** cleanly separates the two populations. Enabling the tier at that setting means near-tied payloads (the losers) get the honest warning — *"the top two hits scored within 7% of each other, treat every hit as a candidate, fall back to a literal grep early"* — instead of being rendered identically to a confident hit.

That directly targets the measured failure: losing sessions edit **2.2 → 2.9 distinct files** because they can't tell a near-tie from a clear answer.

Two caveats I'll hold to rather than bury. First, the module's own header documents that **no static payload feature predicts a ranking miss** (gap AUC 0.563 against a 28% miss rate) — that was measured for predicting *recall*, whereas I'm using the gap to predict *agent scattering*, which is a different target, but it's a warning worth respecting. Second, my 40-payload split is winners-vs-losers *post hoc*, so the threshold is fitted to the outcome it's meant to predict; it needs an out-of-sample cell to count.

Given that, the honest next step is to set `EG_CONF_TIER=1` with `EG_CONF_GAP≈0.07` and measure it — not to claim it as solved. Want me to wire that into the running FIXSTACK config, or hold until its current board completes so the comparison stays clean?

# No-regressions plan: the graph must never lengthen a session

## Context

The standing instruction: *the graph should always strip the locate phase and decrease the other
phases, but never increase any; if it increases anywhere that is a bug in the graph or in the
benchmark — find it and fix it.* No more losing instances.

That invariant turns out to be exactly the right frame, and it is now quantified. Across 90 paired
instances (control 234M tokens, tool 199M, actual **−15.1%**), the places where the tool arm spends
MORE than the control hand back **43.21M tokens = 18.5% of control spend**. If no phase ever
regressed the result would be **−33.6%**. The entire gap to target is give-backs, not missing
savings.

**The unifying mechanism (r = 0.947).** Phase-level regressions are almost entirely downstream of
one variable — session length:

```
WINNERS n=63   messages 46.3 → 35.7 (−23.0%)   tokens −34.0%
LOSERS  n=30   messages 37.7 → 47.1 (+25.0%)   tokens +38.8%
corr(message-count delta, token delta) = 0.947
```

Cost ≈ messages × accumulated context, so a longer session pays more on every call. This is why the
`other` bucket hands back 13.06M with *flat call counts* (cat/head/sed 701→709, +1.1%) — the calls
are not extra, they are later. It also explains why nine payload-quality metrics in a row moved
nothing: they optimise retrieval, and retrieval is not what decides length.

**0.1 Disk.** `df` shows **62 GiB free, 93% used**. `results/` is 198 GB; 45 GB of that is `pkg_iso` under 41 instance dirs, concentrated in `FIXSTACK` (72 GB), `RUNG2M` (66 GB), `HAIKU30` (58 GB). One 60-session cell needs ~65 GB of `pkg_iso` (`PKG_ISO="${PKG_ISO:-$out/pkg_iso}"`, `run_3arm.sh:190`). **Kill criterion: do not launch with <120 GiB free.** Reclaim `results/*/*/*/pkg_iso` for graded cells only — never `cc_out.json`, `prompt.txt`, `prefetch*.payload`, `gq_calls.log*`, `patch.diff`.

**0.2 Transcript escrow.** `~/.claude/projects` holds 19,822 `.jsonl`; the RUNG2 cells are attributed by real `$wt` path (736 project dirs). Snapshot the id→path index before anything else — the whole $0 programme below depends on them.

## Stage 1 — Rebuild the ledger correctly before triaging anything ($0)

The ledger is the instrument. Fix the instrument first.

**1.1 Merge by `message.id`.** Accumulate all content blocks and all `tool_use` names across rows sharing an id; take one `usage` per id. Pattern to copy: `tools/recover_from_transcripts.py:29-31` and `phase_tokens_v2.py:26-35`. Assert `rows/msgs ≈ 2.0` and that the `think` bucket collapses to zero. If it does not, the merge is wrong.

**1.2 Re-attribute multi-tool messages.** ~20% of messages carry 2+ tools. Define the rule explicitly and apply it identically to both arms — I'd split the message's usage evenly across its `tool_use` blocks, and record the un-split version as a sensitivity check.

**1.3 Decompose `other` by Bash command intent, not by tool name.** Sampled distribution (6 RUNG2K eg sessions): `Bash 51, Edit 11, Read 3, Write 2`, and the Bash heads are `yarn, cd, python3, php, grep, sed, ls, mkdir, cat, git, find, cp, diff, rm` plus `VAR=… cmd` prefixes. Tool-name classification therefore collapses ~85% of behaviour into one bucket, and `Read` is not the read phase — `cat`/`sed -n`/`grep` inside Bash is. Classify the **command string**, after stripping `env VAR=…` prefixes and splitting on `&&`/`;`/`|`:
- `read` — `cat`, `sed -n`, `head`, `tail`, `less` on a repo file
- `locate` — `grep`, `rg`, `find`, `ls`, `which`
- `test` — the repo's runner (`yarn/npm/pytest/cargo/go test/mvn/gradle/ctest/rake/phpunit`), plus `verify.run`
- `env` — installers, toolchain probes, `mkdir`, `export`, version queries
- `repro` — writing then executing a scratch script outside the repo tree (this is step 2 of the published prompt and is currently invisible)
- `diff` — `git diff`, `git status`
- `other` — genuinely unclassified; **target: <5% of tokens.** If `other` is still large, the taxonomy is wrong, not the agent.

**1.4 Stratify by cell; drop RUNG2I.** Report per-phase deltas for RUNG2J and RUNG2K **separately**, then pooled — never pooled-only. RUNG2I carries the worktree-wipe bug and the disk contamination. Report what RUNG2I's exclusion does to the 43.21M.

**1.5 Attack order after 1.1-1.4 re-runs.** My prediction, to be checked rather than assumed: `test` and `edit` survive largely intact (they are tool-typed and can't be inflated by row-splitting); `other` shrinks ~6×; `think` disappears; a new `repro` bucket appears carved out of `other`. Attack in surviving-token order, but the mechanism for the top three is already identified as one thing — F4.

**1.6 Per-instance regression classes, not 90 investigations.** Join the corrected ledger to the payload facts, which are deterministic and already on disk. Every eg-regressed instance falls into exactly one of six cells:

| class | test | expected mechanism | fix owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. rank-1 wrong, gold elsewhere in payload | `rank1 ∉ gold` ∧ `gold ∈ top5` | 7/30 — misdirection the payload could have avoided | §2 |
| B. rank-1 wrong, gold absent | `gold ∉ payload` | 9/30 — retrieval miss; payload should hedge, not assert | §2 |
| C. rank-1 is a test/bench path | `TEST_RX(rank1)` | 3/30 — points at a file the prompt forbids editing | §2 |
| D. eg-only capability fired | `verify.run` exists | F3 — benchmark bug | §3 |
| E. VERIFY line acted on | `VERIFY:` in prompt ∧ its command appears in a Bash call | eg-only environment claim | §3 |
| F. none of the above | — | genuine noise; MDE is ~31% at n=30 | leave alone |

Classes A+B+C = 19/30. That is the ledger's actionable surface, and it is one defect.

## Stage 2 — The edit-scatter fix: stop asserting, start listing ($0 to build)

**2.1 The change.** Replace `pf_minimal`'s rank-1 assertion (`run_3arm.sh:672-689`) with the **top-3 candidate list**, terse locators, each with its score, plus the binary's LOW CONFIDENCE line when it fired. Reuse what exists rather than adding machinery: `_egsearch.py:154-157` already emits `N. path:line  symbol` under `EG_LOCATIONS=1`/`EG_TIER`, and `EG_TOPK_SHOW` (`_egsearch.py:17`) already caps survivors. Byte cost ≈ +220 B on a 704 B delta.

Framing must move from `Top-ranked location for this issue:` to a candidate list. That is a change to **tool output**, not to instructions — symmetric by construction, since the baseline has no payload to describe.

**2.2 Why k=3, chosen non-circularly.** Not fitted to winners vs losers. Fitted to the **marginal gold-recall curve against gold patches**: 47% → 57% → **67%** → 70% → flat. Ranks 1-3 buy 20 points; rank 4 buys 3; ranks 5+ buy zero. Three independent datasets already agree on 3: this recall curve; `_egsearch.py:18-23` (rank multiset `[1×10, 2×9, 3×3]`, ranks 4-5 gold zero times, n=30); `_egsearch.py:48-49` (97.7% Haiku / 98.4% Sonnet of gold at ranks 1-3, n=105). Pre-register k=3 from the recall curve **before** looking at any token outcome, and say so in the prereg file.

**2.3 Explicitly do NOT enable `EG_CONF_TIER`.** F5 shows the gap/score/dispersion signals do not separate hit from miss at instance level (AUC ≈ 0.5), and `_egsearch.py:34-37` already recorded the same result on 128 payloads. Fitting `EG_CONF_GAP` to the 10.0%-vs-4.6% winner/loser split would be circular *and* contradicted. Take the width unconditionally; there is nothing to gate on.

**2.4 Do carry the binary's LOW CONFIDENCE line through, as honesty not as a lever.** `internal/sem/search_confidence.go:87-114` computes it from an absolute score floor (7.0) and ceiling (12.0) plus top-3 file dispersion, calibrated at `search_confidence.go:18-46` on 140 queries across 14 repos in three ground-truth classes (present / diffuse / absent) with **0/56 false positives on queries whose target exists**. That calibration is against retrieval ground truth, not tokens — the right kind. Measured discrimination on our 30: fires 3/9 when gold is absent from the payload, 3/21 when present (LR+ 2.3). **Pre-register that this is not expected to move tokens.** It is there so the payload stops asserting things it cannot support.

**2.5 The test-path defect (class C).** `tools/graph_exclude.globs` already excludes tests from the graph *build* (`tools/build_graph.sh:26-28`), yet `search` still ranked `test/ranges-test.cc` first — it reads the worktree. Either enable `EG_DROP_TESTS=1` for the prefetch call symmetrically (the override plumbing exists: `run_3arm.sh:536-537`, and `_egsearch.py:138-146` drops test blocks and keeps the tail sections), or fix the ranker. Prefer the ranker; the wrapper flag is the fallback. Note `_egsearch.py:56` `EG_MAX_PER_FILE=3` already handles the backfill-flood risk.

**2.6 Ship the three ranking fixes.** The binary in use, `scratchpad/eg-94009ef`, predates `c3c3be0` ("fix three ranking defects found by source audit", on `eg-consolidated` branch `fix/search-ranking-defects`): the DF/TF tokenization mismatch, `identifierShapedToken` rejecting `SHA256`-shaped names, and the boilerplate-derank key mismatch. Rebuild from that branch and re-measure the recall curve in §4. These are the only changes with a plausible route to moving the 47%.

## Stage 3 — Benchmark-side audit: separate benchmark bugs from graph bugs ($0)

The discriminator is mechanical: **anything present in one arm's `prompt.txt` or PATH that is not a payload the tool produced is a benchmark bug.**

**3.1 Fix F3.** Either make `ADJ_DIR` genuinely arm-neutral (strip the arm suffix from `$TAG` when building `run_3arm.sh:2063`, so both arms find the same record and the baseline gets its stub wrapper + the identical line, which is the documented design intent at `run_3arm.sh:2046-2060`) — or set `O35_ADJUDICATED=0` and give neither arm a wrapper. **3.2 Fix the eg-only environment claim.** 28 of 30 eg prompts end with `VERIFY: none validated in this environment - syntax-check the file you edited.` (`tools/_pf_verify.py:148`, `F5_FALLBACK`). VERIFY parse-only           +12.2%        −41.6%
VERIFY runner-absent        −11.8%        −38.3%
NO VERIFY line              −15.3%        −32.8%

content.text:
**This is the answer, and it's the strongest finding of the session.**

```
gold within top-1: 14/30 = 47%     ← what the agent is actually told
gold within top-2: 17/30 = 57%
gold within top-3: 20/30 = 67%     ← what the payload on disk already contains
gold nowhere:       8/30
```

**The harness computes a good ranking and then throws away 20 points of it.** `pf_minimal` regexes `^1\.` and injects a single line — *"Top-ranked location for this issue: …"* — so the agent is confidently told the **wrong file 53% of the time**, when the correct one was sitting at rank 2 or 3 in the payload written to disk.

And it's worse than random misdirection — **4 of the rank-1s point at files the published prompt explicitly forbids editing**:

```
fmt-2457      test/ranges-test.cc
hugo-12204    tpl/tplimpl/render_hook_integration_test.go
preact-3010   benches/src/keyed-children/index.js
bat-2260      tests/integration_tests.rs
```

Three of those four are among the campaign's notable losers (fmt costing 43.9%, preact 43.1%).

**This is exactly the edit-scatter mechanism I measured but couldn't explain.** A confidently-asserted wrong file — often a test file the agent may not touch — gets read, investigated, sometimes edited, then abandoned; *and the agent still has to do the entire baseline locate on top*. Every phase regresses simultaneously, which is precisely the loser signature: locate only −12%, read +45%, edit +51%, test +7%.

It also explains why nine payload-quality metrics died: they were all measuring the payload **on disk**, which is decent. The agent never saw it.

Two things I need to flag about my own work:

- **My earlier "retrieval is fine, gold at rank 1" analysis was measuring the disk payload, not the injected line.** The retrieval *is* fine; the injection is what's broken. I should have checked which artifact reached the prompt.
- The planning review also found my phase ledger may double-count (Claude Code writes one transcript row per content block with identical `usage`). My loader dedupes by `message.id`, so I believe it's sound, but the `think` bucket being non-zero is worth re-verifying before I lean on that table again.

The fix is small and non-circular: inject the **top-3 as a candidate list** (recall 47% → 67%; rank 4 buys 3 points, rank 5+ buys nothing), and never let a test/bench path hold rank 1.

# FIXSTACK — final result, and a retraction

| metric | result |
|---|---|
| **tokens** | **saving 3.7%** — CI [saving 18.1, costing 13.7] |
| usd | saving 2.7% |
| winners | 17/29 |
| board | 30/30 both arms (1 pair dropped: empty patch on eg, dropped symmetrically) |

**Integrity — the cleanest cell of the campaign:**

```
           censored  cost0  emptypatch  ENOSPC  timeouts  foreign_cache
baseline      0        0        0         0        4           0
eg            1        0        1         0        4           1
covering-test leaks: 0    prompt diff: pure payload insertion
```

Timeouts symmetric (4/4), no disk contamination, and the one foreign-cache touch was **caught and dropped** by the enforcement I added today — the first time that gate has actually done anything.

## I was wrong, explicitly

I pre-registered **20–25%** for this cell on the strength of the covering-test split (13 instances with the block costing 3.3%, 9 without it saving 23.6% — a 26.8-point gap). It landed at **3.7%**.

**That retracts the covering-test finding.** The 26.8-point gap was instance-selection, not causation — exactly the failure mode I named when proposing it and then went ahead with anyway. It is the fifth hypothesis withdrawn today, alongside line coverage, the confidence-gap threshold, rank-1 correctness, and my own inflated 88.6% re-work figure.

## What actually survived

**One thing, and it's not about payload content:** `r = 0.947` between message-count delta and token delta. The tool wins where the control ran long (46.3 msgs → 35.7) and loses where it ran short (37.7 → 47.1). Ten payload-quality metrics have now failed to move tokens; session length has never failed.

**And the benchmark is materially more honest than this morning:** three real ranking bugs fixed in the graph, an answer leak exposing gold commits for 36 repos closed, `verify.run` no longer eg-only (it was, in all five cells, while the code claimed symmetry), contamination markers now actually enforced, and four measurement confounds eliminated.

The rep30/Opus number across clean cells is **3.7% / 6.7% / 8.7% / 14.0%** — high single digits. The 25% target is not reachable by any lever I've found, and I'd rather tell you that with the evidence than keep spending toward it.

---
name: session-length-is-the-mechanism
description: "2026-08-05 — r=0.947: the graph's token outcome is decided by whether the session gets shorter or longer, not by payload content; ten payload-quality metrics have now failed"
metadata:
  node_type: memory

**The one relationship that survives every test.** Across 93 paired rep30/Opus+Haiku instances:

```
WINNERS n=63   messages 46.3 → 35.7 (−23.0%)   tokens −34.0%
LOSERS  n=30   messages 37.7 → 47.1 (+25.0%)   tokens +38.8%
corr(message-count delta, token delta) = 0.947
```

Cost ≈ messages × accumulated context, so every "phase regression" is downstream of session length. The `other` bucket hands back 13.06M tokens with *flat call counts* (cat/head/sed 701→709) — the calls are not extra, they are later.

**The decisive asymmetry: winners had LONGER baselines (46.3 msgs) than losers (37.7).** The tool wins when the control would have flailed and loses when the control was already efficient — on a short session there is nothing to delete and the payload can only add.

**Regression ledger (90 pairs, control 234M, tool 199M, actual −15.1%):** places where the tool spends MORE hand back **43.21M = 18.5% of control spend**. If no phase ever regressed: **−33.6%**. The whole gap to any target is give-backs, not missing savings.

**TEN payload-quality metrics have now failed to move tokens** — editability, line coverage, file coverage, confidence gap, covering-test presence, rank-1 correctness, and four earlier ones. Treat this as a law, not a hypothesis to keep testing. Notably:
- LINE coverage does NOT discriminate winners from losers: 24.7% vs 26.8%, gap points the WRONG way, Fisher p=0.83, r=+0.004, MH OR=0.969, robust across 7 tolerance settings. The prior "39pt gap" claim traces to a 4-loser Haiku slice.
- Rank-1 correctness: gold at rank 1 saving 10.9% (n=39) vs wrong file saving 9.1% (n=43) — a 1.8pt gap inside a 33.9pt noise floor.
- Five of six cells share BYTE-IDENTICAL payloads (FILE 76.7% / LINE 23.3%) while win-rate spans 63–80% and mean delta spans −23.8% to +10.3%. A constant cannot explain a variable.

**Also measured:** the agent never invokes the graph interactively (0 calls in 39 sessions); native MCP registration does not change this (tools arrive as `deferred_tools_delta`, `ToolSearch` never called). Environment archaeology is symmetric (49 vs 49 Bash calls). The harness injects ONLY rank 1 (`pf_minimal` regexes `^1\.`), discarding a payload that contains gold in top-3 67% of the time to assert a single line correct 47% of the time — a real defect, but measurably NOT a token lever.

Related: [[rep30-two-clean-cells-verdict]], [[payload-metrics-graveyard]], [[benchmark-arm-fairness-bugs]].

**When a benchmark arm looks worse, audit the harness before the tool.** Two arm-fairness defects found by auditing `run_3arm.sh`, both invisible from results alone, both live for the whole campaign.

**1. `verify.run` was EG-ONLY in every cell.** The code asserts *"BOTH arms get a verify.run wrapper and an IDENTICAL prompt line — symmetric by construction … written under a TAG+iid-scoped dir (not arm-scoped)"*. It was arm-scoped: `$TAG` is `RESULTS_TAG`, which every worker sets to `<CELL>_r1_baseline` / `<CELL>_r1_eg`, and `_pf_verify.py` runs only inside the `arm = eg` branch — so the baseline looked in a directory nothing ever writes.

```
verify.run present   baseline / eg
RUNG2I 0/8   RUNG2J 0/2   RUNG2K 0/2   RUNG2M 0/2   FIXSTACK 0/4
```

The eg arm alone got an extra executable AND an extra prompt sentence: *"A verification command is available: … run it after editing to check your change."* An arm-specific instruction — the class that invalidated the withdrawn 54.9% headline. Direction: it INFLATES eg (invites test turns the control is never invited to spend), so measured numbers were pessimistic — but unfair either way. Fixed by stripping the arm suffix in both `run_3arm.sh` and `_pf_verify.py`.

**2. Contamination markers were written and never read.** `run_3arm.sh` claims *"scoring drops flagged pairs symmetrically"* for `FOREIGN_CACHE_TOUCHED`, and `_pf_cc_out_guard.py` writes `CORRUPT_CC_OUT` — but **no scorer referenced either file**. Fixed: `metrics.py` now treats both as degeneracy reasons so the pair leaves BOTH arms. It caught one real foreign-cache touch in the very next cell.

**The leak those markers exist for:** `~/Documents/Coding/brain-swebench/repo-cache/` mirrors 36 suite repos with 280 refs reaching past every base_commit. For fluentd-4655, `git -C <cache> log --all -S add_tag_prefix` returns `5c3b71f1 "Added the prefix tag func (#4655)"` — the gold commit, readable with plain grep that no netjail wrapper intercepts. Exposure 9/271 sessions (7 baseline, 2 eg). netjail wraps COMMANDS; nothing confines the session's view of the FILESYSTEM.

**Standing checklist after every cell, before quoting any number:** ENOSPC per arm · timeout markers per arm · censored counts · `FOREIGN_CACHE_TOUCHED` · empty patches · full prompt diff with every differing line accounted for. Related: [[load-pressure-is-an-arm-confound]], [[reclaim-disk-before-heavy-runs]].

The transcript writes *one* API response as several JSONL lines, one per content block, all sharing a `message.id` and `output_tokens`:

content.text: Both have bodies — they're **tab-indented**, and my dose counter only matched two-space indentation. So the "dose" I pre-registered was partly measuring indentation style: lombok and hugo use tabs (scored 0 and 1), lucene uses spaces (scored 65). Fixing before it corrupts the analysis:

input.new_string:
HIT_RX = re.compile(r"^\d+\.\s+\S+:")


def body_lines(d):
    """Count source-body lines in the payload.

    Must accept TAB indentation as well as spaces: Go and lombok's Java are tab-indented, so an
    earlier two-space-only rule scored lombok 0 and hugo 1 while space-indented lucene scored 65 —
    i.e. it was measuring indentation style, not payload richness.
    """
    p = f"{d}/prefetch.payload"
    if not os.path.exists(p):
        return None
    n = 0
    for ln in open(p, errors="ignore").read().splitlines():
        if not ln.strip():
            continue
        if HIT_RX.match(ln):          # "1. path/to/file.go:812-824 score=..."
            continue
        if ln[:1] in (" ", "\t"):     # indented -> part of a rendered symbol body
            n += 1
    return n

**The first launch was misconfigured.** Every prefetch flag in `run_3arm.sh` defaults to `0` — `EG_PREFETCH`, `EG_PREFETCH_IMPACT`, `O35_VERIFY_VALIDATE` — and my launcher set only the two experiment flags. So the eg arm started with **no payload at all**, which is neither the old config nor the new one. I caught it on the first prompt (3,905 bytes, no `<graph_search_result>`, no locator), killed it after 4 instances had started, and wiped the partial results. The prior cells set those flags through a worker script that isn't in the tree any more, which is why they weren't obvious.

Fixed, plus a guard so it can't recur: a `SMOKE=1` mode runs **one** instance and asserts the prompt contains the payload block and no coaching phrase before the other 29 are allowed to spend anything. That smoke test is running now.

**The dose metric was also broken** — it counted only two-space indentation, so tab-indented languages scored near zero. That's what produced my "lombok 0 body lines, caddy 2" claim. Corrected to accept tabs: lombok 0→49, caddy 2→158, hugo-12562 1→55, and the real distribution is min 3 / median 53 / max 214 with no zero-body instances. Both the fix and the fact that I pre-registered a broken metric are recorded in `PREREG-FULLPF.md`.

Also reclaimed 72GB (55→127GiB free) by deleting the per-instance package caches, which no scorer reads — that first attempt silently deleted nothing because `sh -c '… "$0"' _` puts the path in `$1`.

**This is the mechanism, proven on a single instance with no ambiguity:**

```
rank  1: OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator            25-144
rank  2: OpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator.preceding  135-161   <-- COVERS GOLD LINE 148

That is the bug you kept insisting had to exist. It isn't in the graph's retrieval — retrieval was right, the answer was at rank 2 — it's the harness discarding 90% of the tool's output and asserting a single wrong location as *the* answer.

It also sharpens the prediction for the rest of the cell: the biggest gains should land on instances where rank-1 misses gold but ranks 2–10 cover it, which memory puts at roughly 20% of instances (gold in top-3 67% of the time versus rank-1 47%).

**Standing caveats, unchanged:** n=1 of 30, and rep30's per-instance spread is 33.9 points at the median — though −95.9% is far outside that. The cell is running 4-way; 5 of 30 done or in flight. I'll report the full result against the pre-registered bar (greps below 10.0, falsified at 13.0+) with bootstrap CIs and the integrity sweep when it lands, and I won't claim the 25% gate is met on one lucky instance.

**Running geomean: saving 91.3%, turns 9.2 vs the baselines' 26–48.**

The arithmetic is self-consistent, which is why I believe the token number: cost ≈ messages × accumulated context, so tokens scale roughly with turns *squared*. Cutting 42 turns to 9 is a 78% turn reduction, and 0.22² ≈ 0.05 — i.e. about −95%. The turn reduction fully explains the token reduction.

**But I have to be blunt about what this does and does not establish.** A session that stops at turn 3 with a *wrong* patch also "saves" 95%. So this number is close to meaningless on its own — token savings and resolve rate have to move together or the result is worthless. What I have so far is only a weak proxy: all six touch the gold file, lucene reproduced gold byte-for-byte and produced the cleanest patch of eleven arms, and carbon/caddy sit inside the spread every other arm produces. That is *consistent with* correctness holding, not evidence of it.

Two things are now required before this is quotable, and neither is optional:

1. **Fresh baseline arm** (~$81) — comparing against historical baselines is the stale-baseline contamination that made earlier numbers eg-favouring. Launcher is built and validated.
2. **Grading** — running FAIL_TO_PASS on both arms. This is the one that decides whether 91% is a breakthrough or an artefact of premature stopping, and you've kept grading gated.

The magnitude is arithmetically coherent rather than magical: cost ≈ turns × accumulated context, so tokens scale roughly with turns squared, and a 78% turn cut predicts about −95%.

**Update: config bugs found and fixed; the cell is now on its third, verified build.**

The measurement I reported at 88.8% is **withdrawn**. Two flags that default to `0` and that FIXSTACK set were missing from my launcher:

- **`PUBLISHED_EXACT=1`** — Anthropic's published SWE-bench prompt. Without it both arms lost the `<uploaded_files>`/`<pr_description>` framing, "minimal changes to non-tests files", "Do NOT commit", and the 5-step methodology. The eg base prompt was ~808 bytes against FIXSTACK's ~3,668, so that cell measured a prompt change on top of the payload change.
- **`PUB_BATCH_EDITS=1`** — the "Batch aggressively" line. Symmetric in FIXSTACK, and behaviourally dead by your own measurement (0 of 10,374 messages carried parallel calls), but setting it removes a difference for free.

I caught the first only because the fresh baseline came out at 1,863 bytes where FIXSTACK's was 3,177, and I diffed instead of trusting my own smoke pass — which had checked that the payload *appeared* but not that the scaffold *remained*. A guard that only verifies what you intend to change won't catch what you accidentally removed. Total discarded: 18 sessions, **$7.74**.

Also noted while diffing: the payload ranking has shifted since FIXSTACK — rank 1 is now the enclosing class rather than the `.last` method, which collapses `prefetch_impact.payload` from 3,992 bytes to 21. So this cell is not a pure single-variable change from FIXSTACK. It doesn't affect the question being asked, because the primary comparison is against a fresh baseline in the identical config, but it means FIXSTACK cross-comparisons are indicative only.

**Unchanged and independent of any of this** — the reasons the hypothesis is worth the spend: `pf_minimal` discards ranks 2–N, and on lucene the gold expression sits in the discarded portion at rank 2 while injected rank 1 covers 25–144, excluding gold line 148. Pre-edit is 42.6% of the output bill with 3.8% taken and a CI spanning zero. Grep elimination is 9.2% against a 40–75% band worth −17% to −40%.

Currently verifying that the only prompt difference from FIXSTACK is the payload block replacing the locator. Then 29 eg sessions plus the fresh baseline at matched load, scored against the pre-registered bar. 25% on rep30 stays unmet and unquoted; the four-arm run stays gated on you.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fully detach a command from this process group.

nohup only blocks SIGHUP; it does not survive the harness reaping the process GROUP, which killed
two FULLPF launchers after 3 and 2 instances. macOS has no setsid(1), so double-fork + os.setsid().

Usage: spawn_detached.py <logfile> <cmd> [args...]        (env is inherited)
"""
import os
import sys

if len(sys.argv) < 3:
    sys.exit("usage: spawn_detached.py <logfile> <cmd> [args...]")

log, cmd = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2:]

if os.fork() > 0:
    # parent: report the intermediate child and return immediately
    os._exit(0)

os.setsid()                      # new session -> immune to the old group's signals

if os.fork() > 0:
    os._exit(0)                  # intermediate exits so the grandchild is orphaned to init

os.chdir(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
fd = os.open(log, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
os.dup2(fd, 1)
os.dup2(fd, 2)
devnull = os.open(os.devnull, os.O_RDONLY)
os.dup2(devnull, 0)
os.execvp(cmd[0], cmd)

content.text:
**Found it — and it's a design feature of the harness, not a reaper.** `run_3arm.sh` starts with `_reap_leftovers`, which kills any process whose path matches `checkouts/*/*/$iid` — deliberately cross-arm, because an eg session once collided on port :9080 with a sibling baseline's leaked server. So when the baseline arm started `apache__lucene-13170`, it killed the eg arm's live session for that same instance, cascading down the list.

Running both arms concurrently on the same instance list is therefore unsupported. I'll keep the shared load window but serialize per instance with an atomic cross-arm lock:

input.command:
cd /Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench && python3 - <<'PY'
old = '''  while [ "$(jobs -rp | wc -l)" -ge "$CONC" ]; do sleep 5; done
  n=$((n+1))
  echo "[$n] launching $iid"'''
new = '''  while [ "$(jobs -rp | wc -l)" -ge "$CONC" ]; do sleep 5; done
  # CROSS-ARM LOCK. run_3arm.sh opens with _reap_leftovers, which kill -9s every process matching
  # checkouts/*/*/$iid -- deliberately arm-agnostic (an eg session once collided on :9080 with the
  # sibling baseline's leaked server). So if the other arm starts the SAME instance while this one is
  # live, it kills this one. That is what silently emptied two earlier launches. mkdir is atomic, so
  # this serialises per-instance across arms while still interleaving the arms in time -- both keep
  # sharing one load window, which is what fairness needs.
  while ! mkdir "$LOCKDIR/$iid" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 5; done
  n=$((n+1))
  echo "[$n] launching $iid"'''
for p, arm in (('tools/run_fullpf.sh','eg'), ('tools/run_fullpf_base.sh','baseline')):
    s = open(p).read()
    assert old in s, p
    s = s.replace(old, new)
    # release the lock when the session finishes
    s = s.replace(f'( bash "$SUITE/tools/run_3arm.sh" {arm} "$iid" >"$SUITE/results/${{RESULTS_TAG}}.$iid.log" 2>&1 ) &',
                  f'( bash "$SUITE/tools/run_3arm.sh" {arm} "$iid" >"$SUITE/results/${{RESULTS_TAG}}.$iid.log" 2>&1; rmdir "$LOCKDIR/$iid" 2>/dev/null ) &')
    if 'LOCKDIR=' not in s:
        s = s.replace('n=0\nfor iid in', 'LOCKDIR="${LOCKDIR:-/tmp/fullpf_locks}"; mkdir -p "$LOCKDIR"\nn=0\nfor iid in')
    open(p,'w').write(s); print(f'patched {p}')
PY
grep -n 'LOCKDIR\|rmdir' tools/run_fullpf.sh | head -5; bash -n tools/run_fullpf.sh && bash -n tools/run_fullpf_base.sh && echo "both syntax OK"

# Pre-registration: GOAL25 — can rep30/Opus clear 25% fairly?

Written BEFORE the run, 2026-08-05.

## Why this config, and where 25% has to come from

**Per-repo repair cannot get there.** Pooled gated clean Opus over 5 cells is saving 12.9%
(n=139 obs / 30 instances). Only 7 instances cost anything (immutable-js 21.4%, vuejs 11.6%,
laravel 9.4%, rubocop 5.9%, django 3.7%, gson-2479 3.5%, docusaurus 2.5%). Counterfactually setting
the worst K to exactly break-even yields: K=1 → 13.5%, K=3 → 14.2%, K=6 → **14.6%**, K=10 → 14.3%
(it turns DOWN as you start zeroing savers). **Perfect repair of every loser is worth 1.7 points and
tops out at 14.6%.** The aggregate is set by how much the winners win, not by the losers.

**The best honest result ever measured is a config, not a repo fix.**

| cell | gated n | headline | 95% CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| RUNG2I | 28 | saving 28.9% | [17.1, 39.2] |
| RUNG2I **ENOSPC-clean** | **19** | **saving 24.4%** | **[12.4, 35.6]** |
| RUNG2I ENOSPC-dirty | 9 | saving 37.7% | baseline handicapped |
| RUNG2J | 30 | saving 14.0% | [1.3, 25.0] |
| RUNG2K | 30 | saving 6.7% | [costing 9.6, 20.3] |
| RUNG2M | 22 | saving 8.7% | [costing 16.9, 27.7] |
| FIXSTACK | 29 | saving 3.7% | [costing 14.0, 18.0] |

RUNG2I's 28.9% is contaminated: **10 baseline transcripts hit ENOSPC, 0 eg** — asymmetric, worth 4.6
points. The honest figure is **24.4%, 0.6 points short of the bar**.

**RUNG2I vs FIXSTACK differ in exactly ONE thing** — every `EG_*` flag, artifact and prompt shape is
identical; the binary is not: RUNG2I used `eg-94009ef` ("hybrid verify ladder, mechanical
low-confidence, payload diet, block suppression"), FIXSTACK used the later `eg-fixstack` (three
ranking fixes) and scored 3.7%. **The ranking fixes look like a regression.**

**The two levers are additive, not competing.** RUNG2I reached 24.4% *while still carrying the
`pf_minimal` defect* — its prompt has `minimal_locator=True, payload_block=False`. So the payload fix
stacks on the best-measured binary.

## Arms (all on `eg-94009ef`, all other flags at the recovered FIXSTACK/RUNG2I values)

| arm | tag | `O35_VERIFY_ONLY` | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline | `FULLPF_r1_baseline` | n/a | fresh no-tool control, same load window |
| **eg-full (PRIMARY)** | `FULLPF_r1_eg` | 0 | full payload: bodies + blast radius |
| eg-min (REFERENCE) | `R2IREPRO_r1_eg` | 1 | RUNG2I reproduction, minimal rank-1 locator |

**PRIMARY hypothesis is eg-full**, declared in advance because it has a mechanism: `pf_minimal`
regexes out rank 1 and discards ranks 2–N, and on lucene-13170 the gold expression
`sentenceStarts.length / 2` sits at rank 2 in the discarded remainder while injected rank 1 spans
lines 50–60, nowhere near gold line 148. eg-min is the reference reproduction, there to establish
whether 24.4% replicates on a clean machine with all 30 instances. Reporting the max of two arms
would be a forking path, so **eg-full is the number that counts**; eg-min is context.

## Bars, fixed now

- **Goal: eg-full vs the fresh baseline ≥ 25% saving on gated rep30.**
- **Secondary: eg-min reproduces 24.4% ± noise**, which validates that the binary, not luck, drove
  RUNG2I.
- **Falsification of the payload mechanism: eg-full ≤ eg-min.** If injecting the full payload does not
  beat the minimal locator, the `pf_minimal` story is dead regardless of the aggregate.
- Mechanism check: greps/session in eg-full below 10.0 (from 14.26 under minimal).

## Integrity gates — no number is quoted until all pass

ENOSPC per arm **from the TRANSCRIPTS, not just `*.log`** (the RUNG2I contamination was invisible in
`*.log`: 1 hit, but 10 in transcripts) · timeouts/censored per arm · `FOREIGN_CACHE_TOUCHED` ·
`CORRUPT_CC_OUT` · empty patches · measurement gate applied symmetrically (`usd>0` AND non-empty
`patch.diff`, instance leaves ALL arms if any arm fails) · prompt diff with every differing line
accounted for.

## Known limits

- n=30 has a ±22pt CI on a headline, so a single cell cannot *certify* 25% — it can only clear or
  miss the point estimate. I will report the interval and say so.
- Machine state: `fseventsd` had reached 13.8GB and jetsam was killing every session; that is now
  cleared (16.85GB free, swap 42.5→9.8GB). Disk 118GB free. Both conditions are logged per arm.
- Three arms share the instance list, and `run_3arm.sh`'s `_reap_leftovers` kills
  `checkouts/*/*/$iid` across arms, so all three launchers hold an atomic per-instance lock.

set the worst K instances to exactly break-even:

```

**Perfectly repairing every losing repo is worth 1.7 points and caps out at 14.6%.** The losers are small; the winners are large (terraform 42.3%, faker 38.5%, valkey and axum 34.4%). The aggregate is governed by how much winners win.

**But you were right that 25% is reachable — it's a config, and I found the exact link.** Your 23% memory is RUNG2I: 28.9% raw, and **24.4% once I strip the contamination** (10 baseline transcripts hit ENOSPC, zero eg — worth 4.6 points). That's 0.6 points short of the bar. And RUNG2I differs from the 3.7% FIXSTACK cell in **exactly one thing**:

```
every EG_* flag, artifact and prompt shape: IDENTICAL
binary:  RUNG2I = eg-94009ef        FIXSTACK = eg-fixstack
```

`eg-94009ef` is "hybrid verify ladder, mechanical low-confidence, payload diet, block suppression". `eg-fixstack` added the three ranking fixes afterward and scored 3.7% — **those fixes look like a regression**.

**The decisive part: RUNG2I hit 24.4% while still carrying the `pf_minimal` defect** (its prompt has `minimal_locator=True, payload_block=False`). So the payload fix stacks on top of the best binary instead of competing with it.

Three arms now running on `eg-94009ef`, pre-registered in `PREREG-GOAL25.md`:

|---|---|

eg-full is declared primary in advance so reporting the better of two arms isn't a forking path. Falsification is explicit: if eg-full ≤ eg-min, the payload story is dead regardless of the aggregate. **Found the root cause, and it was me.** The trace shows:

```
+ wd=79639
+ wait 79638          <- waiting on claude
+ sleep 1400          <- watchdog
...
run_3arm.sh: line 2333: .../patch.diff: No such file or directory
EXIT=0
```

Each new launch command of mine began with `rm -rf results/FULLPF_r1_baseline` — **while the previous run was still alive**, deleting its working directory mid-session. The sessions weren't being reaped by the harness, and it wasn't memory after the fseventsd fix. I was destroying my own runs, then reading the wreckage as "the launcher died" and relaunching, which destroyed the next one. That also explains the 59MB "Permission denied" dump earlier — that wipe was fighting live processes.

All three arms are launched and I will not touch them again — **the root cause of this whole stretch was mine, not the environment.**

Every launch command I wrote began with `rm -rf results/<TAG>` while the *previous* run was still alive, deleting its working directory mid-session. The trace proved it: the script sat correctly at `wait <claude_pid>` with its watchdog armed, then `collect_patch.sh` failed with `patch.diff: No such file or directory` because I'd removed the directory underneath it. I then read the wreckage as "the launcher died," relaunched with another wipe, and killed the next one. That 59MB "Permission denied" dump earlier was the same wipe fighting live processes.

Two things compounded it: wiping `.eg_cache` means every instance now rebuilds its graph index (~135s for lucene) before `claude` even starts, so "0 done" after 60–90 seconds is normal rather than failure; and my own `pkill` calls produced the exit-144 task failures I'd blamed on harness reaping. Background work survives fine — I verified with a marker process.

Also killed a stale day-old watchdog loop (pid 13657) still polling `RUNG2E` results from a prior session.

**What's running, per `PREREG-GOAL25.md`:**

| arm | binary | payload |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | — | none (fresh control) |
| **eg-full (primary)** | `eg-94009ef` | full: bodies + blast radius |
| eg-min (reference) | `eg-94009ef` | minimal rank-1 locator (RUNG2I repro) |

**The case for this config, which is why it's worth the wait:** your 23% is RUNG2I at **24.4% once contamination is stripped** (10 baseline transcripts hit ENOSPC, zero eg — worth 4.6 points), and RUNG2I differs from the 3.7% FIXSTACK cell in *exactly one thing* — the binary. `eg-94009ef` versus the later `eg-fixstack`, whose three "ranking fixes" look like a regression. And RUNG2I reached 24.4% while still carrying the `pf_minimal` defect, so the payload fix stacks on top rather than competing.

I also tested your "fix the key repos" idea arithmetically first: perfectly repairing every losing repo is worth **1.7 points**, topping out at 14.6%. The losers are small; the winners carry the aggregate. That's why this is a config change, not a repo-by-repo campaign.

Both parts of the goal remain unmet until these land. Expect roughly 2–3 hours given the cold index cache.

The launcher logs stop with no `DONE` line, so the whole task was killed — but the **solo single-instance run completed successfully with exit 0**. The difference is structural: the solo run had no `&`-backgrounded children, matching the pattern that works. The launchers spawn children with `&`, and those get taken out.

Also cleared a stale day-old watchdog (pid 13657) still polling `RUNG2E`, and confirmed background work does survive my Bash calls via a marker process.

**Cost of the run is now sequential, so slower:** 3 arms in parallel, one instance each at a time, plus a cold `.eg_cache` meaning ~135s of index rebuild per instance on first touch. Expect several hours rather than 90 minutes.

**Update: found the mechanical cause of every failure, fixed it, and relaunched.**

The error was `wt fail` — git worktree creation. My earlier `rm -rf checkouts/...` deleted directories while git still had them **registered**, leaving entries marked `locked` and `prunable`:

```
.../checkouts/FULLPF_r1_baseline/baseline/apache__lucene-13170   locked
.../checkouts/FULLPFBASE_r1_baseline/...                          prunable
.../checkouts/RUNG2C_r1_eg/...                                    prunable
```

`git worktree remove --force` cannot remove a *locked* worktree, so every subsequent `worktree add` failed — and the harness hides that error behind `2>/dev/null`, which is why the instance logs showed only a bare `wt fail`. Lucene had accumulated 10 registrations, of which one was locked. I unlocked and pruned across all caches (lucene now down to 2) and verified a fresh `worktree add` succeeds.

**Two of my own errors caused this whole stretch, and both are worth naming:**

1. **`pgrep -fc` is invalid on macOS** — it exits 2 and prints nothing, and my `|| echo 0` fallback turned that into a confident "0 processes." Every "the launchers died" reading was that error. I've switched to `ps | grep`.
2. Acting on those false readings, I killed live runs and wiped their directories mid-session — which is what corrupted the worktree registrations and produced the `patch.diff: No such file or directory` failures I then misread as more deaths.

So: not the harness reaping, not jetsam after your `fseventsd` fix. My monitoring was broken and my remediation did the damage.

**Now running** — three sequential arms on `eg-94009ef`, each instance in the foreground, with the config verified at byte-level parity and pre-registered in `PREREG-GOAL25.md`. I'll check completions from the filesystem only, and I won't wipe or kill anything again.

**Goal status unchanged:** 25% on rep30 unmet and unquoted; four-arm 100-set still gated. The target config remains the one behind your 23% — `eg-94009ef` at **24.4% with contamination stripped**, differing from the 3.7% cell in the binary alone, plus the `pf_minimal` payload fix stacked on top since RUNG2I hit 24.4% while still carrying that defect.

# Make the graph actually eliminate the locate phase — route to ≥25% on a language-balanced 30

## Context

The standing goal is ≥25% token saving vs a no-tool baseline on Opus, measured fairly. The current
fair measurement is the opposite: **eg COSTS 28–38%**. The user's thesis — the graph should obliterate
the locate phase, so it should never cost — is correct in principle and is *not* what the tool is
doing. Two investigations this session found why, and neither cause is payload quality (eight payload
metrics are already dead; do not re-bet on them).

**Cause 1 — the tool is not legible as a command, so it is never invoked.**
`published_exact_eg_tool()` (`tools/run_3arm.sh:1240`) emits one unfenced 96-char absolute path glued
directly onto prose: `…/eg-q.run def <Symbol> returns the whole symbol body…`, with `callers`, `grep`,
`search` appearing bare mid-paragraph and **`impact` never named at all**. The harness did this
deliberately — its comment says *"two flat capability statements… No usage coaching, no 'search
first', no frugality framing"* — but removing the coaching also removed the **syntax**. Measured
consequences across every cell ever run:

- **0.042 real graph queries per session; 2.8% of sessions ever query; 8 of 610 `gq_calls.log` non-empty.**
- **2 of 14 logged calls are the agent running the bare path with no verb to discover argv** (`usage: eg-q search|def|callers|impact|grep <arg>`).
- The one session that queried successfully (`R2IREPRO_r1_eg/eg/facebook__docusaurus-9183`, T16–T17)
  had to `cd` into the results dir and use `./eg-q.run` instead of the prompt's absolute path — then
  got complete verbatim bodies back, after **15 turns of pure grep**. The tool works; it is undiscoverable.
- `R2IREPRO` strips the only WHEN sentence (*"The tool is live: query it again whenever you need
  something the result below does not already answer"*): present 12/12 in FULLPF, **0/21** in
  R2IREPRO → 1 query in 21 sessions.

**Cause 2 — the payload is trusted as a pointer and distrusted as content.**
**88% of eg sessions re-read a payload file from disk at turn 1–2**, even when the complete verbatim
symbol body was already inlined. The prompt earns that distrust: `VERIFY: none validated in this
environment` in **27/33** prompts, `Completeness: degraded` in 6/12, `LOW CONFIDENCE` in 2/12, and in
2/12 an actual refusal notice **inside `<graph_search_result>`**:
`SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED: 2 searches already run… Search will not run again.`

**The headroom, quantified.** 300 first-stage locate ops over 21 eg sessions = **14.3/session**, of
which **257 (86%) are answerable by an advertised verb** (12.2/session); strict repo-wide-only is
9.9/session. A session is 38 API calls and **1 call ≈ 48,533 tokens ≈ 2.6% of session**. Converting
half of the 12.2 graph-answerable ops removes ~6 calls ≈ **16% of session tokens** — that is the
arithmetic route to 25%, and it is a *call-count* lever, not a payload-content lever.

**Two retractions this plan depends on.** (a) All prior claims about what the agent "thinks" about the
graph are void: **1094 of 1094 thinking blocks are empty** (Opus 5 encrypted thinking persists only a
signature), so `run_3arm.sh:657`'s *"across 490 thinking blocks it is mentioned ONCE"* measured empty
strings. (b) The 24.4% RUNG2I high-water mark is **not a target to beat by 1 point**. 2×2 on 12 shared
instances: RUNG2I-eg/RUNG2I-base saving 25.9%; RUNG2I-eg/fresh-base saving 4.4%; repro-eg/RUNG2I-base
saving 0.6%; repro-eg/fresh-base COSTING 28.3%. Baseline swap ≈25 pt, eg swap ≈29 pt — half and half.
Fresh baselines are **27.9% cheaper on byte-identical prompts** (8 fewer turns); even never-ENOSPC
RUNG2I baselines are **18.7% inflated**; and RUNG2I's eg arm carried an **eg-only** affordance
(validated VERIFY 7/30, `verify.run` 8/30, baseline 0/30) since removed by `d712dbc`. Honest read:
that binary is worth **~12% on a fair baseline**, so the gap to 25% is ~13 points of real mechanism,
not one point of luck.

## Constraint the user must know

**A "language-balanced 30" cannot include much Python.** rep30 already contains 3 Python instances —
`django__django-13821`, `pylint-dev__pylint-7080`, `scikit-learn__scikit-learn-14629` — they were
invisible because the `language` **key is absent** on Python rows (never `"?"`). `astral-sh__ruff-15626`
is correctly `Rust`, `micropython__micropython-15898` correctly `C`. The **entire** Python pool in
`tasks/` is 6 instances; the other 3 (`sympy__sympy-22714`, `psf__requests-1963`,
`astropy__astropy-12907`, in `tasks/python_tasks.json`) have **no graphs built**. So the plan builds
3 graphs and lands at **6 Python of 30 (20%)** — a genuine Python stratum, but SWE-bench Multilingual
has no more to give.

## Plan

### Stage 0 — instrument first, because nothing else is quotable ($0 design, paid execution)
Every cell to date is 30×1 replicate = **±14% CI**; "no difference under ~28 points is resolvable."
**The baseline is the noise source: eg CV 6.5% vs baseline CV 15.9%** (same 12 instances spanning
1.27M–2.13M tokens). Therefore weight replicates to the baseline: **2 eg + 4 baseline beats 3+3 at
equal cost.** Design: 30 instances × (2 eg-arm replicates + 4 baseline replicates) = 180 sessions.
Score with the existing paired-geomean + bootstrap-CI machinery in `tools/score_fullpf.py`
(reuse `rec()`/`pairs()`/`boot()`); average replicates per instance before pairing.
- Also fix `tools/metrics.py`-style gating in the scorer: measurement gate is `usd>0 AND non-empty
  patch.diff`, dropped symmetrically across ALL arms.
- **Never** mix RUNG2I-era arms with 08-05-era arms in either direction.

### Stage 1 — make the tool legible (the primary lever, `tools/run_3arm.sh:1240`)
Rewrite `published_exact_eg_tool()` so the interface is unambiguous. This is the tool's **normal
interface**, which its own README requires for any valid claim — it is capability, not coaching:
- A fenced block, one line per verb, **absolute path repeated on every line**, `impact` included:
  `<path>/eg-q.run search <words>` / `def <Symbol>` / `callers <Symbol>` / `impact <Symbol>` / `grep <regex>`.
- Restore the WHEN sentence to **both** eg configs (it exists already in `PREFETCH_BLOCK`,
  `run_3arm.sh:694`): *"The tool is live: query it again whenever you need something the result below
  does not already answer."*
- **Fairness line, applied per-line:** anything meaningless without the tool (verb syntax, "query it
  again", `impact` for sites sharing a defect) → eg only. Anything a no-tool arm could also act on
  (read-size limits, verify-once, "don't write a throwaway harness") → **both arms or neither**.
  Assert per cell: `count(frugality lines, eg) == count(baseline)`.

### Stage 2 — stop poisoning the payload's credibility
Suppress from the **injected** payload (keep on disk for forensics): `VERIFY: none validated in this
environment` (27/33 prompts), `Completeness: degraded`/`failed to parse`, `LOW CONFIDENCE`, and above
all `SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED … Search will not run again` — a refusal notice currently shipped inside
`<graph_search_result>`. Cheapest place: the `_pp`/`_strip_*` filter chain in `tools/eg-q` (~line 162)
plus the `pf_minimal`/`PREFETCH_BLOCK` assembly in `run_3arm.sh`.

### Stage 3 — suppress a rank-1 that resolves to a test file
`gohugoio__hugo-12204`'s rank 1 was `tpl/tplimpl/render_hook_integration_test.go` — a file the prompt
forbids editing. The eg agent followed it and spent **74 turns vs the baseline's 49 (+25)**. Demote
test-file hits out of rank 1 when a non-test candidate exists. Reuse the existing test-path detection
behind `EG_DROP_TESTS`/`_egsearch.py` rather than writing new matching.

### Stage 4 — expose `verify`, the one phase where eg is measurably worse
POST-last-edit is eg 9.51 vs baseline 8.95 = **+0.56 ops, 20.7% of the session**, and
`entire graph verify` (commit `db24f74`: delta-not-state, verdict-not-evidence, 9 runner parsers) was
built for exactly this — but `tools/eg-q` does not expose it as a verb (only internal `_strip_verify`).
Add `verify` to the shim's verb list and to the fenced block.

### Stage 5 — the fresh language-balanced 30
Build from `tasks/multilingual_300.json` (300 rows, `language` populated on all) plus the 6 Python
instances. Target ≈6 Python / 3 Java / 3 Rust / 3 Go / 3 Ruby / 3 PHP / 3 C / 2 TS / 2 JS / 2 C++.
Keep the 12 instances that already have 4-cell coverage where the strata allow, so historical data
stays partially reusable. Build graphs for the 3 Python instances lacking them
(`tools/batch_graphs_rep30.sh` pattern, now fixed for both task-file shapes) and **reject any graph
that builds DEGRADED** — 41 of 112 currently ship degraded silently.

### Stage 6 — $0 offline pre-flight (hard gate before any paid session)
1. Regenerate every prompt for all 30 instances, both arms. Assert: fenced block present with all six
   verbs and absolute path on each; zero occurrences of the four trust-poisoning strings; rank 1 is
   not a test file on any instance; scaffold + batch line present in both arms; frugality-line count
   equal across arms.
2. Replay recorded queries against the pinned binary; assert gold-file rank does not regress.
3. **Pin the binary out of the session scratchpad.** `EG`/`EGI` currently point at
   `/private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/eg-94009ef` — a reproducibility landmine. Copy to a stable
   path and record its sha256 in the cell metadata (`entire graph version` reports `dev`).
4. Verify `eg-q.run` runs from the prompt's absolute path with no `cd`, for all six verbs.
**Kill criterion:** any assertion fails → fix before spending.

## Verification and gates

Per-lever, numeric, checked **before** the aggregate is read:
- **Legibility (Stage 1):** graph queries/session **≥3.0** (from 0.042). Falsified below 1.0 — if the
  agent still won't call a fenced, fully-pathed command, discoverability was not the binding cause.
- **Locate conversion (Stages 1–3):** first-stage locate ops/session **≤8.0** (from 14.3) and
  repo-wide-before-first-edit **≤3.0** (eg is 3.0 in FULLPF vs baseline 6.2 — must not regress).
- **Trust (Stage 2):** payload-file re-reads in first 8 turns **≤40%** of sessions (from 88%).
- **Post-edit (Stage 4):** POST-last-edit ops **≤8.95** (baseline parity; from 9.51).
- **Aggregate:** paired geomean over replicate-averaged instances, bootstrap CI. Goal **≥25% saving**
  with the CI's unfavourable bound still a saving.
