input.content:
# Four-arm benchmark runbook — fresh machine to a result

Everything needed to reproduce a 300-instance, four-arm token measurement from a bare checkout, and
the guardrails that stop it producing a confident wrong number. Default scale is **300 × 4 arms**;
§7 scales down to 100 or 30.

Web version: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/22f8e56b-0d25-4136-a086-dc2073fa287a

---

## §0 · What is being measured

Four arms solve the same SWE-bench Multilingual instances with the same agent and the same prompt
scaffold. The only difference is what code-context tooling each is handed.

| arm | what it gets | role |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline` | nothing — shell, read, edit | the control; every ratio is against this |
| `eg` | entire-graph | tool under test |
| `cmm` | codebase-memory-mcp | comparator |
| `graphify` | graphify index | comparator |

Output is **tokens and cost per instance, paired against the control**. Resolve grading is a
separate optional stage (§9) and is *not* installed by default — every number is token-only until
you install it, and must be labelled so in the same sentence.

---

## §1 · Prerequisites

```
claude   >= 2.1.221   # record the version — it shifts results ~5 points between minor releases
gh                    # authenticated: gh auth status
go       >= 1.22      # CGO required (tree-sitter)
python3  >= 3.11
git, docker, uv
```

Hardware actually used: 48 GB RAM, ~8 concurrent sessions comfortably (≈1–2 GB resident each, plus
whatever the repo's own build wants — a JDK or cargo build is the real consumer).

**Reclaim disk first.** A previous run filled the volume mid-batch and killed dockerd, losing a
whole cell. Budget in §7. Keep the suite off volatile paths like `/private/tmp`, which gets reaped.

---

## §2 · Bootstrap

```bash
git clone https://github.com/entirehq/graphmark.git
cd graphmark/agentic-swebench
uv venv .venv --python 3.11
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python datasets tiktoken tabulate
```

Build the tool binary and **pin it by hash**:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph.git
cd entire-graph && go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph
cp entire-graph ../graphmark/agentic-swebench/bin/entire-graph-<sha>
shasum -a 256 ../graphmark/agentic-swebench/bin/entire-graph-<sha>
```

`entire graph version` reports `dev`, so **the sha256 is the only real pin**. Record it in the run
manifest. A binary swapped without a recorded hash once caused a −7.9 point regression to be
attributed to a config.

Build the graphs:

```bash
tools/batch_graphs_rep30.sh        # or batch_graphs_rep100.sh / batch_graphs.sh for 300
tools/build_graphify_graph.sh      # graphify arm only
```

~5 s and ~7 MB per repo for entire-graph. **Check graphify's output** — it fails to build on ~9 of
30 instances (`nodes=0`), and a tool-build failure must remove the instance from **all four arms
symmetrically**, never just from the arm that failed, or the arm whose tool is worst has its own
worst instances deleted.

---

## §3 · Configure

Copy `tools/run_minpf.sh` as your cell launcher. These settings are not defaults — each is the
result of a measurement, and several are load-bearing for fairness.

| setting | why |
|---|---|
| `PUBLISHED_EXACT=1` | Anthropic's published SWE-bench prompt, byte-identical across arms |
| `O35_VERIFY_ONLY=1` | **measured.** Inject the one-line locator, *not* the full payload — see §3.1 |
| `EG_VERIFY_MODE=off` | **measured.** A real runner command costs +4.6 turns; no command saves 4.7 |
| `O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1` | **fairness.** Strips the binary's own generic methodology, keeps its derived command |
| `EG_LITERALS/SIBLINGS/CALLEES/ANCHOR=0` | **must stay 0.** Their helper scripts do not exist; setting them to 1 emits an empty payload with no error |
| `O35_QUERY_V2=0`, `O35_QUERY_V3=0` | V3 leaked the gold path out of GitHub permalinks, tool-arm only |
| `GQ_SEARCH_CAP=0` | a frugality clamp on tool arms while the control greps uncapped |
| `CC_MODEL`, `CC_MAX_TURNS=120` | assert the resolved model per session from `modelUsage`; mixed-model pairs are silent poison |
| `CC_EFFORT` | optional (`low…max`). Session-level, applies to both arms, cannot create an asymmetry |

### §3.1 · The payload is charged rent on every turn

**This is the single most expensive thing to get wrong.** An injected payload is re-read on every
turn, whether or not the agent still needs it. Measured, n=4, monotone:

| instance | payload delta | cache_read/turn | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| carbon | +5.2 KB | 51.6K vs 50.0K (+3%) | **saving 1.8%** — smallest payload, only winner |
| caddy | +14.9 KB | 49.4K vs 42.4K (+17%) | costing 0.1% |
| lucene | +11.2 KB | 42.0K vs 31.0K (+36%) | costing 78.9% |
| ruff | +7.1 KB | 45.9K vs 31.7K (+45%) | costing 43.8% |

The ruff pair is the clean proof: **identical turn count (48 vs 48), 44% more tokens.** Not more
work — the same work, re-reading a bigger prompt. A 15 KB payload across 45 turns is ~170K tokens of
rent, and it buys nothing after turn 1 because the agent has already read it.

**Inject the answer (one locator line, ~200 bytes), not the evidence for it.**

### §3.2 · Native MCP tools — no payload at all

The strictly better shape, if it holds: expose the graph as native MCP tools so nothing is injected
and the result is paid only from the turn it is fetched.

```bash
export EG_MCP=1        # five tools: code_search, find_definition, find_callers, impact, verify_command
```

This had **never been exercised**, for two independent reasons, both now fixed:

1. `mcp.json` pointed at `tools/eg_mcp.py`; the file is **`tools/eg_mcp_server.py`**. The server
   never started, silently.
2. **`--safe-mode` silently strips every configured MCP server** — no error, no stderr, no
   transcript trace. The harness passed `--mcp-config` and then `--safe-mode`, which deleted it.

Verified 2026-08-05: with `--safe-mode` the model reports *"no MCP servers are connected"*; without
it, five `mcp__entiregraph__*` tools appear. `run_3arm.sh` now drops `--safe-mode` when `EG_MCP=1`,
**from every arm**, so the arms stay symmetric — the baseline simply has no server configured.

Why it should beat an injected payload: zero prompt rent, and the graph competes in the *tool list*
rather than losing to grep's prior *inside* the Bash tool.

---

## §4 · Preflight — free, and every item has caught a real bug

```
1  disk headroom >= §7 budget            df -g $HOME
2  binary present, hash recorded
3  graphs built; graphify failures listed and symmetrically excluded
4  ANTI_HARNESS == '' in tools/_pf_verify.py
5  smoke ONE instance end to end (~$1), then READ THE SHIPPED PROMPT:
     prefetch.payload            > 0 bytes   (unless EG_MCP=1)
     grep -c '^VERIFY:'          -> expected for your config
     grep -c 'alternative test harness' -> 0
     grep -c 'FAIL_TO_PASS'      -> 0
     diff eg/prompt.txt baseline/prompt.txt   -> account for EVERY line
6  if EG_MCP=1: confirm the tools actually exist —
     claude -p "List tools starting with mcp__" --mcp-config <f> --strict-mcp-config \
       --dangerously-skip-permissions --max-turns 3 < /dev/null
```

**Verify fairness in the prompt that SHIPPED, never in the config that was supposed to produce it.**
Found the hard way: the harness clamp was set to `''` and verified — and the binary's own native copy
sailed straight through into ~30/30 prompts against 0/30 control.

---

## §5 · Run

```bash
for arm in baseline eg cmm graphify; do
  for sh in 0 1 2 3; do
    nohup env ARM=$arm TAG=RUN300 SHARD=$sh NSHARD=4 \
      TASKS_FILE=$PWD/tasks/multilingual_300.json \
      bash tools/run_minpf.sh > results/RUN300.$arm.s$sh.log 2>&1 &
  done
done

nohup bash tools/loadlog.sh results/RUN300.loadlog.tsv >/dev/null 2>&1 &   # prove symmetry
```

The **same shard count must be used for every arm** so load pressure stays balanced. Instances are
idempotent — a driver skips any instance with a non-empty `cc_out.json` — so workers can be added,
killed and restarted freely; `REVERSE=1` walks the same arm from the far end.

While running:

```
per-arm completion                    N/300
dead sessions per arm                 0-byte cc_out with no .running marker
results/<TAG>.empty_payload           MUST stay empty
loadlog: eg_running == base_running   at every sample
```

The strong form of the symmetry check: both arms on the **same instance within seconds of each
other**. Under that pattern load pressure cannot favour either.

---

## §6 · Chaining cells

Never run two cells concurrently — load pressure is a documented sign-flipping confound, and two
cells sharing a machine contaminate each other. Use `tools/chain3.sh` as the pattern:

```bash
wait_for(){ while :; do d=$(ps -A -o pid=,command= | awk -v p="$1" '$2=="bash" && $0~p' | wc -l); [ "$d" -eq 0 ] && break; sleep 60; done; }
launch(){ ... }
wait_for run_minpf; launch run_mcpcell.sh MCPCELL
```

Never append to a script while bash is executing it — bash reads by byte offset and will execute
garbage. Copy to a new path and run that.

Comparing models needs the **same machine state**, not the same wall clock. Chain them too.

---

## §7 · Scale, cost and time

Derived from measured Opus sessions (~$2.75 mean, ~2.4 M tokens) at 8 workers ≈ 0.6 completed
sessions/minute.

| set | instances | sessions (4 arms) | cost, Opus | wall @8w | @16w | disk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `multilingual_300.json` *(default)* | 300 | 1,200 | ~$3,300 | ~33 h | ~17 h | ~250 GB |
| `rep100_tasks.json` | 100 | 400 | ~$1,100 | ~11 h | ~6 h | ~85 GB |
| `rep30_tasks.json` | 30 | 120 | ~$330 | ~3.5 h | ~2 h | ~25 GB |
| rep30, 2 arms only | 30 | 60 | ~$165 | ~1.7 h | ~1 h | ~13 GB |

Change scale by pointing `TASKS_FILE` at a different set — nothing else changes. Add replicates by
re-running with a new `TAG`; a repeated `TAG` resumes rather than redoes.

### What n buys you

```
1 + 1 replicate   ±14.1%      3 + 3 trimmed   ±6.4%      floor at n=30   ±3.4%
TO CLAIM >=25%    YOU MUST MEASURE ~31.4%
```

**30 instances cannot resolve a config difference under ~30 points.** Measured directly: two cells
with byte-identical prompts, binary, flags, CLI version and zero attrition read **15.2%** and
**3.6%**. If your effect is smaller, go to 100 or add replicates — do not read a single 30.

---

## §8 · Score

```bash
python3 tools/score_cell.py RUN300
```

The gate, applied identically to every arm:

```
count a session IFF  subtype == "success"  AND  patch.diff non-empty
drop pairs SYMMETRICALLY — if any arm fails an instance, it leaves ALL arms
```

Omitting the subtype check once inflated a 13.3% result to "22.0%", and let a session that finished
cleanly and wrote **no patch at all** report as "saving 52.2%". A session that does no work always
looks cheap.

Report paired geomean with a bootstrap CI **and** total (Σ/Σ) — never one instead of the other —
then the split by token class. cache_read, cache_creation and output move independently, and
**which one moved is the finding**.

Integrity sweep before quoting anything:

- ENOSPC **from transcripts, not `*.log`** — one cell showed 1 hit in logs against 10 in transcripts
- censoring (`error_max_turns`) symmetric between arms
- arm time-window overlap ≥ 70%
- corrupt/empty `cc_out.json`; per-instance prompt diff; foreign-cache markers

---

## §9 · Resolve grading (optional, not installed)

```bash
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python swebench
tools/assemble_preds.py && tools/run_eval_model.sh    # Docker only, $0 API
```

Power is ±12.5 pp at n=30×3, so pre-register a non-inferiority margin and state that anything
smaller is undetectable at that size. Until this is installed, write **"token-only"** in the same
sentence as every number.

---

## §10 · Guardrails

### Cost model

| model | cache_read | cache_create | output | cost share cr/cc/out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 | 1.00 | 20.31 | 49.63 | 22 / 39 / 39 |
| Opus 5 | 0.50 | 10.19 | 24.73 | 26 / 38 / 36 |
| Sonnet | 0.29 | 6.33 | 14.78 | 41 / 31 / 28 |
| Haiku | 0.10 | 2.09 | 4.96 | 46 / 28 / 25 |

$/Mtok. **"95% of tokens are cache_read" is a token count, not a cost share** — output is priced
20–50× higher and is a quarter to two-fifths of the bill. A tool that cuts reading and raises
writing loses money.

### Traps that produce a clean-looking wrong number

- **Helpers referenced but absent, failing OPEN.** Five so far: `_eglit.py`, `_egsiblings.py`,
  `_egcallees.py`, `_eganchor.py`, and `eg_mcp.py` (really `eg_mcp_server.py`). Each fails silently
  and degrades the tool arm to a control — sometimes with a *smaller* prompt than its comparison
  group. **Assert the artifact, not the flag.**
- **`--safe-mode` strips MCP** with no error, no stderr, no transcript trace.
- **Tree-keyed index cache.** A/B two binaries without a separate `--cache-dir` each and the second
  silently returns the first's results.
- **Transcript parsing.** One API response spans several JSONL lines sharing a `message.id`; UNION
  the content blocks. Keeping "the longest" drops `tool_use`. Opus thinking blocks are encrypted —
  1094/1094 empty — so never analyse thinking text.
- **Environment, not patch.** A derived command that fails because the checkout was never
  provisioned sends the agent to repair the environment — 15 turns hand-assembling a classpath.
- **One-armed environment destruction.** The `O35_VERIFY_VALIDATE` block sits inside
  `if [ "$arm" = eg ]`, so its `git clean -fd` wipes provisioning for the tool arm only.
  Baseline-favouring. Default off; check before enabling.
- **Shell.** `pgrep -fc` is invalid on macOS (exits 2, prints nothing, so `|| echo 0` calls a healthy
  run dead). An unmatched glob aborts the whole command line in zsh, so cleanup silently never runs.
  The Go module cache is read-only — `chmod -R u+rwX` first.

### Do not re-propose

| lever | why it is dead |
|---|---|
| payload-quality metrics | **ten** have failed as causal token levers. Treat as law |
| per-loser repair | neutralising *every* losing instance is worth **+0.35 pt**; 93% flip sign between cells |
| LOCATE-reduction elasticity | corr(ΔLOCATE, Δtokens) = **+0.188** |
| confidence tier on score margin | **AUC 0.503**; the margin is *higher* when rank-1 is wrong |
| query prefetch from issue text | 8 losses, 0 wins against the agent's own query |
| oracle config selection | min-of-k is invariant to label shuffling; equals the null exactly |
| raising the turn cap | both arms grow proportionally |

### Standing results

- **Grep elimination is the strongest predictor.** corr(search ratio, log token ratio) ≈ **+0.575**
  [+0.476, +0.672], n=113, while corr(*baseline* greps, outcome) ≈ 0 — so it is not difficulty
  leaking through. Fit: `log(tokratio) = −0.635 + 0.475 × search_ratio`.
- **The injected payload is not used as a tool.** 97.6% of tool-arm sessions never query the graph
  once. Whatever effect exists comes from the block appended to the prompt — which is why §3.1 and
  §3.2 matter more than payload content.
- **A "validated" test command is unreachable by construction.** The gold test ships in `test_patch`,
  never applied to the pristine tree, so nothing derived from the repo's own build files can fail
  pre-fix. Every firing instance fires on unrelated pre-existing breakage — firing rate measures how
  broken a repo's suite already is, not command quality. Record-a-baseline-then-compare
  (`entire graph verify`) is the only primitive that works on a green repo.

---

## Discipline

Keep an audit ledger tagging every claim solid / moderate / retracted, with its basis. When a result
contradicts an earlier one, find the mechanism before believing either. Correct notes in place when
falsified. Do not stop at a negative finding — but going deeper is not a licence to loosen the
standard of evidence. Report the interval, publish the retractions, and say plainly when a target was
not reached.

**The prediction held, and overshot it.** Same instance, before and after the payload fix:

```
ruff-15626       payload      turns      tokens     cr/turn      outcome
FULL payload     +7,130 B     48 vs 48   2.32M      +45%         costing 43.8%
ONE-LINE         +  615 B     48 vs 49   1.52M      -16%          saving 18.3%
```

**A 62-point swing on the same instance, with the turn count essentially unchanged (48 vs 48, then 48 vs 49).** The only thing that changed is how many bytes get re-read every turn. I predicted "roughly break-even"; it came in at saving 18.3%, and `cr/turn` went from a 45% *penalty* to a 16% *advantage*.

That's a causal confirmation, not a correlation — same instance, same model, same binary, same turn budget, one variable.

**What this establishes:** the payload rent mechanism is real and it was the dominant cost term. The tool was being charged more for delivering evidence than it earned by delivering the answer.

**What it doesn't establish yet:** n=1 on the new cell. Per-instance noise here runs 33–45 points median, so a single instance cannot carry a claim — even a clean one. What makes this stronger than a normal n=1 is that it's a *paired before/after on the same instance* with matched turns, which removes instance difficulty entirely.

I'm not calling the goal met on one data point. But this is the first time in the session that the corrected config is on the right side of zero, and the mechanism behind it is understood rather than lucky.

# collect_patch.sh <worktree> <out_patch>
# Build the SWE-bench model_patch = the agent's SOURCE edits, INCLUDING newly-created source
# files, while excluding dependency lockfiles, vendored/build artifacts, and the agent's own
# reproduction/test scripts.
#
# Why untracked files matter (the bug this fixes): plain `git diff` shows only tracked
# modifications, so a fix that ADDS a new source file (a new module/class/helper) was silently
# dropped from the prediction — symmetrically capping resolved% for both arms. We `git add -N`
# (intent-to-add) the untracked SOURCE files so they show up in the diff as new files.
#
# Why the exclusions (the pollution bug this must NOT re-introduce): a prior `git add -A` swept
# in package-lock.json and agent repro scripts, breaking `git apply` in the official eval and
# making the arm-to-arm comparison unfair. So we filter untracked paths to real source only:
# no lockfiles, no vendor/node_modules, no build/dist/target, no *.log/patch files, and no
# test/reproduction files (SWE-bench's own instructions forbid submitting those).
set -uo pipefail
wt="${1:?worktree}"; out="${2:?out patch path}"

git -C "$wt" ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
| while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
    case "$f" in
      node_modules/*|*/node_modules/*|vendor/*|*/vendor/*)                   continue ;;
      # Provisioned dependency trees. `--exclude-standard` only skips them when the project's OWN
      # .gitignore happens to list them, and plenty do not (scikit-learn's has no `.venv` entry),
      # so without this a provisioned virtualenv's entire site-packages is `git add -N`'d into
      # model_patch. Must stay in sync with PROVISIONED_DIRS in tools/_pf_verify.py, which is what
      # keeps these trees alive past the VERIFY step. Applies to BOTH arms identically.
      .venv/*|*/.venv/*|venv/*|*/venv/*|.bundle/*|*/.bundle/*)                continue ;;
      .tox/*|*/.tox/*|.gradle/*|*/.gradle/*|.m2/*|*/.m2/*)                    continue ;;
      build/*|*/build/*|dist/*|*/dist/*|target/*|*/target/*)                 continue ;;
      *package-lock.json|*yarn.lock|*pnpm-lock.yaml|*composer.lock|*Cargo.lock|*go.sum|*.snap) continue ;;
      *.log|patch.txt|patch.diff)                                            continue ;;
      test_*|*/test_*|*_test.*|*Test.*|*.test.*|*_spec.*|*.spec.*)           continue ;;
      tests/*|*/tests/*|test/*|*/test/*|spec/*|*/spec/*|__tests__/*|*/__tests__/*) continue ;;

      reproduce*|*/reproduce*|repro_*|*/repro_*|repro.*|*/repro.*)           continue ;;

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Does the harness's own query hurt retrieval? ($0, deterministic, n=30)

WHY NOW. With the payload cut to a ONE-LINE locator, retrieval accuracy IS the product: the
agent is handed an answer with no supporting evidence, so a wrong rank-1 is a wrong answer.
Base rank-1 gold is 13/30 (43%) -- meaning 57% of sessions are told the wrong place.

The harness ships the WHOLE problem statement as the query, including markdown headers, version
strings, and base64 reproduction URLs:

  "use v-for rendering a shallowReactive array ... ### Vue version 3.5.3 ### Link to minimal
   reproduction https://play.vuejs.org/#eNp9UsFOAjEQ/REDACTED..."

The adversarial reviewer independently found that a 10-word first-sentence query ranks caddy's
gold #1 on the UNMODIFIED binary, where the harness query buries it outside the top 10.

This measures every variant against gold on all 30, one binary, separate --cache-dir per variant.
Gold is read ONLY to score, never to build a query.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import collections

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
EG = os.environ.get("ENTIRE_GRAPH", f"{SUITE}/bin/entire-graph-94009ef-ts")
WTROOT = "/tmp/recall_wt"


def gold_files(t):
    return set(re.findall(r"\+\+\+ b/(\S+)", t.get("patch", "") or ""))


def clean(s):
    s = re.sub(r"https?://\S+", " ", s or "")          # reproduction URLs / permalinks
    s = re.sub(r"```.*?```", " ", s, flags=re.S)        # fenced blocks
    s = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", " ", s)                      # inline code (often contains the path)
    s = re.sub(r"^\s*#+\s*.*$", " ", s, flags=re.M)     # markdown headers (### Vue version 3.5.3)
    s = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", s)                      # html
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


def variants(t):
    ps = (t.get("problem_statement") or "").strip()
    c = clean(ps)
    sents = [x for x in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", c) if x.strip()]
    words = c.split()
    lines = [l for l in ps.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    return {
        "harness_full": re.sub(r"\s+", " ", ps)[:1200],   # what ships today
        "cleaned_all": c[:1200],
        "first_sent": (sents[0] if sents else c)[:300],
        "first10w": " ".join(words[:10]),
        "title_raw": re.sub(r"\s+", " ", lines[0])[:200] if lines else c[:200],
    }


def search(wt, iid, q, tag, topk=10):
    cmd = [EG, "search", "--query", q, "--repo", wt, "--format", "json",
           "--top-k", str(topk), "--profile", "full",
           "--cache-dir", f"{SUITE}/.eg_cache/{iid}"]
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
        d = json.loads(r.stdout or "{}")
    except Exception:
        return []
    return [h.get("file_path") for h in (d.get("results") or [])]


def main():
    os.chdir(SUITE)
    tasks = json.load(open("tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]
    if not os.access(EG, os.X_OK):
        sys.exit(f"not executable: {EG}")
    names = list(variants(tasks[0]).keys())
    agg = {n: collections.Counter() for n in names}
    rows = []
    print(f"{'instance':30s} " + " ".join(f"{n:>13s}" for n in names))
    for t in tasks:
        iid = t["instance_id"]
        wt = f"{WTROOT}/{iid}"
        if not os.path.isdir(wt):
            continue
        gold = gold_files(t)
        if not gold:
            continue
        vs = variants(t)
        cells = []
        for n in names:
            files = search(wt, iid, vs[n], n)
            rank = next((k for k, f in enumerate(files, 1) if f in gold), None)
            agg[n]["n"] += 1
            if rank == 1:
                agg[n]["r1"] += 1
            if rank and rank <= 5:
                agg[n]["r5"] += 1
            if rank:
                agg[n]["r10"] += 1
            cells.append(f"{(str(rank) if rank else '-'):>13s}")
        rows.append(iid)
        print(f"  {iid:28s} " + " ".join(cells), flush=True)

    print(f"\n{'variant':16s} {'n':>4s} {'gold@1':>9s} {'gold@5':>9s} {'gold@10':>9s}")
    for n in names:
        a = agg[n]
        if not a["n"]:
            continue
        print(f"  {n:14s} {a['n']:4d} {a['r1']:4d} {a['r1']/a['n']*100:5.0f}% "
              f"{a['r5']:4d} {a['r5']/a['n']*100:4.0f}% {a['r10']:4d} {a['r10']/a['n']*100:4.0f}%")
    base = agg["harness_full"]
    print(f"\n  harness_full is what ships today: gold@1 = {base['r1']}/{base['n']}")
    best = max((n for n in names), key=lambda n: agg[n]["r1"])
    if best != "harness_full":
        d = agg[best]["r1"] - base["r1"]
        print(f"  BEST variant: {best}  gold@1 {agg[best]['r1']}/{agg[best]['n']}  (+{d} instances)")
    else:
        print("  the harness query is already the best variant -- no free win here")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

**TS-binary hypothesis: refuted** — but it surfaced something more important.

```

docusaurus              2               3          TS marginally worse
preact               None            None          SAME  <- gold NOT FOUND by either

The TypeScript fix isn't causing the losses. **On preact and vuejs the gold file isn't in the top 10 at all — for either binary.** So the agent is handed a *wrong location, stated as fact, with no supporting evidence to judge it by*. Both cost ~58%.

That's the real mechanism, and it's the flip side of the fix that worked:

> **A one-line locator is high-variance. When rank-1 is right it's a big win (+59%, +39%, +36%). When it's wrong it actively misleads (−58%, −58%, −38%).** With the full payload the agent could see the evidence was irrelevant and discount it; with one line there's nothing to discount.

And rank-1 is right only **30%** of the time (9/30 shipping today, 11/30 with the best query). So the config I built is winning a third of the time and misleading the rest.

The obvious repair is in the numbers I already have: **gold@1 = 37%, but gold@5 = 70%.** Injecting the top-5 locator lines is ~600 bytes — still 25× smaller than the payload that caused the rent problem — and roughly doubles the chance the right answer is present, while presenting a *ranked shortlist* rather than asserting one wrong fact.

That said, **MCPCELL still dominates as the next cell**, because it fixes both failure modes at once: zero rent, *and* the agent issues its own query rather than being handed someone else's wrong guess.

**Found the loser mechanism, and it's the opposite of what the tool is supposed to do:**

```
preact       eg searches 20  vs baseline 10   (2.0x)   reads 9 vs 6
docusaurus   eg searches 22  vs baseline 11   (2.0x)   reads 16 vs 8  (2.0x)
```

**On the losing instances the tool arm greps twice as much as the arm with no tool.** The entire premise is grep elimination, and a wrong pointer *doubles* it.

The causal chain, now measured end to end:

1. The prompt asserts a location as fact.
2. It's wrong (63% of the time — gold@1 is 37%).
3. The agent goes there, explores the wrong area, discovers the miss.
4. It then has to locate from scratch — **but has already burned a full exploration cycle** and is anchored on the wrong subsystem.

So a wrong locator isn't neutral, it's **negative**: it buys an extra wasted exploration pass. That reconciles everything — winners have `search_ratio < 1`, losers ~2.0, and the campaign-long finding `corr(search_ratio, log tokens) = +0.575` is the same fact seen from a distance.

**This sharpens the config question. The harm is anchoring on a wrong location**, so the fix is to stop asserting one:

| option | how it defuses anchoring | status |
|---|---|---|
| **MCPCELL** | nothing injected — the agent forms its own query and is never anchored | queued next, strongest test |
| **TOP5** | shortlist of 5, gold present 70% — dilutes the anchor rather than removing it | queued after; premise now better supported than the n=4 gate suggested |

| FABLE30 / OPUSMAX | same config, other models | replication |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-language and per-repo breakdown for one or more cells.

Usage: tools/breakdown.py TAG [TAG2 ...] [--md out.md]

Same strict gate as score_cell.py: both arms subtype==success AND non-empty patch.diff,
dropped symmetrically. Reports geomean AND total per stratum, because they answer different
questions -- geomean weights every instance equally, total weights the expensive ones.

CAUTION built in: strata on a 30-instance set are tiny (Java 4, Rust 4, Go 4, Ruby 4, PHP 3,
C 3, TS 2, JS 2, C++ 1). This benchmark's own rule forbids reading sub-groups of 3-7, so every
stratum prints its n and anything under 8 is flagged NOISE. The table is for spotting a
direction worth testing, never for a claim.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import math
import random
import statistics
import collections

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
CLASSES = ("input_tokens", "output_tokens",
           "cache_read_input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens")


def sess(tag, arm, iid):
    d = f"{SUITE}/results/{tag}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}"
    cc, pd = f"{d}/cc_out.json", f"{d}/patch.diff"
    if not (os.path.isfile(cc) and os.path.getsize(cc) > 0):
        return None
    try:
        j = json.load(open(cc))
    except Exception:
        return None
    if j.get("subtype") != "success":
        return None
    if not (os.path.isfile(pd) and os.path.getsize(pd) > 0):
        return None
    u = j.get("usage") or {}
    return dict(tok=sum(u.get(c, 0) for c in CLASSES),
                turns=j.get("num_turns") or 1,
                usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0,
                out=u.get("output_tokens", 0),
                cr=u.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0))


def boot(rs, n=20000, seed=12345):
    if len(rs) < 3:
        return (float("nan"), float("nan"))
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    gs = [math.exp(sum(math.log(rnd.choice(rs)) for _ in rs) / len(rs)) for _ in range(n)]
    gs.sort()
    return (1 - gs[int(.975 * n)], 1 - gs[int(.025 * n)])


def collect(tag, meta):
    root = f"{SUITE}/results/{tag}_r1_eg/eg"
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        return []
    ids = sorted(set(os.listdir(root)) |
                 set(os.listdir(f"{SUITE}/results/{tag}_r1_baseline/baseline")
                     if os.path.isdir(f"{SUITE}/results/{tag}_r1_baseline/baseline") else []))
    rows = []
    for i in ids:
        e, b = sess(tag, "eg", i), sess(tag, "baseline", i)
        if not (e and b):
            continue
        m = meta.get(i, {})
        rows.append(dict(iid=i, lang=m.get("language") or "?",
                         repo=(m.get("repo") or i.rsplit("-", 1)[0]),
                         ratio=e["tok"] / b["tok"], eg=e, base=b))
    return rows


def stratum(rows):
    rs = [r["ratio"] for r in rows]
    g = math.exp(statistics.mean(math.log(x) for x in rs))
    se = sum(r["eg"]["tok"] for r in rows)
    sb = sum(r["base"]["tok"] for r in rows)
    ue = sum(r["eg"]["usd"] for r in rows)
    ub = sum(r["base"]["usd"] for r in rows)
    return dict(n=len(rows), geo=1 - g, total=1 - se / sb, cost=1 - ue / ub,
                wins=sum(1 for x in rs if x < 1),
                egt=statistics.mean(r["eg"]["turns"] for r in rows),
                bat=statistics.mean(r["base"]["turns"] for r in rows))


def emit(tag, rows, out):
    if not rows:
        out.append(f"\n### {tag} — no gated pairs\n")
        return
    a = stratum(rows)
    lo, hi = boot([r["ratio"] for r in rows])
    out.append(f"\n## {tag}\n")
    out.append(f"**n = {a['n']}** gated pairs · geomean saving **{a['geo']*100:.1f}%** "
               f"(95% CI [{lo*100:+.1f}, {hi*100:+.1f}]) · total **{a['total']*100:.1f}%** · "
               f"cost **{a['cost']*100:.1f}%** · winners {a['wins']}/{a['n']} · "
               f"turns {a['egt']:.1f} vs {a['bat']:.1f}\n")

    out.append("\n### By language\n")
    out.append("| language | n | geomean | total | winners | note |")
    out.append("|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|")
    by = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for r in rows:
        by[r["lang"]].append(r)
    for k in sorted(by, key=lambda k: -len(by[k])):
        s = stratum(by[k])
        note = "" if s["n"] >= 8 else "**NOISE — n<8, do not read**"
        out.append(f"| {k} | {s['n']} | {s['geo']*100:+.1f}% | {s['total']*100:+.1f}% | "
                   f"{s['wins']}/{s['n']} | {note} |")

    out.append("\n### By repo (per instance)\n")
    out.append("| repo / instance | lang | saving | eg turns | base turns | eg Mtok | base Mtok |")
    out.append("|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|")
    for r in sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["ratio"]):
        out.append(f"| {r['iid']} | {r['lang']} | {(1-r['ratio'])*100:+.1f}% | "
                   f"{r['eg']['turns']} | {r['base']['turns']} | "
                   f"{r['eg']['tok']/1e6:.2f} | {r['base']['tok']/1e6:.2f} |")


def main():
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
    md = None
    if "--md" in sys.argv:
        md = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--md") + 1]
    meta = {t["instance_id"]: t for t in
            json.load(open(f"{SUITE}/tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]}
    out = ["# Cell breakdown — language and repo",
           "",
           "Strict gate: both arms `subtype==success` AND non-empty `patch.diff`, dropped "
           "symmetrically. Geomean weights every instance equally; total weights the expensive "
           "ones. **Strata under n=8 are noise on this benchmark and are marked as such.**"]
    for tag in (args or ["MINPF"]):
        emit(tag, collect(tag, meta), out)
    text = "\n".join(out)
    print(text)
    if md:
        open(md, "w").write(text + "\n")
        print(f"\n[written to {md}]", file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
Agent is digging into the MCP transcripts — specifically *why* 12 of 21 instances never call the tool, and what the ceiling would be if they did.

**My best judgement right now, stated before that agent reports so it's not retrofitted:**

**MINPF is the config to ship.** n=30, geomean +17.1%, total +21.8%, and the leave-one-out proves it isn't resting on any single instance (max swing ±2.9 pts). That's the most solid number this campaign has produced.

**MCPCELL is not yet a real measurement.** At n=7 with individual instances worth ±20 points, it's below the noise floor by a wide margin. It is *not* evidence against MCP — it's an absence of evidence either way.

**The thread worth pulling** is that MCP's failure mode is adoption, not capability: 0.52 calls/session means roughly half the sessions never touch a tool that's sitting right there in the tool list. If the agent used it 2–3 times per session, the theoretical case is strong — zero payload rent *and* no wrong-anchor, the two mechanisms I measured as the dominant costs. But "if the agent used it" has now failed twice: at 0.042 calls/session as a shell string, and at 0.52 as native tools. Exposure moved adoption 12× and still left most sessions not using it.

**What would change my mind:** if the agent's transcripts show it *notices* the tools and declines them for a fixable reason (bad first result, unclear naming, no prompt mention), that's addressable. If it simply never considers them, then the injected locator — despite anchoring on a wrong answer two-thirds of the time — remains the only mechanism that reliably gets the graph's output into the session, and MCP should be parked.

I'll let MCPCELL finish for the record, but I'd be surprised if it beats 21.8%.

**Neutralising JS/TS gets total to 24.57% — still just under 25%.** Making them merely *average* clears it at **26.34%**.

The four instances driving it:

```
preact       -58.5%   eg 3.09M vs base 1.95M
vuejs        -57.7%   eg 0.63M vs base 0.40M
docusaurus   -38.4%   eg 3.82M vs base 2.76M

So the honest read on your gate: **the entire 25% shortfall is the JS/TS stratum.** Strip it and the tool is already at 26.6% total / 22.8% geomean on the other 26 instances. Three repos are costing ~5 points of aggregate.

Two caveats I'd hold onto:

1. **Neutral alone isn't quite enough** — 24.57% misses by 0.4 points. The fix has to make JS/TS *slightly positive*, not just stop the bleeding.
2. **n=4 is a tiny stratum**, and immutable-js already wins at +13.4%. **Three distinct defects, and one is glaring:**

**preact** — the query is literally *"Add support for bigint."* Four words. Every top hit matched on **"add"**:

```
1. benches/scripts/analyze.js        addToGrouping
2. benches/src/keyed-children/...    add
3. benches/src/keyed-children/...    add
4. devtools/src/index.js             addHookName
6. demo/nested-suspense/...          AddNewComponent
7. demo/todo.js                      addTodo
```

**Every single one is from `benches/`, `devtools/` or `demo/` — non-source directories.** "bigint" matched nothing, so the ranker fell back on the most generic verb in the query and filled the entire top-10 with benchmark and demo code.

**docusaurus** — gold is at rank 3, outranked by `CodeBlock/index.ts` (a barrel re-export) and `theme-classic.d.ts` (a type declaration). Neither contains implementation.

**vuejs** — genuinely hard: the query says "shallowReactive", so the ranker returns `reactivity/` files. That's the *symptom* location; the fix is in `runtime-core/helpers/renderList.ts`.

Two of the three share a fixable cause: **non-source directories and declaration files are not demoted.** Implementing that:

Two results, and the second one requires me to correct myself.

**My non-shipped-code fix: safe but marginal.** docusaurus 3 → 2, nothing else moved, gold@1 and gold@5 unchanged at 10/30 and 19/30. **And the MCP finding overturns what I told you earlier. I was wrong.**

So the "12× adoption jump, 0.042 → 0.52 calls/session" I reported was **shell adoption via the old Round-8 prompt text, not MCP**. Three harness bugs made MCPCELL a shell-exposure cell: `EG_OPS_CLAMP` unset so the MCP prompt branch never fired; that branch names tools that don't exist (`graph_search` vs `code_search`); and the prompt promises a ranked payload while `EG_PREFETCH=0` means **0 payload files exist**.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PAIRED runner: for each instance, run BOTH arms back-to-back before moving on.
#
# WHY. Measured tonight: within a single cell, instances completing early score up to 33 points
# differently from those completing late (F4CLEAN: +20.7% vs -12.7%; MINPF: +11.0% vs +22.7%,
# opposite sign). The cause is that each arm runs as its own independent sweep, so a pair's eg and
# baseline halves can finish hours apart on a machine whose state is moving. The ratio then carries
# that drift.
#
# Running the two arms of ONE instance adjacently makes the pair time-matched: whatever the machine
# is doing, it is doing it to both arms at once, and the ratio cancels it. This is the same logic as
# the load-symmetry check, applied at pair granularity instead of cell granularity.
#
# TAG, SHARD/NSHARD, CONFIG (the launcher whose env to inherit) via env.
set -uo pipefail
SUITE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"; cd "$SUITE"
TAG="${TAG:-PAIRED}"
CONFIG="${CONFIG:-tools/run_minpf.sh}"
TASKS_FILE="${TASKS_FILE:-$SUITE/tasks/rep30_tasks.json}"
HARNESS="${HARNESS:-tools/run_3arm.sh}"

# inherit every export from the chosen config, but not its driver loop
eval "$(grep -E '^export ' "$CONFIG" | grep -vE 'RESULTS_TAG|TASKS_FILE')"
export TASKS_FILE

PYBIN="$SUITE/.venv/bin/python"; [ -x "$PYBIN" ] || PYBIN=python3
IIDS=()
while IFS= read -r l; do [ -n "$l" ] && IIDS+=("$l"); done < <("$PYBIN" -c "
import json
t=json.load(open('$TASKS_FILE'))
rows=t if isinstance(t,list) else t.get('instances',t.get('tasks',[]))
print('\n'.join(i['instance_id'] for i in rows))
")
if [ "${NSHARD:-1}" -gt 1 ]; then
  _sh=(); for ((i=${SHARD:-0}; i<${#IIDS[@]}; i+=${NSHARD})); do _sh+=("${IIDS[$i]}"); done; IIDS=("${_sh[@]}")
fi

echo "PAIRED: ${#IIDS[@]} instances, tag=$TAG, config=$CONFIG, harness=$HARNESS"
echo "  binary=$(basename "${ENTIRE_GRAPH:-?}")"
for iid in "${IIDS[@]}"; do
  _free=$(df -g "$HOME" | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
  [ "${_free:-0}" -lt 45 ] && { echo "HALT: ${_free}GiB free"; break; }
  ega="$SUITE/results/${TAG}_r1_eg/eg/$iid/cc_out.json"
  basea="$SUITE/results/${TAG}_r1_baseline/baseline/$iid/cc_out.json"
  [ -s "$ega" ] && [ -s "$basea" ] && { echo "[skip] $iid"; continue; }
  echo "[$iid] pair start $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  for arm in eg baseline; do
    RESULTS_TAG="${TAG}_r1_${arm}" bash "$SUITE/$HARNESS" "$arm" "$iid" \
      > "$SUITE/results/${TAG}_r1_${arm}.$iid.log" 2>&1
  done
  echo "[$iid] pair done  $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
done
echo "PAIRED DONE"
EOF

Two more results, both important:

- **corr(total call inflation, saving) = −0.813.** Tokens *are* calls. Nothing else matters at this level.
- **corr(payload distinct-file count, locate inflation) = −0.064** — shortlist breadth is not the cause, and *wider* payloads score better (5–6 files: +15.8%; 3–4 files: +2.2%). That kills the "narrow the shortlist to 3" fix, and is the 13th payload-quality metric to die.
- Post-edit inflation (−0.529) predicts outcome **more strongly** than pre-edit (−0.331).

Total call Δ orders the languages almost perfectly: Go −12.9→+29.6%, Ruby −4.9→+26.9%, PHP −5.2→+25.8%, Java −2.7→+16.2%, Rust −1.3→+11.5%, JS −3.3→+8.5%, TS +3.3→−7.4%, C +4.2→−16.3%. Slope ≈ **2.7pt per call removed**. Getting 19.6%→25% needs **~2 fewer calls per session**.

One clue stands out: TS is the only language where the agent actually invokes the graph (1.25 calls/session; JS 0.25; everything else **0.00**) — and TS is the worst locate inflater.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""F30: inject the rank-1 BODY, widening to rank-3 when the top hits are near-tied.

MINPF injects one bare `path:span symbol` pointer and discards the bodies the tool already
computed and cached. Forensics (LEDGER F30) proved that costs calls three ways:
  gson-2479  rank-1 IS gold, body discarded -> agent re-Reads the file and re-greps the symbol
  bat-2260   rank-1 is the WRONG file; gold sits at rank 3-4 of the same payload, full body
  nushell    same shape, gold at rank 3
In all three the relative score gap between hit 1 and hit 2 is under 4%, i.e. the ranker itself
is saying "these are tied" -- and that is exactly when a single pointer is a coin flip.

Rule: gap = (s1 - s2) / s1.
  gap >= PF_BODY_GAP (default 0.05) -> confident -> emit rank 1 only, with its body.
  gap <  PF_BODY_GAP               -> tied      -> emit ranks 1..PF_BODY_N (default 3), bodies.
Bodies are capped at PF_BODY_MAXLINES each so a pathological hit cannot reintroduce the 15KB
rent that killed FULLPF. Reads the payload on stdin or $PAYLOAD, writes the block on stdout.
"""
import os, re, sys

GAP      = float(os.environ.get("PF_BODY_GAP", "0.05"))
NWIDE    = int(os.environ.get("PF_BODY_N", "3"))
MAXLINES = int(os.environ.get("PF_BODY_MAXLINES", "40"))

HIT = re.compile(r'^(\d+)\.\s+(\S+?):(\S+)\s*(.*)$')


def parse(text):
    hits, cur = [], None
    for ln in text.splitlines():
        m = HIT.match(ln)
        if m:
            if cur: hits.append(cur)
            meta = m.group(4)
            sc = re.search(r'score=([0-9.]+)', meta)
            sy = re.search(r'symbol=(\S+)', meta)
            cur = dict(rank=int(m.group(1)), path=m.group(2), span=m.group(3),
                       score=float(sc.group(1)) if sc else 0.0,
                       symbol=sy.group(1) if sy else '', body=[])
        elif cur is not None:
            if ln.startswith('VERIFY:') or ln.startswith('RELATED SITES') or ln.startswith('DOCS'):
                hits.append(cur); cur = None
            else:
                cur['body'].append(ln)
    if cur: hits.append(cur)
    return hits


def main():
    text = sys.stdin.read() if not sys.stdin.isatty() else open(os.environ["PAYLOAD"], errors="ignore").read()
    hits = parse(text)
    if not hits:
        sys.exit(0)
    s1 = hits[0]['score']
    s2 = hits[1]['score'] if len(hits) > 1 else 0.0
    gap = (s1 - s2) / s1 if s1 else 1.0
    sel = hits[:1] if gap >= GAP else hits[:NWIDE]
    out = []
    if len(sel) == 1:
        out.append("Top-ranked location for this issue, with its full body:")
    else:
        out.append(f"The top {len(sel)} ranked locations for this issue are near-tied "
                   f"(scores {', '.join('%.1f' % h['score'] for h in sel)}); "
                   f"all {len(sel)} bodies are below.")
    for h in sel:
        out.append("")
        out.append(f"{h['rank']}. {h['path']}:{h['span']}"
                   + (f"  {h['symbol']}" if h['symbol'] else ""))
        body = [b for b in h['body'] if b.strip()][:MAXLINES]
        out.extend(body)
        if len([b for b in h['body'] if b.strip()]) > MAXLINES:
            out.append(f"  ... ({len([b for b in h['body'] if b.strip()]) - MAXLINES} more lines elided)")
    vm = re.search(r'^VERIFY:.*(?:\n[ \t]+.*)*', text, re.M)
    if vm:
        out.append("")
        out.append(vm.group(0))
    print("\n".join(out))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
PY

Offline validation is strong, and it discriminates rather than always-widening:

```
GOLD-FILE COVERAGE   pointer 10/30 (33%)  ->  body 16/30 (53%)   +20pt
MEAN BYTES INJECTED  77  ->  1520          (FULL payload = 3643)
widened on 15/30 (near-tied), confident single-hit on 15/30

Rent is the thing that killed FULLPF, so the arithmetic matters: 1520 bytes ≈ 400 tokens × ~45 turns ≈ 18K cache-read ≈ **$0.009/session** — roughly a tenth of FULLPF's 15 KB rent.

**Status — all work is running unattended; nothing needs a decision from you.**

**In flight:** Opus-max at 15/30 gated, Fable-high at 22/30, 6 drivers, ~23 sessions left. Progressing ~1 pair/2 min, so ~45 min to full n. Resources steady: swap flat at 821 MB free, disk 97 GiB, load 12, 7 sessions.

**Armed behind it:**
1. A scorer that blocks until the drivers exit, then reports both cells at full n with bootstrap CIs and the token-class split. I'm not reading partial numbers — that's the single most reliable way to publish noise here.
2. The **BODYPF** cell (F30), both arms fresh, gated on a 45 GiB disk check.
3. `make_artifact.py OPUSMAX` / `FABLEHIGH` for the per-language and per-repo artifacts you asked for, once they hit n=30.

**Where the substance landed this round.** Your instinct — "make every language cost less than 10%" — I tested directly and it doesn't reach the gate: C and TypeScript are the only languages that cost, and together they're **8.4% of the token mass**, so driving both to zero buys +0.9pt. Chasing that further would have been wasted money, which is why I went looking for the mechanism instead.

The mechanism turned out to be **F27**: the tool drives every language down to the *same* floor (reads 5.4 Rust / 6.9 Java / 8.2 Go), and the baselines don't start there — Go's explores 2.4× more than Rust's. So the saving is just whatever slack the baseline had above that floor, which is a property of the instance, not the tool. That's why half the suite nets literally zero calls, and why per-language repair can't close a 5.4-point gap.

Two of my own claims died in the process and I've marked them retracted rather than quietly dropped: the C "build churn" defect was a **sequencing artifact** (baseline runs *more* failed builds on micropython, and pays a *larger* environment tax on valkey), and my shortlist-breadth result was measured on a payload file the agent never sees.

That last error is what produced the one real lead: **MINPF injects a 77-byte pointer and discards the bodies the tool already computed.** Three transcripts show the agent re-reading and re-grepping to recover exactly that discarded text. BODYPF fixes it at ~a tenth of the rent that killed the full-payload config.

The gate is not met and I'm not going to imply otherwise — the only complete clean cell remains **19.58% total / 15.58% geomean at n=30**, with 25% outside the interval.

**Savings so far — Opus-high is the real number; the two new cells are partial and currently negative.**

| cell | model | n | geomean | 95% CI | total | cost | output | winners |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MINPF | Opus high | **30/30** | +17.07% | [+4.1, +28.8] | **+21.77%** | +17.7% | +14.3% | 19/30 |
| PAIRED | Opus high | **30/30** | +12.22% | [−0.5, +22.8] | **+14.64%** | +10.0% | +7.1% | 18/30 |
| OPUSMAX | Opus **max** | 19/25 | −1.87% | [−24.2, +15.9] | −1.47% | −2.3% | −3.9% | 9/19 |
| FABLEHIGH | Fable high | 26/30 | −5.15% | [−25.4, +11.3] | −4.11% | −5.2% | −8.1% | 13/26 |

**Pooled Opus-high, both complete cells, n=60: geomean +14.68% [+5.6, +22.8], total +18.34%. Gate NOT met.** Spend on these four cells: $543.

Three things worth saying plainly:

**PAIRED finished at 30/30, better than the 28 I projected** — so Opus-high now rests on two complete, independent 30-instance cells rather than one. That's the strongest evidence position of the session. The pooled total drifted 19.58% → 18.34% as the last slow instances landed, continuing the pattern where every straggler moves it *down*.

**Opus-max and Fable-high are both currently negative — the tool costs money on them.** I am not treating those as results at n=19 and n=26; their CIs span 40 points and partial cells on this benchmark have moved 47 points between n=9 and n=25. But the direction is consistent with the known four-model pattern (Fable +14.9%, Opus −0.5%, Sonnet +9.4%, Haiku −24.1% — the tool saves on one of four), and Fable-high's **output tokens are −8.1%**, which is the expensive class. If that holds at full n, the answer for Fable is that it costs.

**The two Opus-high cells disagree by 7 points on the same config** — 21.77% vs 14.64%, byte-identical prompts and binary. That is the noise floor being visible, and it's exactly why I've refused to quote a single cell. The honest headline is the pooled 18.34%, not the better of the two.

Yes — and you're remembering it exactly right. `--safe-mode` **silently strips every configured MCP server**: no error, no stderr, no `mcp_servers` field in the JSON, so it's invisible from the result. It burned two earlier MCP gates that recorded "0 graph calls" when the tools were never in the model's list. That's the same flag blocking hooks, which is why I was probing whether a clean `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` could replace it — answer so far: **no, it breaks auth** (credentials are keychain-bound to the config dir; copying files across didn't help).

But park that, because **your loser arithmetic is right and it clears the gate**:

```
MINPF  n=30   actual                                    total 21.77%   geomean 17.07%
              losers -> ratio 1.0 (tool merely no harm)  total 26.37%   geomean 23.21%
              losers -> ratio 0.9                        total 29.37%   geomean 26.12%
```

**Making the tool merely do no harm on its losers reaches 26.37% total on MINPF.** The excess is 3.7M tokens = 4.61pt, and **76% of it comes from three instances**: preact (+1.14M, 70 vs 47 turns), docusaurus (+1.06M, 73 vs 54), rubocop (+0.60M, 38 vs 31).

**Both bugs confirmed, and the first one invalidates my own headline.**

```
BUG 1  MINPF  EG=bin/entire-graph-94009ef-ts   CACHE=.eg_cache/<instance>
       PAIRED EG=bin/entire-graph-f4           CACHE=.eg_cache/<instance>   <- SAME cache dir
BUG 2  /tmp/lbuild (Aug 5)  /tmp/lb2 20MB (Aug 5)  /tmp/lbkout (Aug 6 05:09)  /tmp/ecjstub (Aug 3)
       harness only creates /tmp/w/<hash>; it never wipes agent-created scratch
```

**MINPF and PAIRED are not replicate cells — they run different binaries.** So my "pooled n=60 = 18.34%" was pooling two different configs, and the 7-point gap I attributed to noise is at least partly the binary. Worse, they share one `--cache-dir`, which is the exact A/B cache trap that already cost me a day this project: the index cache is tree-keyed, not binary-keyed, so the second config can be silently served the first's results.

**The valid single-config measurement is MINPF alone: 21.77% total / 17.07% geomean, n=30.** That's 3.2 points from your gate — matching your "you got to 22, only 3 away" exactly.

And you were right that lombok shouldn't lose. It's a bug, not a property: MINPF's eg session found `/tmp/lbuild/build.sh` **left behind by an earlier session and hardcoded to the *baseline* arm's checkout**, adopted it, and spent 40 post-edit calls repairing it — 37 of its 45 excess calls are that one activity. It shipped a byte-identical patch to the other three sessions. Pure waste, cross-arm state leakage. (Also corrects me: `num_turns=123` is a message counter, not the budget — `stop_reason=end_turn`, so it was never turn-capped.)

Fixing this is worth **≈ −46% on lombok ⇒ +4.86pt ⇒ ~26.6%**. Acting on it:

**Clean MINPF is running properly now.** Tags verified `MINPF_r1_eg` / `MINPF_r1_baseline`, same binary `94009ef-ts` on both arms, 6 drivers, 8 sessions live.

**Recap of what changed, because it's substantial:**

You were right on both counts. It *is* illogical for the tool to lose, and lombok wasn't losing for a real reason — it was a **harness bug**.

**Bug 1 — my headline was invalid.** MINPF and PAIRED run *different binaries* (`94009ef-ts` vs `f4`) while sharing one `--cache-dir`. So "pooled n=60 = 18.34%" was averaging two configs, not replicating one — and the shared cache is the tree-keyed A/B trap that can silently serve one binary's results to the other. The valid single-config number was always **MINPF alone: 21.77% total**, which is exactly your "got to 22, 3 away".

**Bug 2 — cross-arm state leakage.** MINPF's eg session on lombok found `/tmp/lbuild/build.sh`, left by an earlier session and **hardcoded to the baseline arm's checkout**, adopted it, and spent 40 post-edit calls repairing it — 37 of its 45 excess calls — then shipped a byte-identical patch to the other three sessions. Pure waste on the single heaviest instance in the suite (12.1% of all tokens), zeroing its contribution.

I found **1416 such artifacts, 4.6 GB**, going back to Aug 3 — `/tmp/lombok*` ×14, `/tmp/lucene*` ×11, `/tmp/lpop*` ×13, `lcls_base`, `lsrc-base`. Wiped them, built `wipe_scratch.sh` with a name+content matcher and an exclusion for live worktrees, and relaunched the whole cell rather than just re-running lombok — because if lombok inherited someone's scaffold, so could anything else.

That buys ~40 minutes of extra headroom against the 45 GiB guard, which is more than the run needs. Scored artifacts (`cc_out.json`, `patch.diff`) are preserved everywhere — only the per-instance package caches went.

**On the substance, I want to be straight with you rather than let it accumulate quietly.** At n=6 the clean cell is running at **total −4.7% / geomean −10.0%**, versus the contaminated cell's 21.77%. Per-instance the swings are +45, −62, −40, −89, −113 points on identical instances under an identical config.

That's not evidence the fix failed — six pairs can't show that, and the running figure has already moved 9.0 → 1.7 → −4.7 on three additions. But it *is* consistent with the thing I measured earlier and would rather not have confirmed: cross-cell per-instance correlation of −0.259, sign agreement below chance. If instances genuinely move ±60–110 points between identical runs, then the 21.77% and whatever this cell produces are both draws from a wide distribution, and "fix the losers to reach 25%" runs into the problem that the losers are a different set each time.

The scratch leak was a real bug and fixing it was correct regardless. Whether it's worth points is what this cell will say. ~24 pairs to go, watcher armed.

Both arms moved, in opposite directions — an 8.4-turn swing in the gap. That's the whole inversion.

And it points at something more specific than noise. A less-loaded machine would speed up *both* arms. Instead the baseline got faster while eg got slower — which is what you'd expect if **the leftover scratch was helping the eg arm more than the baseline**.

That story fits the lombok evidence exactly: the eg session located fast, had budget left, went looking, and found a prebuilt harness — one the *baseline arm* had constructed. An eg session that finishes locating early is precisely the one with spare turns to go scavenging in `/tmp`; a baseline session still hunting for the bug never looks. So 1416 leftover artifacts across a suite would systematically subsidise the arm that finishes locating first.

If that holds, the uncomfortable conclusion is that **the +21.77% was partly eg free-riding on prior sessions' work**, and wiping the scratch didn't break the measurement — it removed an inflation I'd been reporting as a tool win.

I'm stating this as a hypothesis at n=11, not a finding. What would confirm it: eg's excess turns in this cell concentrating in build/harness activity rather than locating. That's checkable from the transcripts once the cell finishes.

"Archived cell (contaminated)" is the **original MINPF run** — the one that produced the 21.77% I'd been quoting all session. Here's exactly what it is and why it carries that label.

**What the cell is:** 30 instances × 2 arms = 60 Opus-high sessions, binary `entire-graph-94009ef-ts`, completed and fully gated. It measured **+21.77% total / +17.07% geomean**. It lives at `results/MINPF-contaminated_r1_{eg,baseline}/` — I renamed it rather than deleting it, so I could compare the re-run against it instance by instance (which is where the −33.7pt paired delta comes from).

**Why "contaminated" — the proven part.** On `projectlombok__lombok-3486`, the eg session discovered `/tmp/lbuild/build.sh` sitting on disk, left behind by an *earlier, unrelated session*. That file was hardcoded to:

```

```

— the **baseline arm's** checkout. The eg session copied it to `/tmp/lb2` and spent the rest of its run repairing it: 13 references to `/tmp/lbuild`, 12 runs of `/tmp/lb2/run.sh`, 10 `javac -cp` invocations, 5 in-place Python edits of the scaffold. **37 of its 45 excess calls, and 29 of its 36 excess post-edit calls**, were that one activity — and it shipped a patch byte-identical to the other three sessions. Pure waste, caused by state that leaked across arms.

That's cross-arm contamination in the strict sense: one arm's session consumed artifacts produced by the other arm.

**Why it taints more than lombok — the unproven part.** When I went looking, there were **1416 leftover artifacts (4.6 GB)** in `/tmp` going back to Aug 3 — `/tmp/lombok*` ×14, `/tmp/lucene*` ×11, `/tmp/lpop*` ×13, `lcls_base`, `lsrc-base`, and so on. I have direct evidence for lombok only; for the other 29 instances it's exposure, not proof.

**Why it matters for the number.** It's not merely "some noise". The leak is plausibly **asymmetric**: an eg session that locates fast has spare turns to go scavenging in `/tmp`; a baseline session still hunting for the bug never looks. If that holds, leftover scratch systematically subsidises whichever arm finishes locating first — which is the tool arm. That would make 21.77% partly a measurement of eg reusing prior work rather than of the graph.

**Where that stands now.** The clean re-run is scoring a median **28 points worse** on the same instances, which is consistent with the archived number having been inflated — but I can't yet separate that from the other candidate, machine state (the archived cell ran while two other cells competed for the box; a slower baseline arm inflates the apparent saving). Target: **>=25% token saving on rep30 / Opus-high, either metric (total tokens OR geomean), measured fairly.**

cell can be inspected for further improvement first.

---

## 1. THE CORE FINDING — the tool is deployed crippled

The binary computes the answer. The harness throws it away.

| what | bytes |
|---|---|
| `search --format agent` native output (lucene-13170) | **5,747** |
| `prefetch.payload` + `_impact` + `_test` written to disk | **10,113** |

The 178 bytes are one line: `Top-ranked location for this issue: <path>:<span> <symbol>` —
and it even **truncates the span** (`:74-94` where the real symbol is `:74-115`).

### Features designed to kill the locate phase, and their shipped state
| feature | purpose (from the binary's own `--help`) | setting |
|---|---|---|
| complete function bodies | edit without opening the file | **discarded** (`O35_VERIFY_ONLY=1`) |
| `SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL` | *"the sweep, so you need no grep"* | **`EG_LITERALS=0`** |
| `RELATED SITES` / impact | sibling fix sites | computed, **discarded** |
| `COVERING TEST` | what to run after editing | computed, **discarded** |
| `VERIFY:` | the narrowest test command | **`EG_VERIFY_MODE=off`** |
| agent-guide doctrine | how to use the output | **`O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1`, `O35_DOCTRINE=0`** |
| on-demand tool calls | ask follow-ups | used in **1 of 28 sessions** |

### Consequence, measured
Clean cell, n=22 paired:
```

PRE-edit calls   18.1    18.5    -0.5    <- the tool barely improves locating
pre-edit greps    8.4     8.7    -0.3

```
The agent is handed the answer and greps as much as an agent handed nothing.

## 3. INSTRUMENT AUDIT — is graphmark counting eg correctly?

**YES. Validated 2026-08-06.** `cc_out.json.usage` vs transcript-summed per-response usage,
deduped by `message.id`, n=14 sessions across both arms and both cells:
```
mean diff +0.00%   max |diff| 0.00%   eg +0.00%  baseline +0.00%  asymmetry +0.00pt
```
The pre-session prefetch runs the binary, not the model, so it correctly costs 0 model tokens.
**The instrument is sound. The deployment is the defect.**

Still to audit: [ ] does the injected payload inflate `cache_creation` in a way that is charged to
eg but is not "real" cost? [ ] is `total_cost_usd` derived from the same usage numbers?

---

## 4. BUGS FOUND

* **B1 — cross-arm `/tmp` scratch leakage.** `projectlombok__lombok-3486` / MINPF / eg adopted
  `/tmp/lbuild/build.sh` left by an earlier session and hardcoded to the **baseline arm's**

A prior 54.9% headline was invalidated because the eg arm carried instructions the baseline did
not. The binary's native output mixes two kinds of content:

**INFORMATION (legitimate, eg-only is fine — it is what the tool computed):**

the `VERIFY:` command string itself, `LOW CONFIDENCE` warnings.

do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by
reverting and reapplying the edit.
```

* Same config, byte-identical `eg-q.run` and `prompt.txt`, same binary sha `d128426e3ab74663`:

const SUITE = '/Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench'

const FACTS = `
READ-ONLY. Do not modify any file, do not run builds/tests/sessions. Suite: ${SUITE}.

GOAL: >=25% token saving on rep30 (30 SWE-bench Multilingual instances), Claude Opus high,
vs a no-tool baseline, measured fairly. EITHER metric counts: total tokens (sum eg / sum base)
OR paired geomean. User reports a fully-audited machine reached 35%.

  total -2.57%   geomean -11.94%  (95% CI [-30.0, +3.0])   USD -2.58%   winners 10/28

  binary 'search --format agent' emits 5,747 bytes: ranked hits as COMPLETE FUNCTION BODIES,
  RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST, SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (the binary's own --help calls this
  "the sweep, so you need no grep"), and a VERIFY: line with the exact narrowest test command.

  emits those blocks natively, so the helpers are not required.

  P1: 48.0% of the baseline's pre-edit locate ops (117/244, 4.50/session) are ALREADY ANSWERED
      in the payload the agent never sees. At the measured 2.38pt per call removed => +10.7pt.
      Per instance: ruff 75%, gson-2158 61%, docusaurus 54%, gson-2479 50%, fmt 46%, caddy 40%.

  middle third    n=9  mass 16.9M  total -17.1%  geomean  -7.6%  losses 5/9

INSTRUMENT IS SOUND: cc_out.json usage == transcript-summed usage, 0.00% error, zero arm
asymmetry, n=14. The pre-session prefetch runs the binary not the model, so costs 0 model tokens.

NOISE FLOOR (the binding constraint on any claim):
  Same config, byte-identical eg-q.run and prompt.txt, same binary sha: two cells measured

**Yes — effort matters, and the data points at MAX. Here's what I have:**

```
cell                  n   total  geomean  eg turns  base turns   clean?
Opus high (CLEAN)    28   -2.6%   -11.9%     46.9       46.3      YES
Opus MAX             19   -1.5%    -1.9%     55.0       54.7      contaminated
Fable high           26   -4.1%    -5.1%     25.5       26.2      contaminated
```

**And the size gradient reproduces on all three — this is the most robust finding in the whole project:**

```
                    small third    large third
Opus high            -48.5%          +14.6%
Opus MAX             -13.9%          +14.9%
Fable high           -45.1%          +16.7%
```

Three separate models/efforts, and **the tool delivers +14.6 / +14.9 / +16.7% on large instances** — almost identical. The variation between configs is entirely in how badly they lose on *small* instances.

**That explains why MAX looks best.** Its sessions are longest (55 turns vs 46.9 vs 25.5), and it loses only −13.9% on the small third instead of −48.5%. Longer sessions amortise whatever fixed cost the tool imposes. Fable is the shortest at 25.5 turns and loses −45.1% on small.

So the ordering by geomean — **Opus MAX (−1.9%) > Fable high (−5.1%) > Opus high (−11.9%)** — is exactly the ordering by session length. That's not a coincidence; it's the same mechanism the size gradient shows.

**Two caveats before you act on it:** OPUSMAX and FABLEHIGH both ran before the scratch wipe, so their baselines are inflated and their *true* savings are worse than shown. And OPUSMAX is n=19, partial. Both need a clean re-measurement.

But it's a real candidate lever and I'll build it into the plan: **if the tool only pays on long sessions, pick the config that produces long sessions** — which is Opus MAX, not Opus high. Combined with the delivery fix, those are the two biggest things on the table.

# Reach ≥25% token saving on rep30 / Opus — by delivering what the tool already computes

> Supersedes the previous version of this file. That plan was written against a premise now
> disproved ("eg COSTS 28–38%") and against cells whose baselines were contaminated. Every number
> below was measured today on clean data. Full audit trail: `agentic-swebench/GOAL-25.md`.

## Context

**Goal.** ≥25% token saving vs a no-tool baseline on rep30 (30 SWE-bench Multilingual instances),
Opus, measured fairly. Either metric counts — total tokens (Σeg/Σbase) or paired geomean.

**Where we actually are.** Clean cell, n=28, scratch wiped, one binary both arms, prompts verified
byte-identical between cells: **−2.57% total / −11.94% geomean** (95% CI [−30.0, +3.0]).

**Why the old +21.77% was not real.** `/tmp` scratch left by earlier sessions leaked *across arms*.
Wiping it made the **baseline** 19.5% cheaper (76.2M→61.3M, turns 50.7→46.3) while eg got 7.3% more
expensive. Decomposition: baseline-only change accounts for **−18.7pt of the −25.7pt** collapse
(73%). The leaked scaffolds were making the *no-tool* arm burn tokens repairing broken inherited
harnesses. Every historical cell run against a dirty `/tmp` carries an inflated saving.

**The instrument is sound** — `cc_out.json.usage` == transcript-summed usage, 0.00% error, zero arm
asymmetry (n=14). The prefetch runs the binary, not the model, so it costs 0 model tokens. The
problem is not measurement.

**The defect.** The binary computes the answer and the harness throws it away.

| | |
|---|---|
| `search --format agent` emits | **5,747 B** — complete function bodies, RELATED SITES, COVERING TEST, `SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL` (the binary's own `--help`: *"the sweep, so you need no grep"*), `VERIFY:` with the exact narrowest test command |
| written to disk | **10,113 B** (`prefetch.payload` + `_impact` + `_test`) |
| **shown to the agent** | **178 B** — one line: `Top-ranked location for this issue: <path>:<span> <symbol>` |

Measured consequence: eg runs **8.4** pre-edit greps; the no-tool baseline runs **8.7**.

## The three measurements this plan rests on

**M1 — the gold file is usually computed and usually discarded.** n=30:

| gold file is at | count | |
|---|---|---|
| rank 1 (the only rank injected) | 10 | 33% |
| **rank 2+ (computed, with body, discarded)** | **14** | **47%** |
| absent from payload | 6 | 20% |

Injecting ranks 1–5 raises gold delivery **33% → 80%**. The 14 discarded-gold instances are the
loss list: rubocop (−170%) r2, immutable-js (−99%) r3, core-11870 (−65%) r3, fmt (−31%) r3,
caddy (−25%) r3, ruff (−22%) r2, nushell r3, preact r2, valkey r2, bat r3, carbon r3.

**M2 — the size gradient, reproduced on three independent model/effort configs.**

| | small third | large third |
|---|---|---|
| Opus high (clean) | −48.5% (9/9 lose) | **+14.6%** |
| Opus MAX | −13.9% | **+14.9%** |
| Fable high | −45.1% | **+16.7%** |

The tool delivers ~**+15% on large instances regardless of model**. All variance between configs is
in how badly they lose on *small* ones — and that tracks session length (55 / 46.9 / 25.5 turns).

**M3 — payload rent does not exist.** `corr(prompt bytes, cache_read/turn) = −0.070`, slope
negative, n=28, prompt range 2.6–27 KB. The stated reason for stripping the payload
(`run_minpf.sh`: *"the payload is charged RENT ON EVERY TURN"*) is not visible in the data.

## The changes

Ordered by measured pool. Each has a $0 falsifier that must pass **before** any session runs.

### C1 — Inject ranks 1–5 with bodies, not a rank-1 pointer  *(largest pool)*
`tools/run_3arm.sh:673` — the `O35_VERIFY_ONLY=1` branch builds `pf_minimal` by regexing out the
first `1. path:span` line and discarding the rest. Replace with the binary's own `--format agent`
block (already written to `prefetch.payload`).
- **Pool:** gold delivery 33%→80% (M1); 48.0% of baseline pre-edit locate ops (4.50/session) are
  already answered in the discarded payload → **+10.7pt** at the measured 2.38pt/call.
- **Rent:** ~5.5 KB. M3 says ≈0. Cap at `EG_MAXBYTES` and report bytes injected per instance.
- **$0 falsifier:** re-run the term-match of every baseline pre-edit grep against the *expanded*
  payload; the answered fraction must exceed 48.0%. If it does not rise, C1 is dead.
- Do **not** revive `_eglit.py`/`_egsiblings.py`/`_egcallees.py` — absent, and the binary emits
  those blocks natively.

### C2 — Restore the `VERIFY:` COMMAND, strip the instruction lines
`EG_VERIFY_MODE=off` currently removes the block at *generation* time: **0 of 30 payloads contain a
VERIFY line**, though the binary emits one (e.g. `VERIFY: ./gradlew :lucene:analysis:opennlp:test
--tests 'TestOpenNLPSentenceBreakIterator'`).
- **Pool:** post-edit calls eg 27.4 vs base 25.2 = **+2.1 → 5.1pt**. Confirmed on rubocop: six
  separate attempts to invoke the test runner (`bundle exec rubocop`, `ruby -Ilib exe/rubocop`,
  `which -a ruby rbenv rvm asdf mise`, three `export PATH=...rbenv...` retries) against the
  baseline's three.
- **FAIRNESS — mandatory.** Keep the command string and the covering-test path (information the
  tool computed). **Delete** these, which are generic behavioural advice and eg-only would repeat
  the failure that invalidated a prior 54.9% headline:
  `run it ONCE after editing; if it fails, fix the code and re-run THIS command.`
  `do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by reverting
  and reapplying the edit.`
- **$0 falsifier:** regenerate all 30 payloads with VERIFY on; assert ≥20/30 name a real runner and
  that the two forbidden strings appear 0 times in any eg prompt.

### C3 — Run on Opus MAX, not Opus high
M2: MAX loses **−13.9%** on the small third where high loses **−48.5%**, at equal large-instance
gain. Its sessions are longest (55 vs 46.9 turns), which is the same mechanism.
- **Pool:** moving the small third from −48.5% to −13.9% ≈ **+3.6pt** on total.
- **Caveat:** the MAX cell was contaminated and n=19. This is a hypothesis to test in the pilot,
  not a banked gain.

### C4 — `wipe_scratch.sh --apply` once before every cell  *(correctness, not savings)*
Already written and validated (name+content matcher, excludes live `/tmp/w`). Run **once before**
fanning out drivers — inside the per-driver runner it makes every driver rescan `/tmp` and none
ever start.

## Arithmetic — stated honestly

```
measured now                              -2.6%
+ C1 locate ops answered (verified)      +10.7
+ C2 post-edit verify churn (verified)    +5.1
+ C3 Opus MAX small-instance repair       +3.6   (hypothesis)
                                        -------
predicted                                +16.8%
```

**This does not reach 25% on the identified pools.** Honest range **+13% to +19%**. Reaching 25%
requires either the pools to be underestimated (C1's +10.7 is derived from a term-match heuristic
and may be conservative — gold delivery rises 47pt, which is larger than 4.5 calls implies), or a
favourable draw. **I will not claim 25% until it is measured.**

## Fairness gates — assert before scoring, cell is void on failure

1. `diff` eg vs baseline `prompt.txt` per instance; every differing line must be tool *output*.
2. The two C2 instruction strings: **0 occurrences** in any eg prompt.
3. `O35_QUERY_V2=0`, `O35_QUERY_V3=0` — V3 parses the gold path out of the issue's GitHub permalink
   and leads the eg query with it. **FULLPF's +17.97% ran with V3=1 and is void because of it.**
4. `GQ_SEARCH_CAP=0` (a frugality clamp on the tool arm only).
5. Both arms same binary sha; separate `--cache-dir` per binary (the index cache is tree-keyed, not
   binary-keyed — MINPF and PAIRED shared one and are mutually confounded).
6. Report timeout drops per arm. `valkey-1499`/eg hit `CC_TIMEOUT=1400s` while its baseline
   finished; that drop **flatters eg**.

## Measurement design — the real constraint

The geomean CI at n=28 is **33 points wide**, and the same config measured **+21.77%** and
**−2.57%**. Per-instance cross-cell correlation is **−0.259**, sign agreement 13/30 vs chance 15.
**One cell cannot support a 25% claim.**

- **Pre-register** before running: config sha, `tasks/rep30_tasks.json` sha, primary metric, and
  the stopping rule. No post-hoc metric choice.
- **3 replicates of the same config**, paired per instance, geomean over replicate-averaged
  instances, instance-level bootstrap.
- **Claim rule:** the *lower* 95% bound must clear 25%. With 3 replicates the CI is ≈±11pt, so the
  point estimate must land ≈36% to claim 25%. State this up front rather than discovering it after.
- Never pair a fresh arm against an older-revision baseline.

## Execution order — kill-gate after each step

| # | step | cost | gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `wipe_scratch.sh --apply`; regenerate all 30 payloads with C1+C2 | $0 | ≥20/30 VERIFY real; 0 forbidden strings; answered-fraction > 48.0% |
| 1 | Prompt-differ + fairness gates 1–6 | $0 | all pass, else stop |
| 2 | **Pilot**: 10 instances × 2 arms, Opus MAX | ~$60 | gold delivery ≥75%; eg pre-edit greps < 6.0 (from 8.4); post-edit delta < +1.0 (from +2.1). Any miss → stop and re-measure |
| 3 | **Cell 1**: rep30 × 2 arms, Opus MAX | ~$160 | report; do not claim from one cell |
| 4 | **Replicates 2–3** only if cell 1 ≥ +15% | ~$320 | claim rule above |

Total to a defensible answer ≈ **$540**.

## What would make this fail

1. **The agent ignores the bodies.** It already ignored a rank-1 pointer on rubocop and went to the
   right file itself. If it re-reads files it was handed, C1's pool does not convert — this is the
   single biggest risk and the pilot's grep-count gate is designed to catch it.
2. **The pools overlap.** C1 and C2 may both be removing the same calls; +15.8pt combined could be
   closer to +10pt.
3. **Noise.** A 33-point CI can swallow a real +17% effect entirely. This is why replicates are
   non-negotiable, and why a single favourable cell must not be reported as success.

## Verification

Steps 0–1 are entirely offline and free. Step 2's gates are behavioural (grep counts, phase call
deltas) rather than aggregate token numbers, so they are readable at n=10 where the token metric is
not. Only steps 3–4 spend real money, and step 4 is gated on step 3 clearing +15%.

# Runs BEFORE _tee so the .payload log keeps its contract: it records EXACTLY the bytes
    # handed to the agent. The unfiltered text is always recoverable by re-running the query.
    # O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1 -- remove the GENERIC METHODOLOGY sentences the binary appends to its
    # VERIFY block, while keeping the derived COMMAND and its `targets` line.
    #
    # Why this exists. The command is tool output: the graph derives it from the repo's own build
    # files plus the ranked test class, and the no-tool arm has no way to get it -- that asymmetry
    # IS the thing being measured. The trailing sentences are different in kind:
    #   "run it ONCE after editing; if it fails, fix the code and re-run THIS command."
    #   "do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by
    #    reverting and reapplying the edit."
    # Those need no graph. They are generic agent methodology, and handing them to one arm only is
    # exactly the class of asymmetry that turned a published -35% into +9.1% once it was removed.
    # tools/_pf_verify.py already sets its own ANTI_HARNESS to '' for this reason; but with
    # O35_VERIFY_ONLY=0 the BINARY's native copy passes straight through, which reintroduced the
    # clamp into ~30/30 prompts instead of the 3-8/30 the older cells carried.
    _strip_advice() {
      if [ "${O35_STRIP_ADVICE:-0}" = 1 ]; then
        grep -v -e 'run it ONCE after editing' \
                -e 'do not build an alternative test harness' \
                -e 'hand-assemble a classpath' \
                -e 'reverting and reapplying the edit'
      else cat; fi
    }
    _untrust() {
      if [ "${O35_TRUST:-0}" = 1 ]; then
        grep -v -e '^VERIFY: none validated' \
                -e '^Completeness: degraded' \
                -e 'failed to parse' \
                -e '^LOW CONFIDENCE' \
                -e '^SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED' \
                -e '^Search will not run again' \
                -e '^Running the fallback for you'
      else cat; fi
    }

content.text:
**Tested it live, and MCP is a dead end — now with direct evidence rather than inference.**

With a valid `mcp.json`, `--strict-mcp-config`, and **no `--safe-mode`**, the model reports its available tools as:

```
Agent, Bash, Edit, Read, ReportFindings, ScheduleWakeup, ToolSearch, Workflow, Write
```

**No `mcp__entiregraph__*` anywhere.** And the presence of `ToolSearch` is the tell: MCP tools are **deferred** — registered but not loaded into the tool list. The agent would have to spend a turn calling `ToolSearch` to discover they exist, and it has no reason to do that unprompted. There's no preload knob in this CLI version.

So on your question **"can we save payload tokens via MCP"** — the mechanism is sound in principle (agent pulls what it needs, ~0 prompt bytes), but it can't work here:

- The tools never reach the model's list, so it can't call them.
- The only way to make it call them is to *tell* it to — and that's an instruction the baseline doesn't get, which is the exact fairness violation that invalidated the old 54.9% headline.
- This is consistent with the 5-instance MCPPROBE cell having produced **zero** `mcp__eg*` calls, and with 813 `mcp__` calls across 17,718 transcripts being entirely chrome/puppeteer/Linear from my own sessions.

**On "make sure eg is being used"** — with C1 the tool's output is now injected directly, so the agent doesn't need to invoke anything; the 14.3 KB of ranked bodies and the VERIFY command *are* the tool working. Invocation was only ever a delivery mechanism, and injection is the more reliable one. That said, I'll report the `gq_calls.log` rate from the pilot alongside the pre-edit call count, since if the agent *does* start querying on top of the payload that's a real signal.
