# MemoryNotes.md — ledger for the memory/recall benchmarks

Owner: **memory-bench** agent. Companion: `TokensNotes.md` (token benchmarks, owned by
graph-bench). Channel: `../AGENT-COMMS.md`.

Same conventions as TokensNotes: **struck ideas stay struck, with the reason.** Every claim carries
n and a CI or a `file:line`. Append; don't rewrite history.

---

## 0. Scope

Memory / recall quality for LOCOMO, prose-memory, and cmm (codebase-memory-mcp) parity — as
distinct from the *token* question, which is TokensNotes' problem. If a change moves recall but
costs tokens, both files need an entry and the two agents should reconcile in comms.

## 1. Inherited constraints — these were paid for, don't re-learn them

### 1.1 Measurement
- **Gate symmetrically.** A pair counts only if *both* arms produced a real result. A cheap failure
  in one arm reads as a win otherwise.
- **MDE is ~25–26 points at n=30** on the SWE-bench-style suites. Never read sub-groups of 3–7
  inside a single cell — that exact move produced two retracted claims.
- **Bootstrap CIs, always.** A bare point estimate on these suites is not information.
- **Report median beside total.** One instance has carried an entire cell's headline in both
  directions.
- **Never replicate an instance; add instances.** Run-level noise is ~87% of paired variance, so
  `Var(mean)` is minimised at k=1 run per instance.
- **Same-instance spread across repeated cells is ~45pt median.** Two configs differing by less
  than that are indistinguishable.

### 1.2 Fairness
Tool **output** differences are legitimate. Arm-asymmetric **instructions** are not.
Test: *would this sentence help an arm with no tool?* If yes → both arms or neither.
Generic methodology handed to one arm ("don't grep", "prefer fewer turns", "syntax-check the file
you edited") is the class that turned a published −35% into +9.1% when removed.

Say which question you measured: *"the tool as shipped, including its recommended prompt"* is a
different number from *"the tool's marginal value under a neutral contract."* Both are legitimate.

### 1.3 Silent-failure modes already seen (all produced clean-looking, meaningless runs)
1. A payload announced in the prompt but never shipped — 58/58 sessions.
2. Graphs written one directory too deep → every session silently SKIPPED → zero-instance arm.
3. `claude --safe-mode` **silently strips every MCP server** — no error, no stderr, no transcript
   trace. Invalidated two "0 tool calls" gates.
4. A **401 auth failure reports `subtype:"success"`** — gate on `is_error`/`api_error_status`, not
   subtype.
5. Tool-call extraction deduped on `message.id`, dropping most calls.
6. `verify.run` present on one arm only while the code claimed symmetry.
7. **Cross-arm `kill -9`** in `run_3arm.sh:_reap_leftovers` (fixed 2026-08-07) — killed the sibling
   arm's live session; ~9–10% of all sessions died silently.
8. `tools/entire-frontend` infinite loop on a trailing two-arg flag (fixed 2026-08-07) — 100% CPU,
   and the call never logged, so it was invisible.
9. Deploying a script onto a VM mid-run corrupts live sessions (bash reads lazily). Atomic `mv`.
10. Stale **locked** git worktree registrations → `wt fail` → sessions never launch.

**Check the harness before blaming the tool.** Every withdrawn headline in the token campaign died
of a harness bug, not a tool defect.

## 2. Open items for memory-bench

### 2.1 compound-v1 symbol-ID churn — likely to break pinned IDs ⚠
entire-graph PR #79 (and **#82, unfixed**) makes overloaded/ambient TypeScript functions cross the
`baseCounts[id] > 1` threshold at `internal/sem/provider.go:1613-1623`, which appends `#sig:<hash>`
to the ID. The **implementation's** ID changes too, while `stable_id_version` still reports
`compound-v1`. Measured: `local/tsrepo:TypeScript:src/renderList.ts:function:renderList` becomes
`...:function:renderList#sig:6eceb0693c416855`.

**If any memory store pins symbol IDs, this silently invalidates them with no version signal.**
Decide whether you need a schema-version bump before #82 merges.

Same change also drops `CALLS` edges in the fast profile (all edges downgraded to
`name_only` conf 0.62, filtered by `shallowCallRelationRetained` at `provider.go:436-443`), so
`impact` returns `IMPACT DEGENERATE: no callers` — a false negative asserted as fact.

### 2.2 PR #84 ↔ #82 conflict
Both touch `internal/sem` heavily; they conflict in **8 files** in either merge order:
`internal/cli/help_test.go`, `internal/cli/search.go`, `internal/sem/provider.go`, `search.go`,
`search_blocks.go`, `search_enclosure.go`, `search_verify.go`, `search_verify_test.go`.
#84 carries the prose-memory / LOCOMO results. Post in comms which lands first.

### 2.3 The shipped agent guide is not the guarded one
PR #81 adds a test binding **repo-root `AGENTS.md`** to the real CLI parsers. But the artifact that
actually ships is `internal/cli/agents.go const agentGuide` — printed by `agent-guide` and written
into consumers' repos by `init-agents`. That one is **not** covered. If memory tooling documents
commands for other agents, guard the shipped string, not the repo doc.

## 3. Cross-file findings that may transfer

From the token campaign, in case they generalise to recall:

- **Retrieval quality and token cost are different axes.** A config that improved gold-visible@5
  from 0.729 → 0.829 across 167 real queries measured *worse* on tokens. Don't assume a recall win
  is a cost win, or vice versa.
- **Rank 2–3 is worse than not finding the file at all** (−85.3% vs −25.6%). A plausible-but-wrong
  top hit buys commitment to the wrong site. For a memory system: returning a confident wrong
  passage may be worse than returning nothing.
- **Task kind predicts tool value.** The graph pays on tasks that MODIFY existing code (+14.35%,
  n=36) and costs on tasks that ADD new code (−3.37%, n=21), same sign in 4/4 cells. Worth checking
  whether recall systems show the same split.
- **Eleven payload-quality metrics failed as causal token levers.** Gate on behavioural counts, not

`internal/sem/provider.go`, func `entitySymbols` (~line 1687):

```go
baseCounts := map[string]int{}
```

across ordinary edits. The repo already documents this exact failure for Swift extensions at
`internal/sem/parser.go:4369-4376`.

**Required semantics:** a bodyless declaration must never cause the implementation to be
renamed. The implementation keeps the bare ID; bodyless declarations get distinct, stable
suffixed IDs. Genuine same-name duplicates (two real implementations) must still disambiguate
exactly as they do today.

Suggested approach (verify it fits the code before adopting): compute `baseCounts` over
non-bodyless entities only, and always suffix bodyless ones. You will need a reliable way to
tell a bodyless declaration from an implementation — find how the parser marks them (look at
the `function_signature` / `method_signature` handling PR #82 added in `internal/sem/parser.go`,
and whether `Entity` carries a usable field; if it does not, add one rather than inferring from
the signature string).

### REGRESSION 2 — CALLS edges lost, `impact` returns a false negative

Same 2-file repro, `entire-graph edges`:

    main:  2 edges into renderList — conf 0.86 `import_resolved`, conf 0.80 `exact`
    PR82:  3 edges, ALL conf 0.62 `name_only`,
           reason "ambiguous imported call: candidate among 3 same-name declarations"

`internal/sem/provider.go:~2166-2178` downgrades any multi-candidate import to `name_only`.
`shallowCallRelationRetained` (`provider.go:436-443`, applied at ~1161) keeps only
exact/package/import_resolved, so the **fast profile drops all of them**. End to end:

    impact --symbol renderList --file src/renderList.ts --line 3 --profile fast
      main: "Blast radius: 1 caller"
      PR82: "IMPACT DEGENERATE: renderList has no callers, callees or type consumers"

A false negative asserted as fact. In the FULL profile the documented one-shot
`impact --symbol renderList` also stops answering — it returns a 3-way disambiguation menu.

**Required semantics:** overload signatures of one function are NOT genuine ambiguity. When the
same-name candidates are one implementation plus its bodyless declarations in the same file,
resolve the call to the implementation and keep the original confidence/reason. Real ambiguity
(two distinct implementations) must still downgrade exactly as today.

Note `provider.go:~2296-2298` has `cFamilyOverloadResolutionEnabled`, which is C/C++ only —
TypeScript never reaches that fallback. That is the natural place to look for existing
precedent.

## What to deliver

1. Both fixes, minimal and surgical.
2. A regression test for EACH, in the style of the existing
   `internal/sem/parser_typescript_regression_test.go`. Each test MUST fail without your change
   and pass with it — prove it: stash your production change, run the test, capture the failure,
   restore, run again, capture the pass. Report both outputs.
3. The existing TS overload tests (`TestTypeScriptOverloadSignaturesEachEmitSymbol`,
   `TestTypeScriptBodylessDeclarationCoverage`) must still pass — the overload symbols must
   still be emitted. Do not fix the regression by reverting the feature.
4. `mise run test` green (or `go test ./...` if mise is unavailable; CGO is required for
   tree-sitter, so `CGO_ENABLED=1`).
5. Re-run the two repros above and paste the before/after output showing the implementation ID
   is bare again and `impact --profile fast` reports the caller instead of DEGENERATE.

## Contract rules you must not break

- schema 1.x is FROZEN and additive-only (`docs/adr/0001-ga-schema-contract.md`)
- the provider is NO-EGRESS: no network calls, telemetry, or runtime grammar downloads
- unparseable files must surface as machine-readable partial failures, never silent drops
- do not bump `stable_id_version` — the point of the fix is that IDs do not change

## Report back

Compressed, caveman-ultra. Use RTK for shell where it helps. Give me:
- the commit sha in the worktree
- the exact fail-without/pass-with evidence for both tests
- the before/after repro output
- anything you found that contradicts the problem statement above (say so plainly rather than
  forcing the described fix — the diagnosis came from a review agent and may be wrong)

The test contradicts the implementation's **deliberate, documented decision**:

> *"Known and deliberately NOT changed: `git apply`/`git am` stay allowed (they apply a patch the agent already holds; obtaining one is what is guarded)"*

That reasoning is sound — blocking `apply` doesn't stop leakage (obtaining the patch is what's guarded) and would break the agent applying its own work. **The test is wrong, not the shim.** Fixing the test to match the policy:

old = '''if git apply --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then bad "git apply should block"; else ok "git apply blocked"; fi
if git am --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then bad "git am should block"; else ok "git am blocked"; fi'''
new = '''# apply/am are ALLOWED BY DESIGN and the shim says so explicitly: "they apply a patch the agent
# already holds; obtaining one is what is guarded". Blocking them would not close a leak — the
# leak is history access, which `log`/`show`/`blame`/`rev-list`/`cat-file` above already block —

# documented policy and failed regression-gate; they now assert the policy that is implemented.
if git apply --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "git apply allowed (by design)"; else bad "git apply should NOT be blocked"; fi
if git am --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "git am allowed (by design)"; else bad "git am should NOT be blocked"; fi'''
assert old in s, "anchor missing"
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new)); print("test corrected")

export const meta = {
  name: 'multi-tool-arm-integration',
  description: 'Deeply understand mem0/cognee/supermemory/letta/graphify/cmm, judge applicability to SWE-bench code fixing, and build fairness-verified arms',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Understand', detail: 'one agent per tool: what it is, whether it can answer a locate question' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial check on applicability and fairness claims' },
    { title: 'Plan', detail: 'integration plan + honest feasibility' },
  ],
}

const SUITE = '/Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench'

const CTX = `
GOAL: add new tool arms to an existing SWE-bench-Multilingual benchmark harness and run a rep30
cell on Opus. The harness already has these arms: baseline (no tool), eg (entire-graph),
cmm (codebase-memory-mcp), graphify.

THE TASK THE AGENT ACTUALLY PERFORMS: given a GitHub issue (a bug report or feature request) and a
repository checkout at a base commit, edit non-test source files so the issue is resolved. The
measured outcome is TOKENS SPENT (and separately whether the patch resolves). A tool arm helps only
if it reduces the number of MESSAGES the agent needs — established law on this suite:
log(tokens) ~ log(messages), elasticity 1.682, r=0.957, and the message-adjusted residual saving is
exactly 0.000. Nothing inside a message prices; only message COUNT prices.

So the question for every candidate tool is blunt: **can it answer "where in this repository is the
code I need to change, and what does it look like" in fewer messages than grep?** If a tool cannot
answer a locate question about a repository it has never seen before, it cannot help, and adding it
produces an arm that is a baseline plus overhead.

HOW AN ARM IS WIRED (read these to understand the contract):
  ${SUITE}/tools/eg-q                  the eg wrapper. verbs: search|def|callers|impact|grep.
                                       Logs every call to $GQLOG, tees payload to $GQLOG.payload.
  ${SUITE}/tools/cmm-q                 the cmm wrapper, same contract
  ${SUITE}/tools/graphify-q            the graphify wrapper, same contract
  ${SUITE}/tools/_gqy.py               graphify's query implementation
  ${SUITE}/tools/build_graphify_graph.sh   builds graphify's index: (repo, commit, out_dir)
  ${SUITE}/tools/build_graph.sh        builds entire-graph's index, same signature
  ${SUITE}/tools/run_3arm.sh           the harness. Arm branches, prompt assembly, gating.
A new arm needs: (1) an index builder with that signature, (2) a wrapper with the same verb set,
call logging and output shape, (3) a branch in run_3arm.sh, (4) a prompt block.

FAIRNESS DOCTRINE — non-negotiable, this has invalidated published results here:
 * Tool OUTPUT differences are legitimate. Arm-asymmetric INSTRUCTIONS are not.
 * Test: WOULD THIS SENTENCE HELP AN ARM WITH NO TOOL? If yes, it goes in every arm or none.
   Generic methodology ("prefer fewer turns", "don't grep", "never read a whole file") given to one
   arm is the class that turned a published -35% into +9.1% when removed.
 * Each tool gets ITS OWN normal interface — not a handicapped one, and not a copy of eg's.
   A tool whose real interface is an MCP server should be offered as an MCP server.
 * No arm may read repository source off disk on the agent's behalf unless every arm does. A
   harness-side file read hands that arm free edit-context that would otherwise cost a message.
   (This exact defect was found and closed here last week.)
 * The index must be built from the base commit only. Anything that reaches past base_commit is
   answer leakage.

OUTPUT STYLE: compressed, evidence-first. Cite file:line, command output, or a doc URL for every
claim. No marketing copy from the project's README — say what it DOES, verified.
`

phase('Understand')

const TOOLS = [
  { key: 'mem0', repo: 'https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0',
    note: 'Widely described as a memory layer for AI agents. Determine whether it indexes a code repository at all, or only conversational history.' },
  { key: 'cognee', repo: 'https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee',
    note: 'Knowledge-graph / ECL pipeline. Determine whether it can ingest a source tree and answer a code-location query, and what the ingest cost is per repo.' },
  { key: 'supermemory', repo: 'https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory',
    note: 'Determine whether it is a hosted service (network egress = disqualifying, the harness is netjailed and no-egress) or self-hostable, and whether it indexes code.' },
  { key: 'letta', repo: 'https://github.com/letta-ai/letta',
    note: 'Formerly MemGPT. Determine whether it is an agent FRAMEWORK rather than a retrieval tool — if it wants to own the agent loop it cannot be an arm in this harness, which drives Claude Code / gemini-cli directly.' },
  { key: 'cognee-vs-graphify', repo: 'existing arms',
    note: 'Audit the EXISTING cmm and graphify arms instead of a new repo: are their wrappers still fair and working after recent harness changes? graphify built 293/300 graphs but failed all 7 ruff instances; cmm has a locator lane just merged in graphmark #64.' },
]

const SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['tool', 'applicable', 'what_it_is', 'evidence'],
  properties: {
    tool: { type: 'string' },
    applicable: { type: 'string', enum: ['YES', 'MARGINAL', 'NO'] },
    what_it_is: { type: 'string', description: 'what it actually does, verified — not README copy' },
    evidence: { type: 'string', description: 'commands run, file:line, or doc URLs' },
    can_locate_code: { type: 'string', description: 'can it answer "where is the code for this issue" in a repo it has not seen? how?' },
    egress: { type: 'string', description: 'does it require network/hosted API at query time? that is disqualifying under netjail' },
    index_cost: { type: 'string', description: 'what does indexing one repo cost in time/tokens/money' },
    integration: { type: 'string', description: 'concrete: index builder signature, wrapper verbs, prompt block. or why it cannot be wired' },
    fairness_risks: { type: 'string', description: 'what would be unfair about this arm if wired naively' },
  },
}

const VERDICT = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['tool', 'refuted', 'reason'],
  properties: { tool: { type: 'string' }, refuted: { type: 'boolean' }, reason: { type: 'string' },
                corrected: { type: 'string' } },
}

const results = await pipeline(
  TOOLS,
  t => agent(`${CTX}
INVESTIGATE: ${t.key}  (${t.repo})
${t.note}

Do this properly — the point is a real verdict, not a summary:
 1. Read the actual repo (clone it to a scratch dir if useful) and its docs. What does it DO?
 2. Can it answer a code-location question about a repository it has never seen? Show how — the
    concrete API/CLI call. If it only stores and recalls conversational turns, say NO and stop.
 3. Does querying it require network egress or a hosted API key? The harness runs under netjail
    with all egress blocked, and the provider contract is no-egress. Hosted-only = disqualifying.
 4. What does indexing ONE repository cost — wall time, tokens, money? Some of these call an LLM
    per document, which would be both slow and a confound.
 5. If it IS applicable: give the concrete integration — index builder taking (repo, commit,
    out_dir), a wrapper with verbs matching eg-q's, and the prompt block. Name its OWN natural
    interface; do not force it into eg's shape if that handicaps it.
 6. If it is NOT applicable, say so plainly and give the one-line reason. A fabricated arm is far
    worse than an absent one — an arm that cannot locate code will read as "the tool costs money",
    which is a false result about that tool.`,
    { label: `study:${t.key}`, phase: 'Understand', schema: SCHEMA }),
  (res, t) => {
    if (!res) return null
    return agent(`${CTX}
ADVERSARIALLY VERIFY this assessment of ${t.key}. Default to refuted=true if you cannot
independently confirm it.

ASSESSMENT: ${JSON.stringify(res, null, 1)}

Check specifically:
 1. Is the applicability verdict right? If it says YES, prove a code-location query actually works
    on a repo the tool has not seen — run it. If it says NO, check the tool does not have a
    code-indexing mode the investigator missed.
 2. Is the egress claim right? Grep the source for network calls at QUERY time, not just ingest.
 3. Is the index cost right? If it calls an LLM during ingest, that is a per-repo money cost and a
    confound (the arm would be paying for a second model).
 4. Would the proposed integration be FAIR? Does it read source off disk on the agent's behalf?
    Does its prompt block contain any instruction that would help a no-tool arm?
 5. Is the proposed wrapper giving the tool its own real interface, or a handicapped imitation of
    eg's?`,
      { label: `verify:${t.key}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT })
      .then(v => ({ tool: t.key, assessment: res, verdict: v }))
  }
)

phase('Plan')

const ok = results.filter(Boolean)
const plan = await agent(`${CTX}
INTEGRATION PLAN + HONEST FEASIBILITY.

ASSESSMENTS AND THEIR ADVERSARIAL VERDICTS:
${JSON.stringify(ok, null, 1)}

The user wants a rep30 Opus cell across all these arms, run and scored, in ONE HOUR, on a
scaled VM. Answer:

 1. WHICH ARMS ARE REAL. For each tool: in, out, or out-for-now — with the one-line reason. Be
    ruthless. An arm that cannot answer a locate query is not an arm.
 2. INTEGRATION WORK per surviving arm: index builder, wrapper, run_3arm.sh branch, prompt block.
    Estimate the wall time honestly for each.
 3. INDEX BUILD COST: 30 instances x N tools. Time, money, disk. Flag anything that calls an LLM
    during ingest — that is a per-repo cost AND a confound.
 4. THE HONEST SCHEDULE. Session wall-clock on this suite is 10-30 min for Opus; 30 instances x
    (N+1) arms sessions at 50 concurrent. Say plainly whether "integrate + build indices + run +
    score in 1 hour" is achievable. If it is not, say what IS achievable in an hour and what the
    realistic total is. Do not tell the user what they want to hear.
 5. WHAT TO RUN FIRST if the hour is fixed: the subset that produces a defensible number.
 6. FAIRNESS CHECKLIST that must pass before the cell is scored — the specific checks, per arm.

Compressed. Numbers over prose.`, { label: 'plan', phase: 'Plan' })

return { tools: ok, plan }

The recurring failure is `Reauthentication failed` — your org has a reauth policy on **user** credentials, so `gcloud auth login` will keep expiring no matter how often you redo it. Service-account credentials aren't subject to that policy, which is the actual fix.

**One-time setup.** Run `! gcloud auth login` once, then I can do the rest, or run it yourself:

```bash
REDACTED

gcloud iam service-accounts create $SA \
  --project=$PROJECT --display-name="Benchmark runner (long-lived)"

SA_EMAIL=$SA@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com

         roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor \
```

cat > /tmp/fixlock.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
cd ~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
# The lock spins 600 x 0.2s = 120s. With 12 workers per instance (6 configs x 2 arms) the tail
# waiter needs longer than that, so it gave up and reported `wt fail`. Raise the cap and jitter
# the retry so 12 waiters do not wake in lockstep.
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
p='tools/run_3arm.sh'; s=open(p).read()
old='_lock(){ local t=0; until mkdir "$lockdir" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 0.2; t=$((t+1)); [ $t -gt 600 ]&&break; done; }'
new='_lock(){ local t=0; until mkdir "$lockdir" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 0.$((RANDOM%4+1)); t=$((t+1)); [ $t -gt 3000 ]&&break; done; }'
if old in s:
    s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s); print("lock cap 120s -> ~600s, jittered")
else:
    print("ANCHOR MISS — lock line differs:"); print([l for l in s.split(chr(10)) if '_lock()' in l][:1])
PY
bash -n tools/run_3arm.sh && echo "syntax ok"

      git -C "$c" worktree remove --force "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1; cl=$((cl+1)); }
  done < <(git -C "$c" worktree list 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | awk '{print $1}')
  git -C "$c" worktree prune >/dev/null 2>&1
done

content.text: Everything works manually — all caches and commits present, `worktree add` succeeds. So it's **pure concurrency**: 12 workers per instance racing one repo-cache, and failures spread across all 5 (8/3/6/3/4). The lock isn't the answer; the shared cache is. Giving each config its own cache clone removes the contention entirely:

input.command:
P=graph-benchmarks-504800
cat > /tmp/percache.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
cd ~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
# ROOT CAUSE: 12 workers (6 configs x 2 arms) call `git worktree add` on ONE repo-cache per
# instance. The per-cache lock serialises them, but git also takes its own index/ref locks inside
# the cache and the tail waiters lose. Manual add always succeeds; only concurrent adds fail.
# FIX: one cache CLONE per config. `--shared` reuses the object store, so this is near-instant and
# costs no real disk. Each config then has an uncontended cache.
IIDS=$(python3 -c "import json;print(' '.join(r['instance_id'] for r in json.load(open('tasks/sweep5.json'))['instances']))")
declare -A REPOOF
for iid in $IIDS; do
  REPOOF[$iid]=$(python3 -c "
import json
d=json.load(open('tasks/multilingual_300.json'))
rows=d if isinstance(d,list) else d.get('instances',[])
print([r['repo'] for r in rows if r['instance_id']=='$iid'][0].replace('/','_'))")
done
made=0
for CFG in SW_fable_high SW_fable_xhigh SW_fable_max SW_opus_high SW_opus_xhigh SW_opus_max; do
  mkdir -p "repo-cache-$CFG"
  for iid in $IIDS; do
    r=${REPOOF[$iid]}
    src="repo-cache/$r"; dst="repo-cache-$CFG/$r"
    [ -d "$dst" ] && continue
    [ -d "$src" ] || { echo "  MISSING src $src"; continue; }
    git clone --shared --no-checkout --quiet "$src" "$dst" 2>/dev/null && made=$((made+1)) || echo "  clone failed $dst"
  done
done
echo "per-config cache clones made: $made"
du -sh repo-cache-SW_* 2>/dev/null | head -3
EOF

This audit is decisive, and it changes the plan. **You don't have 7 arms — you have 4**, and two of them are currently broken:

| tool | verdict | why |
|---|---|---|
| **letta** | ❌ NO | agent *framework* — owns the agent loop, can't be an arm in a harness that drives Claude Code |
| **mem0** | ❌ NO | conversational memory; stores natural-language facts, not a code index |
| **cognee** | ❌ NO | most SearchTypes require an LLM — that's a second model in the arm, a confound and a cost |
| **supermemory** | ⚠️ MARGINAL | verdict: "do not run as a rep30 arm" |
| **cmm + graphify** | ✅ YES | real code locators — **but both currently broken** |

**Two blockers, both found by reproducing the harness's own skip path:**

1. **The cmm arm is dead — 30/30 would SKIP.** `devenv/cmm/codebase-memory-mcp` → a symlink whose target `bin.js` was deleted by macOS tmp cleanup. The real 260 MB binary survived elsewhere. This is the *same* failure `run_3arm.sh:77-79` already documents ("30/30 on a haiku cell") — the earlier fix moved the default *path* out of `/tmp` but left the *target* in it.

2. **graphify's 21/30 was a harness bug, not the tool.** 8 of 9 misses were `fatal: '<out>/.src' already exists` → stale dir → 0-node graph → builder correctly rejected it. Today's builder added the pre-clear; the audit rebuilt to **29/30**.

**And it measured retrieval 3-way on rep30** (identical query per instance, gold = non-doc files of the gold patch):

```
EG        gold found 19/30 (63%)   rank1 1   rank<=3 8   payload 3521 B
GRAPHIFY  gold found 17/30 (57%)   rank1 3   rank<=3 8
```

**Three fairness defects that must be settled before the cell** — this is your "settings = 0 or 1" question:
- **F1**: eg and cmm have `SEARCH_ONLY`/`EG_VERIFY` prompt branches; **graphify has none**. Any cell with those set hands graphify a different prompt. → must run `SEARCH_ONLY=0`, `EG_VERIFY=0`.
- **F1b**: cmm's SEARCH_ONLY block is commented "IDENTICAL wording to the eg note" and structurally isn't — the strings coincide only while other knobs are off, and nothing asserts it.
- **F2**: knob plumbing is asymmetric (eg bakes 26 env vars, graphify 11, cmm 3), and the guard at `run_3arm.sh:966-967` **reads the wrong variable** — it can pass while the arms genuinely differ.

So the honest run is **4 arms × 30 = 120 sessions**, not 200+, and it needs the cmm binary repointed and ruff decided (recommend excluding it symmetrically — 1/30 of power, zero interpretation risk) before launch. Fixing the blockers now:

content.text:
**Found it — and it's a harness bug, not cmm.** cmm works perfectly:

```json
{"project":"tmp-cmmp2","nodes":5225,"edges":24943,"status":"indexed"}
```

But the harness pipes through `grep -v 'mem.init\|deprecated'`, and cmm now also emits `level=info msg=index.supervisor.reap outcome=clean...` — which isn't filtered, so `json.load` chokes on it, `project` comes back empty, and **every cmm session SKIPs**. A log line the vendor added silently killed the whole arm.

Fixing it to select the JSON line rather than blacklisting known noise:

input.command:
P=graph-benchmarks-504800
cat > /tmp/cmmfix.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
cd ~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
python3 - <<'PY'
p='tools/run_3arm.sh'; s=open(p).read()
old = """  proj=$("$CMM" cli index_repository --repo-path "$wt" --mode "$CMM_INDEX_MODE" 2>"$out/cmm_index.err" | grep -v 'mem.init\\|deprecated' | "$PY" -c "import json,sys
try:print(json.load(sys.stdin)['project'])
except:print('')")"""
new = """  # LOG-LINE FILTER (fixed 2026-08-07). This blacklisted two known noise lines
  # (`mem.init`, `deprecated`). cmm 0.9.0 also emits `level=info msg=index.supervisor.reap ...`,
  # which sailed through, so json.load() got a log line prepended to the JSON, raised, and `proj`
  # came back empty -- every cmm session then took the SKIP path with a misleading
  # "index failed" message while the index had in fact succeeded (verified: nodes=5225,
  # edges=24943, status=indexed). Select the JSON line instead of enumerating noise, so a future
  # vendor log line cannot silently kill the arm again.
  proj=$("$CMM" cli index_repository --repo-path "$wt" --mode "$CMM_INDEX_MODE" 2>"$out/cmm_index.err" | grep '^[[:space:]]*{' | tail -1 | "$PY" -c "import json,sys
try:print(json.load(sys.stdin)['project'])
except:print('')")"""
assert old in s, "anchor missing"
open(p,'w').write(s.replace(old,new)); print("cmm index parse fixed")
PY
bash -n tools/run_3arm.sh && echo "syntax ok"
echo "=== verify the fixed pipeline against real cmm output ==="
CMMBIN=$HOME/cmm-prefix/node_modules/codebase-memory-mcp/bin/codebase-memory-mcp
wt=/tmp/cmmp3; rm -rf $wt

import json;d=json.load(open('tasks/multilingual_300.json'));r=d if isinstance(d,list) else d.get('instances',[])
print([x['base_commit'] for x in r if x['instance_id']=='google__gson-2158'][0])")
git -C repo-cache/google_gson worktree add --force --detach $wt $cm >/dev/null 2>&1
proj=$(timeout 600 $CMMBIN cli index_repository --repo-path "$wt" --mode full 2>/dev/null | grep '^[[:space:]]*{' | tail -1 | python3 -c "
import json,sys
try: print(json.load(sys.stdin)['project'])
except Exception: print('')")

random.seed(50)
bylang = collections.defaultdict(list)
for r in ml: bylang[r.get("language","?")].append(r)
tot = sum(len(v) for v in bylang.values())
quota = {k: max(1, round(40 * len(v) / tot)) for k, v in bylang.items()}
# trim/pad to exactly 40
while sum(quota.values()) > 40:
    k = max(quota, key=lambda k: quota[k]); quota[k] -= 1
while sum(quota.values()) < 40:

sel = []

input.command:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=$HOME/gfyvenv/bin:$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin:$HOME/.local/bin
export GRAPHIFY=$HOME/gfyvenv/bin/graphify
cd ~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
export ENTIRE_GRAPH="$PWD/bin/entire-graph-linux"
# My earlier clone did: clone --bare X.bare; clone --shared X.bare X; rm -rf X.bare
# --shared points X at X.bare/objects via alternates, so deleting the bare repo left every
# object unreachable ("unable to normalize alternate object path"). Plain clone instead.
for repo in ansible/ansible internetarchive/openlibrary qutebrowser/qutebrowser; do
  cache="repo-cache/$(echo "$repo"|tr '/' '_')"
  rm -rf "$cache" "$cache.bare"
  echo "  cloning $repo (full) ..."
  git clone --quiet "https://github.com/$repo.git" "$cache" 2>&1 | tail -2
  echo "    $(git -C "$cache" rev-list --count HEAD 2>/dev/null||echo 0) commits, $(du -sh "$cache" 2>/dev/null|cut -f1)"
done
echo "=== verify every rep50 python commit resolves ==="

**The 4-arm rep50 cell is running — 196 sessions, 107 live, and critically: 0 `wt fail`, 0 cmm skips, 0 graphify skips.** The per-arm cache clones fixed the contention completely, and the cmm arm is genuinely participating for the first time.


**One instance dropped symmetrically:** `astral-sh__ruff-15543` has no graphify graph, so it was removed from **all four arms** — dropping it from graphify alone would have flattered that arm by deleting its worst case. 50 → 49.

## What this run is, that no previous one was

Everything is now consistent end-to-end. VM synced to merged main (`4a2ea826`), and all six fixes verified present on the running harness:

| fix | why it mattered |
|---|---|
| scoped reap | was killing the sibling arm — ~9–10% of all sessions died silently |
| cmm json filter | the cmm arm SKIPped in **every prior cell** while reporting "index failed" |
| MCP arm gate | the Gemini baseline was being handed the graph |
| framing conditional | the prompt announced a payload and shipped none, 58/58 sessions |
| VERTEX export | `${VAR:+A=B}` killed 8/8 sessions |
| REPO_CACHE_DIR | 24/60 `wt fail` → 0 |

**Task mix:** 39 language-stratified + 10 Python from SWE-bench Pro — the first cell here with any Python at all, since SWE-bench Multilingual excludes it by design.

**The one caveat that limits what this can claim:** cmm and graphify were both broken in every previous cell, so there is no prior 4-arm number to compare against — this is a first measurement, not a replication. And at n=49 the MDE is still ~20 points, so I'll report bootstrap CIs and medians rather than a headline.

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, decide whether the loop continues.** If the task needs another iteration, call ScheduleWakeup with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks more frequent than the task needs are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
   If it doesn't need another iteration, stop instead (step 6) — re-arming is a per-turn choice, not a default.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then make the same decision. If the loop should continue, call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 (the Monitor remains the wake signal; the new wakeup is only the fallback heartbeat). If the event means the work is finished, stop (step 6).
6. **To stop the loop** — the task is complete, further iterations can't make progress, or the user asked you to stop — call ScheduleWakeup with `stop: true` (no other fields) and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context). Stopping is the loop's normal ending — the user can restart it anytime with /loop. Before you stop, send a one-line outcome via PushNotification — the user may be away and waiting to hear it's done. Skip this if you're stopping because the user just told you to; they're already here.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/vxproxy2.py <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Vertex model-pinning proxy, hardened for concurrent benchmark load.

gemini-cli's bundled model table has no gemini-3.6-flash, so `-m gemini-3.6-flash` silently falls
back to 3.5. REST confirms 3.6 IS available. This rewrites the model segment of the URL path so the
CLI's request is served by the intended model. Arm-agnostic -- same endpoint for every arm.

v2 CHANGES, after v1 stopped accepting under ~28 concurrent sessions while its PROCESS stayed
alive (0 sockets on :8109, "fetch failed sending request" in every session, silent for ~40 runs):
  * raise RLIMIT_NOFILE (v1 died against a 1024 fd cap)
  * never let one connection kill the accept loop -- handle_error is swallowed, and the serve
    loop is wrapped so a transient accept() error retries instead of terminating
  * bound the thread pool instead of one unbounded thread per request
  * Connection: close on both legs so sockets are not held open by keepalive
  * a heartbeat line every 60s, so a dead listener is visible in the log instead of silent
"""
import os, sys, re, time, threading, socket, resource
import http.server, socketserver, urllib.request, urllib.error

UPSTREAM = "https://aiplatform.googleapis.com"
FROM = os.environ.get("PIN_FROM", "gemini-3.5-flash")
TO   = os.environ.get("PIN_TO",   "gemini-3.6-flash")
PORT = int(os.environ.get("PIN_PORT", "8109"))
LOG  = os.environ.get("PIN_LOG", "/tmp/vxproxy.log")

try:
    soft, hard = resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)
    resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (min(65535, hard), hard))
    print("fd limit %d -> %d" % (soft, resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)[0]), flush=True)
except Exception as e:
    print("fd limit raise failed: %s" % e, flush=True)

_rw = [0]
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"
    timeout = 600
    def log_message(self, *a): pass
    def handle_error(self, *a): pass          # one bad peer must not take down the server
    def _relay(self, method):
        path = self.path
        new = re.sub(r"(/models/)" + re.escape(FROM) + r"(?=[:/?]|$)", r"\g<1>" + TO, path)
        if new != path:
            _rw[0] += 1
            try:
                with open(LOG, "a") as f: f.write("REWRITE %s -> %s\n" % (FROM, TO))
            except Exception: pass
        body = None
        n = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
        if n:
            try: body = self.rfile.read(int(n))
            except Exception: return
        req = urllib.request.Request(UPSTREAM + new, data=body, method=method)
        for k, v in self.headers.items():
            if k.lower() not in ("host", "content-length", "accept-encoding", "connection"):
                req.add_header(k, v)
        req.add_header("Connection", "close")
        try:
            r = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=900); status, hdrs = r.status, r.headers
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            r, status, hdrs = e, e.code, e.headers
        except Exception as e:
            try:
                self.send_response(502); self.send_header("Connection","close"); self.end_headers()
                self.wfile.write(str(e).encode())
            except Exception: pass
            return
        try:
            self.send_response(status)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", hdrs.get("Content-Type", "application/json"))
            self.send_header("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked")
            self.send_header("Connection", "close")
            self.end_headers()
            while True:
                chunk = r.read(8192)
                if not chunk: break
                self.wfile.write(b"%X\r\n" % len(chunk) + chunk + b"\r\n"); self.wfile.flush()
            self.wfile.write(b"0\r\n\r\n")
        except Exception:
            pass
        finally:
            try: r.close()
            except Exception: pass
    def do_POST(self): self._relay("POST")
    def do_GET(self):  self._relay("GET")

class T(socketserver.ThreadingTCPServer):
    allow_reuse_address = True
    daemon_threads = True
    request_queue_size = 256
    def handle_error(self, request, client_address): pass

def heartbeat(srv):
    while True:
        time.sleep(60)
        try:
            s = socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", PORT), timeout=5); s.close()
            print("%s alive rewrites=%d" % (time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), _rw[0]), flush=True)
        except Exception as e:
            print("%s LISTENER DEAD: %s" % (time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"), e), flush=True)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    srv = T(("127.0.0.1", PORT), H)
    threading.Thread(target=heartbeat, args=(srv,), daemon=True).start()
    print("pinning %s -> %s on :%d" % (FROM, TO, PORT), flush=True)
    while True:
        try:
            srv.serve_forever(poll_interval=0.2)
        except Exception as e:                 # a transient accept() error must not end the server
            print("serve_forever raised %s -- continuing" % e, flush=True)
            time.sleep(0.5)

Found the real bug, and it's my fix that's incomplete.

**Zero-byte outputs across all arms** (baseline 8, eg 8, cmm 16, graphify 22 = 54 sessions), no stderr, and the run log shows a session ending `patch=0L cost=$?` immediately followed by a *new* `claude (opus)…` for the same instance.

The supervisor relaunches any instance without a valid result every 90s. A session that's still running 90s later gets relaunched — and the new worker's `_reap_leftovers` matches `checkouts/$TAG/$arm/$iid`, which is **the incumbent's own path**, and kills it. I scoped the pattern to stop the *cross-arm* kill but left the reap running **before** the lock, so it now self-kills within the arm. The earlier review told me to move it after the lock and I only did half the fix.

Fixing both — and adding the speed tracking you asked for:

**Root cause found, with direct evidence: 2 workers per `(arm, iid)`** — `eg prometheus-9248`, `eg lombok-3326`, and more.

The single-run lock can't stop it. `run_3arm.sh` writes `.running` at line ~176, but **provisioning and worktree setup happen before that** and take 60–120s. My supervisor re-scans every 90s, sees the instance still has no valid result, and launches a second worker inside that window — before the first one has taken the lock.

The reap fix was treating a symptom. Fixing the actual cause — the supervisor must track what it has already launched:

input.command:
cat > /tmp/sv50b.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=$HOME/gfyvenv/bin:$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin:$HOME/.local/bin
export GRAPHIFY=$HOME/gfyvenv/bin/graphify
cd ~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
export ENTIRE_GRAPH="$PWD/bin/entire-graph-linux"
export CMM_BIN="$HOME/cmm-prefix/node_modules/codebase-memory-mcp/bin/codebase-memory-mcp"
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN="$AT"; unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
TARGET=${TARGET:-60}

# WHY THIS TRACKS IN-FLIGHT WORK ITSELF:
# run_3arm.sh writes its single-run lock ($out/.running) only AFTER provisioning + worktree setup,
# which takes 60-120s. A supervisor that re-scans every 90s therefore relaunches an instance that
# is already running but has not yet taken the lock. Measured: 2 workers on the same (arm,iid) for
# many instances, 51 zero-byte cc_out.json, and throughput collapsing to 6 sess/h as the duplicates
# killed each other. The lock cannot fix this -- the launcher must not double-launch in the first
# place. We keep our own in-flight set keyed on "arm/iid" and only reap it when the pid exits.

declare -A INFLIGHT   # "arm<TAB>iid" -> pid
count_live() { local n; n=$(ps -A -o command= | grep -c "[c]laude -p" || true); echo "${n:-0}"; }

for round in $(seq 1 600); do
  # drop finished pids from the in-flight set
  for k in "${!INFLIGHT[@]}"; do
    kill -0 "${INFLIGHT[$k]}" 2>/dev/null || unset 'INFLIGHT[$k]'
  done

  python3 - <<'PY' > /tmp/w50.tsv
import os,json
d=json.load(open('tasks/rep50_run.json'))['instances']
def ok(a,i):
    p="results/REP50_r1_%s/%s/%s"%(a,a,i); f,q=p+'/cc_out.json',p+'/patch.diff'
    if not(os.path.isfile(f) and os.path.getsize(f)>0): return False
    try: j=json.load(open(f))
    except Exception: return False
    if j.get('api_error_status') or j.get('subtype')!='success': return False
    return os.path.isfile(q) and os.path.getsize(q)>0
for a in ('baseline','eg','cmm','graphify'):
    for r in d:
        if not ok(a,r['instance_id']): print(a+"\t"+r['instance_id'])
PY
  left=$(wc -l < /tmp/w50.tsv)
  running=${#INFLIGHT[@]}
  if [ "$left" -eq 0 ]; then echo "$(date +%H:%M) REP50 COMPLETE"; break; fi
  echo "$(date +%H:%M) round=$round remaining=$left inflight=$running live=$(count_live)"

  slots=$(( TARGET - running ))
  if [ "$slots" -gt 0 ]; then
    launched=0
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r arm iid; do
      [ "$launched" -ge "$slots" ] && break
      key="$arm	$iid"
      [ -n "${INFLIGHT[$key]:-}" ] && continue          # already running -- never double-launch
      (
        set -a
        source <(grep -E '^export (EG_|O35_|PUB|GQ_|CC_MAX|CMM_)' tools/run_REP50.sh | sed 's/^export //')
        set +a
        export O35_ARGV_PARITY=1 O35_FORCE=0 EG_LEGACY_FRAMING=0 SEARCH_ONLY=0 EG_VERIFY=0
        export CC_MODEL=opus CC_EFFORT=max CC_MAX_TURNS=120
        export CMM_BIN="$CMM_BIN"
        export REPO_CACHE_DIR="$PWD/repo-cache-REP50-$arm"
        export RESULTS_TAG="REP50_r1_${arm}" TASKS_FILE="$PWD/tasks/rep50_run.json"
        bash tools/run_3arm.sh "$arm" "$iid" > "logs/sv50_${arm}_${iid:0:36}.log" 2>&1
      ) &
      INFLIGHT[$key]=$!
      launched=$((launched+1))
      sleep 0.2
    done < /tmp/w50.tsv
    [ "$launched" -gt 0 ] && echo "           launched $launched new"
  fi
  sleep 60
done
SCRIPT

**That's it — and it's a definition mismatch, not a race.**

```
[gson-2024/cmm] ALREADY COMPLETE (cc_out.json non-empty) -- skipping; set O35_FORCE=1 to re-run
```

`run_3arm`'s idempotence guard skips on **`cc_out.json` non-empty**. My supervisor's "done" test is stricter: `subtype==success` AND `patch>0` AND no API error. So any session that wrote a non-empty-but-invalid `cc_out.json` is **"not done" to the supervisor and "already done" to the harness** — relaunched every round, exiting instantly, forever. That's the churn, the flat `remaining=138`, and the collapsed throughput. Nothing to do with duplicates or the reap.

Fixing it at the source — purge the invalid artifact so the harness agrees:

# cc_out.json is merely NON-EMPTY, while "done" here means subtype==success AND patch>0 AND no
# api_error. A session that wrote a non-empty but INVALID cc_out.json was therefore "not done" to
# this supervisor and "ALREADY COMPLETE" to the harness -- relaunched every round, exiting in
# under a second, forever. Measured: 60 launches/round with inflight collapsing to 0, remaining
# frozen at 138, throughput 66 -> 6 sess/h. Delete the invalid artifact so both agree.
purged=0

        for f in ("cc_out.json","patch.diff"):
            fp=p+"/"+f
            if os.path.isfile(fp):
                try: os.remove(fp); purged+=1
                except Exception: pass
        print(a+"\\t"+i)
import sys
if purged: print("purged %d stale artifacts"%purged, file=sys.stderr)

# a claude session whose parent chain no longer contains run_3arm cannot have its patch collected
orph=0
for pid in $(pgrep -f "claude -p" 2>/dev/null); do
  ppid=$(ps -o ppid= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d " ")
  if [ -z "$ppid" ] || [ "$ppid" = "1" ]; then kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; orph=$((orph+1)); continue; fi
  # walk up: if no run_3arm ancestor, it is orphaned

    case "$c" in *run_3arm*) found=1; break;; esac
    cur=$(ps -o ppid= -p "$cur" 2>/dev/null | tr -d " "); [ -z "$cur" ] && break; [ "$cur" = "1" ] && break
  done
  [ "$found" -eq 0 ] && { kill -9 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; orph=$((orph+1)); }
done

**My duplicate detector was wrong the whole time.** The two processes are **parent and child** — pid `3104868`'s parent is pid `3090465`, which is the real worker. `top-level: 36, nested: 36` — exactly one genuine worker per instance, plus its own forked subshell (the timeout watchdog, which keeps the parent's argv so `ps` shows it twice).

The churn in the last half hour was substantially self-inflicted.

cat > /tmp/speed2.py <<'PYEOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""rep50 throughput + PER-ARM session speed.

Two different questions, both useful:
  1. throughput  -- how fast is the CELL finishing (sessions/hour, ETA)
  2. session speed -- how long does one session TAKE, per arm, and is a tool arm faster than the
     no-tool baseline on the SAME instances (paired, which is the only fair comparison)
"""
import os, json, time, statistics
os.chdir(os.path.expanduser("~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench"))
ARMS = ("baseline", "eg", "cmm", "graphify")
ids = [r["instance_id"] for r in json.load(open("tasks/rep50_run.json"))["instances"]]
now = time.time()

def rec(a, i):
    p = f"results/REP50_r1_{a}/{a}/{i}"; f, q = p+"/cc_out.json", p+"/patch.diff"
    if not (os.path.isfile(f) and os.path.getsize(f) > 0): return None
    try: j = json.load(open(f))
    except Exception: return None
    if j.get("api_error_status") or j.get("subtype") != "success": return None
    if not (os.path.isfile(q) and os.path.getsize(q) > 0): return None
    dur = (j.get("duration_ms") or 0) / 1000.0
    if dur <= 0: dur = None
    return dict(mtime=os.path.getmtime(f), dur=dur, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0)

data = {a: {i: rec(a, i) for i in ids} for a in ARMS}
done = {a: sum(1 for i in ids if data[a][i]) for a in ARMS}
total_done = sum(done.values()); total = len(ids)*len(ARMS); remaining = total - total_done
mt = [data[a][i]["mtime"] for a in ARMS for i in ids if data[a][i]]
cost = sum(data[a][i]["usd"] for a in ARMS for i in ids if data[a][i])

print(f"  progress: {total_done}/{total} ({100*total_done/total:.0f}%)   remaining {remaining}")
print("  per arm:  " + "  ".join(f"{a}={done[a]}/{len(ids)}" for a in ARMS))
for win, lbl in ((600,"10m"), (1800,"30m"), (3600,"60m")):
    n = sum(1 for m in mt if now-m < win); rate = n/(win/3600)
    eta = remaining/rate if rate else float("inf")
    print(f"  rate {lbl}: {n:3} done -> {rate:5.1f} sess/h   ETA {('%5.1fh'%eta) if eta!=float('inf') else '  n/a'}")

print("\n  SESSION SPEED (per arm)")
print(f"    {'arm':10} {'n':>3}  {'median':>8} {'mean':>8}  {'turns':>6}   vs baseline (paired)")
base = data["baseline"]
for a in ARMS:
    d = [data[a][i]["dur"] for i in ids if data[a][i] and data[a][i]["dur"]]
    t = [data[a][i]["turns"] for i in ids if data[a][i]]
    if not d: print(f"    {a:10} {0:>3}  {'-':>8} {'-':>8}"); continue
    med, mean = statistics.median(d)/60, statistics.mean(d)/60
    tm = statistics.mean(t) if t else 0
    if a == "baseline":
        print(f"    {a:10} {len(d):>3}  {med:7.1f}m {mean:7.1f}m  {tm:6.1f}   (reference)")
    else:
        pair = [(data[a][i]["dur"], base[i]["dur"]) for i in ids
                if data[a][i] and base[i] and data[a][i]["dur"] and base[i]["dur"]]
        if pair:
            rel = statistics.median([(x/y-1)*100 for x, y in pair])
            faster = "FASTER" if rel < 0 else "slower"
            print(f"    {a:10} {len(d):>3}  {med:7.1f}m {mean:7.1f}m  {tm:6.1f}   {rel:+6.1f}% {faster}  (n={len(pair)} paired)")
        else:
            print(f"    {a:10} {len(d):>3}  {med:7.1f}m {mean:7.1f}m  {tm:6.1f}   (no paired yet)")
if mt:
    span = (max(mt)-min(mt))/3600
    if span > 0: print(f"\n  overall {len(mt)} done over {span:.1f}h -> {len(mt)/span:.1f} sess/h")
    print(f"  spend ${cost:.2f}   projected ${cost*total/max(1,total_done):.2f}")

content.text:
Speed tracking is live, and it's already more informative than the token numbers at this n:

```
arm          n    median     mean   turns   vs baseline (paired)
baseline    22     11.6m    11.6m    50.7   (reference)
eg          16     10.0m    11.3m    45.2     -5.4% FASTER  (n=7)
cmm         10     11.9m    12.4m    38.5    +84.4% slower  (n=4)
graphify    11     20.0m    17.9m    51.2   +121.4% slower  (n=5)
```

It reports both **throughput** (how fast the cell finishes) and **session speed** (how long one session takes), the latter paired on identical instances — the only fair way to compare arms.

**What stands out:**

- **eg is 5.4% faster** and uses **45.2 turns vs baseline's 50.7** — consistent with the whole campaign's mechanism, where the tool pays by shortening the session.
- **cmm uses the fewest turns (38.5) yet runs 84% slower.** Fewer turns but more wall-clock means time is going somewhere other than the model — almost certainly its `index_repository` step, which builds a SQLite symbol graph *per session*. That's an indexing cost the other arms don't pay, and it's worth separating from model time before anyone reads it as "cmm is slow."
- **graphify is 2.2× slower at the same turn count** (51.2 vs 50.7) — same amount of model work, twice the wall clock.

Caveat as always: n=4–7 paired. Wall-clock is also noisier than turns because it includes provisioning and machine load, so I'd trust the **turns** column sooner than the minutes.

I'll include this block in every update from now on. Throughput is still the weak spot — 0 done in 10 min, though the oldest session is only ~9 min old after the restart, and the 60-min window (18/h) is the honest current read.

    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'skeptics try to refute the best-model claim' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'one honest answer with its caveats' },
  ],
}

const SSH = `Use: perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 240 gcloud compute ssh <VM> --project=graph-benchmarks-504800 --zone=us-east1-b --tunnel-through-iap --quiet --command='<cmd>'
VMs: graphbench-b (rep30 + the model x effort sweep), graphbench-c (rep50). Suite dir on each: ~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench
gcloud auth expires ~hourly; if ssh returns code 255, retry ONCE then report AUTH_FAIL and return what you have.
Results live under results/<TAG>/<arm>/<instance>/ with cc_out.json (has usage + total_cost_usd + subtype + num_turns), patch.diff, prompt.txt.
OUTPUT RULES: caveman-ultra compressed. Numbers + paths only. No prose, no preamble, no restating the task. Use rtk for git/file ops where it applies.`

const RECOVER = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['found', 'configs', 'notes'],
  properties: {
    found: { type: 'boolean' },
    configs: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['tag', 'model', 'effort', 'n_gated', 'sum_eg_tokens', 'sum_base_tokens', 'sum_eg_usd', 'sum_base_usd'],
        properties: {
          tag: { type: 'string' },
          model: { type: 'string' },
          effort: { type: 'string' },
          n_gated: { type: 'integer' },
          sum_eg_tokens: { type: 'number' },
          sum_base_tokens: { type: 'number' },
          sum_eg_usd: { type: 'number' },
          sum_base_usd: { type: 'number' },
          instances: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
        },
      },
    },
    notes: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

phase('Recover')

const [raw, sign, prompts, power] = await parallel([
  () => agent(`${SSH}

TASK: Locate the "model x effort sweep" cells (~5 instances each, configs across Opus and Fable at effort high / xhigh / max). Likely tags contain SWEEP/OPUSMAX/OPUSHIGH/OPUSXHIGH/FABLEMAX/FABLEXHIGH/FABLEHIGH. Check graphbench-b first, then graphbench-c.

For EACH config found, for EACH instance, read results/<TAG>/eg/<iid>/cc_out.json and results/<TAG>/baseline/<iid>/cc_out.json.
GATE an instance only if BOTH arms have subtype=="success", no api_error_status/is_error, AND non-empty patch.diff. Drop failures as a PAIR (both arms).
Sum over gated instances only: total tokens (cache_read + cache_creation + input + output) and total_cost_usd, per arm.
Report exact tags and exact directory paths so another agent can re-read them.`, { label: 'recover:raw', phase: 'Recover', schema: RECOVER }),

  () => agent(`${SSH}

TASK: Determine the SIGN CONVENTION used by the sweep scorer, empirically. Do NOT trust any doc.
1. Find the scorer script that produced the sweep table (look for ~/sc*.py, ~/*sweep*, tools/score*, on graphbench-b and -c).
2. Read the line that computes the TOKEN percentage. Report the literal expression.
3. Independently compute, for ONE config, Sum(eg tokens) and Sum(baseline tokens) from raw cc_out.json, and state whether the scorer's printed number for that config is (base-eg)/base [positive = eg SAVES] or (eg-base)/base [positive = eg COSTS MORE].
Return: the literal formula, the config you checked, both raw sums, and an unambiguous one-line verdict of the form "positive means eg SAVES" or "positive means eg COSTS MORE".`, { label: 'recover:sign', phase: 'Recover' }),

  () => agent(`${SSH}

TASK: Establish whether the model x effort sweep ran with the DEFECTIVE prompt or the FIXED one.
Background: a known bug made the eg prompt ANNOUNCE a graph payload while shipping none, suppressing tool use in 58/58 sessions and inflating results. The fix made the framing conditional on a payload actually being present.
For each sweep config: read results/<TAG>/eg/<iid>/prompt.txt and check (a) whether it announces a payload, (b) whether a payload is actually present in the prompt.
Also count actual graph usage per config: results/<TAG>/eg/<iid>/gq_calls.log (non-empty = tool was called). Report calls-used / total per config.
CRITICAL fairness check: also confirm results/<TAG>/baseline/<iid>/ has NO gq_calls.log content and NO graph instructions, and diff eg vs baseline prompt.txt reporting EVERY differing line.
Return per config: defective|fixed, graph-used count, and the full list of prompt lines that differ between arms.`, { label: 'recover:prompt', phase: 'Recover' }),

  () => agent(`${SSH}

TASK: Compute statistical power and stability for the sweep.
For each sweep config: n gated pairs, per-instance paired token delta, bootstrap 95% CI on the total (Sigma eg / Sigma base), and the MEDIAN paired delta alongside the total.
Then answer three questions with numbers:
1. Do any two configs' CIs fail to overlap? List every pair that separates.
2. Is the per-config ranking driven by one instance? For each config report the single instance contributing the largest share of the total, and recompute the total with it removed.
3. Are the SAME instances present in every config? List instances present in all configs vs those only in some. Cross-config comparison is only valid on the common set - report the common-set-only ranking too.`, { label: 'recover:power', phase: 'Recover' }),
])

log('recovered sweep data; launching skeptics')

phase('Verify')

const VERDICT = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['refuted', 'reason', 'confidence'],
  properties: {
    refuted: { type: 'boolean' },
    reason: { type: 'string' },
    confidence: { type: 'string', enum: ['low', 'medium', 'high'] },
  },
}

const EVIDENCE = `RECOVERED DATA:
--- raw sums ---
${JSON.stringify(raw)}
--- sign convention ---
${sign}
--- prompt integrity ---
${prompts}
--- power / stability ---
${power}`

const LENSES = [
  { k: 'power', q: 'The claim rests on n=4-5 per config against a measured MDE of ~25-30 points on this benchmark. Same-instance spread across repeated cells is 45pt median with a tail to 335pt. Is ANY ranking among these configs distinguishable from noise? Default to refuted unless CIs actually separate.' },
  { k: 'fairness', q: 'Did the sweep run on the defective prompt that suppressed tool use? If the eg arm never called the graph, the cell measures prompt text, not the model. Also check for arm-asymmetric instructions. Default to refuted if the prompt was defective or asymmetric.' },
  { k: 'composition', q: 'Are the configs compared on the SAME instance set? If config A ran easy instances and config B hard ones, the ranking is instance composition, not model. Also check whether one instance carries a config. Default to refuted if the common set is not identical.' },
  { k: 'construct', q: 'Does "best model" even mean what the table reports? The table measures the eg-vs-baseline DELTA per model, not the model quality. A model can post the biggest delta while being the worst coder, and cost in USD differs from tokens by 20-50x on output. State plainly what the metric actually ranks. Default to refuted if the metric does not answer "which model was best".' },
]

const verdicts = await parallel(LENSES.map(l => () =>
  agent(`You are a skeptic. Try to REFUTE this claim:

CLAIM: "On the 5-instance model x effort sweep, opus max was the best model (TOKEN +48.67%), followed by opus high +27.83% and fable max +27.59%; fable high was worst at -14.39%."

YOUR LENS: ${l.q}

${EVIDENCE}

Reach a verdict. Default to refuted=true if you cannot independently establish the claim from the evidence above. Be specific with numbers.
OUTPUT: caveman-ultra compressed. No preamble.`, { label: `refute:${l.k}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT })
))

phase('Synthesize')

const kills = LENSES.map((l, i) => ({ lens: l.k, v: verdicts[i] })).filter(x => x.v && x.v.refuted)

const answer = await agent(`Write the final answer to the user's question: "what was the best model on the 5 runs?"

${EVIDENCE}

--- skeptic verdicts ---
${JSON.stringify(LENSES.map((l, i) => ({ lens: l.k, verdict: verdicts[i] })))}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Lead with the direct answer: which config topped the table, with its number and the CORRECT sign interpretation (state explicitly whether positive means saves or costs).
- Then state plainly whether that ranking is real or not, given n and the skeptics.
- Give the full 6-row table (config, n, TOKEN, delta turns) with the sign convention labelled in the header.
- If the sweep ran the defective prompt, say so as a headline caveat.
- Distinguish "best model to run the benchmark on" from "model where the graph tool helps most" if the metric only supports the latter.
- Be concise: table + at most 6 sentences. No hedging filler, no restating the question.
OUTPUT: markdown, ready to paste.`, { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize' })

return { answer, kills: kills.map(k => k.lens), raw, sign, prompts, power }

**Opus at max effort** topped that sweep — but the table does not support calling it "the best model," and I'd treat the ranking as unreadable.

Recorded sweep (positive = eg saves vs its own no-tool baseline):

| config | n | TOKEN | Δturns |
|---|---|---|---|
| **opus max** | 4 | **+48.67%** | −22.25 |
| opus high | 4 | +27.83% | −2.00 |
| fable max | 4 | +27.59% | −8.00 |
| fable xhigh | 4 | +15.30% | −2.00 |
| opus xhigh | 4 | −10.31% | +0.25 |
| fable high | 5 | −14.39% | +0.20 |

Three reasons not to bank this:

**n=4–5 against a ~25–30pt MDE.** Every gap in that table is inside the noise floor; same-instance spread on this benchmark runs 45pt median. You're watching the rep50 cell do exactly this live right now — eg has decayed +36.5 → +20.5 across five readings as n went 9 → 19.

**It ranks the wrong thing.** Each row is the eg-vs-baseline *delta* for that config, not model quality. Opus max posting the largest delta means the graph helped it most, which is partly just that its baseline flailed hardest — note it also cut 22 turns, and the one law that has survived everything here is that tokens track messages (elasticity 1.682, r=0.957). Every config that shortened the session "won"; every one that lengthened it "lost."

**Prompt provenance is unresolved.** The neighbouring rep30 cells at these same configs — FABLEMAX +22.17%, OPUSHIGH +13.81% — are both flagged defective-prompt, and their fixed-prompt reruns collapsed to +2.21% and −4.65%. If the sweep shares that prompt, these numbers measure the prompt, not the model.

I have a workflow running now that pulls the raw per-instance sums off the VMs, pins the sign convention from the scorer source rather than my notes, checks whether the sweep used the defective prompt, and tests whether the configs even share a common instance set. Four skeptics are set to refute the opus-max claim. I'll report what survives.

Give a benchmark status update: rep50 4-arm cell (baseline/eg/cmm/graphify) pair counts and token results per arm, plus Gemini 300 and any remaining rep30 cells. Flag any wt fails, cmm/graphify SKIPs, or arm-asymmetric problems. Keep it short — a table and anything that changed.

## Why Gemini stalled — found and restarted

It wasn't stalled, it was **dead for ~6.7 hours**. `gem300.sh` is a fire-and-forget ramp launcher, not a supervisor: it starts 16 shard drivers in four ramp stages and exits. Nothing watches them. The log froze at `[ramp 4/4]` at 16:31 UTC and never wrote again.

State when I found it: **supervisor 0, locks 0**, 8 straggler processes, and only **170/300 instances per arm** with any output. About 43% were never attempted. n=87 wasn't converging — it was frozen.

Relaunched just now: 4 drivers up, 22 sessions, ramping to 16. `run_3arm` skips completed instances, so it resumes rather than redoes.

One thing that caps it: **112 baseline / 113 eg sessions produced an empty patch**, plus 31 hard errors. Empty patch is the dominant gate-fail mode, so even at a full 300 attempted, expect ~150–170 pairs, not 300.

## How to actually find the best model

The table you're looking at cannot answer it, for a reason that isn't sample size:

**It measures the wrong quantity.** Each row is Δ(eg vs baseline) *within* that model — how much the graph tool helped. That's not model quality. Opus max tops it at +48.67% largely because its baseline flailed hardest (−22.25 turns, by far the biggest swing in the table). A model with a sloppy no-tool arm posts a big delta. That's a statement about the baseline, not the model.

**And the power is worse than it looks.** Comparing two configs is a difference-of-differences, so the variance roughly doubles — MDE goes from ~30pt paired to ~40pt at n=30. At n=4–5 it's north of 100pt. Every gap in those six rows is inside that.

The metric that answers "best model" is **$ per resolved instance**: run the *baseline* arm only (no tool, so nothing about the ranking depends on entire-graph), same instance set for every model, grade with the SWE-bench harness, then report resolve rate and cost.

**The cheap version is available right now at zero model spend.** We already hold baseline-arm sessions for Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku and Gemini across the existing cells, on overlapping instances. Grading those costs compute, not API calls, and yields resolve-rate-per-dollar per model on the common set immediately. That is the single highest-value thing left to run, and it needs no new cell.

Two caveats before starting it: run `reclaim.sh` first — the cmm cache filled the volume and killed dockerd during the last grading attempt — and note the standing "no grading until ≥35%" constraint in my notes is stale, since that 35% target was itself withdrawn as arithmetically unreachable.

Say the word and I'll start grading the existing baseline arms. The sweep-verification workflow is still running and will tell us whether those six rows were even run on a fair prompt.

Five things. We have three; **two are missing, and one of them is the whole blocker.**
