input.plan:
# entire-graph: the honest ceiling is ~+17%, and what to build to reach it

> **VERDICT: 35% is not reachable on a fair measurement.** Six independent estimates converge on
> **+15–21%**, the directly addressable waste is **+2.67–4.57%**, and the best fair cell ever
> measured is **+17.21%** (opus xhigh, n=26). The original +35.06% target was an arithmetic
> artifact and is retracted below. This plan targets **+17–21%** and says plainly what it cannot do.

| route | ceiling |
|---|---|
| directly addressable post-edit waste | **+2.67% to +4.57%** |
| expensive-baseline tercile (78% of mass) | +8.07% |
| fair symmetric ceiling (all post-edit pools) | +14.99% |
| perfect post-edit behaviour | +15.4% |
| **best fair cell measured** | **+17.21%** (n=26) |
| mechanism model, N≈6–8 calls removed | +18–21% |

**Why not 35%:** 97.7% of the loss is post-edit work the graph does not touch; eg's saving is
bounded by *baseline waste* (`corr(baseline tokens, eg delta) = +0.305`; cheap baselines
−27.76%), which the graph does not control.

## Context

rep50 finished at **eg +1.35%** (n=49, Opus max, median −4.16%, 24/49 wins). Goal: **35% token
savings** vs a no-tool baseline, fairly measured.

The loser-repair framing is the only one whose arithmetic reaches the target, and it is
**measured, not extrapolated**:

| scenario | suite |
|---|---|
| today | **+1.35%** |
| all 22 losers merely neutral (eg = base) | **+20.99%** |
| all 22 losers behaving like the winner group | **+35.06%** ← target |

**Neutralising is not enough.** 35% requires the losers to *win*, not merely stop losing.

## What the losses actually are (transcript decomposition, n=8 worst)

**97.7% of the loss is POST-EDIT.** ΔPre = +0.40M (2.3%); ΔPost = **+17.31M**.
Pre-edit calls 147 vs 134 (+10%); post-edit **370 vs 248 (+49%)**.
Split of the +17.71M: turn-count **10.95M (62%)**, context-density **6.79M (38%)**.

**The graph already does its job.** Localization was net-free, and *cheaper* in 3 of 8.

**Retrieval quality is ANTI-correlated with winning** — gold at rank 1: losers **6/8 (75%)**,
winners **2/5 (40%)**. `lombok-3674` (**+71.0%**) had a **0-byte payload**; `redis-11510`
(**+68.4%**) missed gold entirely. **Do not spend effort on ranking.**

**Mechanism: the agent gets the repo's native harness working and cannot stop.**

| instance | eg harness runs | base | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| valkey-790 | `./runtest`×11, `make`×6 | 7 / 2 | −127.4% |
| javaparser-4538 | `javac`×19 | 8 | −142.3% |
| bat-1892 | `cargo test`×7, `build`×6 | 1 | −79.8% |
| **redis-11510** | `./runtest`×**1**, stop | 10 | **+68.4%** |
| **laravel-48636** | `phpunit`×**1** | 15 | **+50.7%** |

`redis-11510` is the clean control: same repo, same tcl harness, opposite outcome. Each retry
drags in `sleep 120`, `pkill`, port juggling, and **tailing its own transcript** to recover
truncated Bash output. Winners' post-edit calls: 93 vs 196 (**−53%**).

Sub-split: **B1 "couldn't stop" 6/8 ≈ 15.9M**; **B2 "context density" 2/8 ≈ 2.2M**
(javaparser-4538 is the sole pre-edit-dominant case and is expected NOT to convert).

## Why conversion is possible (confounds checked, all pass)

**Same repo, opposite outcome — 7 repos on BOTH sides:** laravel (−59.4/−124.1 vs +50.7/+38.8),
lombok (−19.4 vs **+71.0**), tokio (−114.4 vs +32.5), fmt (−23.2 vs +62.1), prometheus,
qutebrowser, ansible. **8 of 10 languages appear on both sides** — not an ecosystem effect.
**Winners had HARDER baselines** (median 2.64M tok / 56 turns vs losers 2.01M / 42) — the
winner profile is not "easy instances".

The difference is behavioural, not intrinsic. That is what makes it fixable.

## FAIRNESS REVIEW — ashtom's objection, and why it lands

> *"That seems like cheating then? Why is baseline able to run the tests cheaper than eg is?"*

**Answer to the second question: it isn't.** Both arms run tests through the same Bash tool in
the same checkout with identical access (verified: only the eg `entire` shim differs on PATH).
The baseline is not cheaper per run — **eg simply runs the harness more often** (losers: eg
9–19× vs baseline 4–10×). That is an eg behavioural regression, not a baseline advantage.

**Answer to the first: partly yes, on scope.** `verify` is cheap because of an *output
contract*, not privileged access — `cli/verify.go:31` returns an **adjudicated verdict, never
raw output**, capped at **2,048 B** (`:41`). The baseline could pipe `pytest` through `head`;
it doesn't. That is a genuine tool capability. **But** shipping it means we stop measuring
"does the code graph save tokens" and start measuring "does a bundle of dev tools save tokens".

**Consequence for this plan: L1 is demoted from PRIMARY to optional, and must be labelled.**
If run, report it as *graph + verify* against *no tools*, and report the graph-only number
beside it. Do not let it become the headline for entire-graph.

## ⛔ THE +35.06% NUMBER IS AN ARTIFACT — retracted

**eg's saving is a function of BASELINE WASTE, not of graph quality.**

| baseline cost tercile | median baseline | eg TOKEN | eg median |
|---|---|---|---|
| cheap | 0.99M | **−27.76%** | −28.0% |
| mid | 2.48M | −2.99% | +6.2% |
| expensive | 5.13M | **+8.07%** | +8.9% |

`corr(baseline tokens, eg delta) = +0.305`; `corr(baseline turns, eg delta) = +0.284`.
Below-median baselines: **−14.64%**. Above-median (78% of token mass): **+5.87%**.

**Why this kills the arithmetic:** the winner group's eg/base ratio of 0.604 was achieved on
instances whose baselines spent **2.64M median / 56 turns**. Applying that ratio to a 0.99M
baseline is impossible — there is no waste there to capture. "Convert every loser to
winner-quality" is not merely hard, it is **arithmetically unavailable** for the ~half of
losers whose baselines are already efficient.

The ceiling is therefore set by *how much the no-tool baseline wastes*, which the graph does
not control. On the 78% of token mass where waste is greatest, eg captures **+5.87%**.

**Empirical ceiling, all fair cells at n≥25: `opus xhigh` +17.21% (n=26).** That is the largest
honest number this project has produced.

## HONEST CEILING — the two estimates disagree, and the lower one is better founded

- **Winner-ratio model (mine):** convert all 22 losers to the winner eg/base ratio → **+35.06%**.
  This is an *upper bound*: it assumes total conversion of every loser.
- **Mechanism model (architecture review):** removing N post-edit calls yields +2.8% at N=0,
  **+17.3% at N=8**, **+24.3% at N=12**. R2+R3+R4 together plausibly reach N≈6–8 → **+18–21%**.

The mechanism model is grounded in measured elasticity; mine assumes an outcome. **The honest
expected range is +18% to +25%, and 35% is the ceiling only under total conversion.** Say this
plainly rather than quoting +35.06%.

## The fix

### L1 — ~~expose the executing `verify` verb~~ **REMOVED** (ashtom's objection accepted)

Running the tests for the agent makes eg cheaper at work **both arms do identically** — the
baseline is not cheaper per run, eg simply runs the harness 9–19× vs 4–10×. It would book a
subsidy for an eg regression as a graph win, and it changes the claim from "the code graph
saves tokens" to "our bundle does dev work cheaply". **Dropped. Do not run it.**

### L1′ — fix the VERIFY *derivation* so the first invocation works (REPLACEMENT)

Same target (post-edit waste), fair by construction: deriving the correct test command from
build files **plus the graph** is code intelligence. It makes the graph's answer better rather
than making eg cheaper at shared work.

The waste is not legitimate re-testing. From the transcripts it is failing to get the harness
running: `sleep 90/120/150` polling, `pkill` ×4, `--baseport` juggling, tailing its own
transcript to recover truncated Bash output, hand-built `/tmp` rigs.

Three concrete defects:
1. **Wrong scope.** nushell (−141.2%): the manifest walk emitted `cargo test -p nu-cli` when the
   fix was in `nu-command`. **The graph knows which crate/package/module owns the symbol; the
   manifest walk cannot.** Use symbol→file→package to scope the command.
2. **No runnability check.** The only probe is `exec.LookPath` on the runner
   (`search_verify.go:1526`) — it confirms `pytest` is installed, never that the command runs.
   Add a collect-only probe (`pytest --collect-only`, `go test -run XXX -count=0`,
   `cargo test --no-run`) and drop to the next rung on failure.
3. **Coverage 8/33.** Most payloads carry no VERIFY line at all. Raise toward ~100% or this
   reaches only a quarter of Class B.

Fairness: the derived command is tool output computed from the repo, the same class as the
ranked hits. It ships no instruction and the baseline arm is untouched.

### L1-OLD — expose the executing `verify` verb (REMOVED — kept for the record)

**The capability already exists and was never wired up.** `internal/cli/verify.go:193` runs
`exec.CommandContext(ctx,"sh","-c",cmd)` + `CombinedOutput()` via `runVerifyCommands` (:158).
It has ecosystem-aware timeouts (`verifyCompiledCommand` :178 — cargo/go test/mvn/gradle/cmake/
ctest/make/bazel/dotnet/swift), **discards setup output** so install logs don't pollute test
parsing, returns exit code **separately** from error (a failing suite is normal), caps output via
`maxBytes`, and never mutates the tree.

But `tools/eg-q` exposes only `search|def|callers|impact|grep`. **No rep50 session could reach
it**, so every agent ran the harness by hand through Bash.

**VERIFIED (read-only, this session):**
- Reachable: `internal/cli/root.go:80  case "verify":`; tests drive it as
  `verify --repo R --test "sh run.sh"` (`verify_test.go:259`).
- **6 ecosystem parsers ship**: `cargo, ctest, gotest, jest, phpunit, pytest` + `unknown`
  fallback (`internal/cli/testdata/verify/`).
- Two-phase baseline is real: `--record-baseline` pre-edit, `--pre-edit-baseline` post-edit →
  reports only what *this* edit broke or fixed. That directly kills the "is this failure mine
  or pre-existing?" loop driving the retries.

**RISK — two hard preconditions (`verify.go:113-119`):**
```
verify requires --test <command>
verify requires --pre-edit-baseline <path> (or --record-baseline <path> to create one)
```
The agent must supply the command AND have called verify *before* editing. The VERIFY block
that derives a command appeared in only **8 of 33** payloads. **Shipped as-is, L1 fails for
most sessions.**

**Mitigation — put the protocol in the wrapper, not the agent.** `eg-q verify [cmd]` should:
1. derive the test command when not supplied (reuse `internal/sem/search_verify.go`),
2. manage the baseline file itself — `--record-baseline /tmp/egq-vb-$IID.json` on first call,
   `--pre-edit-baseline` thereafter,
3. return the parsed delta.
The agent then just calls `eg-q verify`. This is tool engineering, not instruction.

**Parser coverage vs our actual losers:** bat→`cargo` ✓, ansible/openlibrary→`pytest` ✓,
laravel/carbon→`phpunit` ✓ (**5/8**). valkey (tcl `./runtest`), javaparser (`mvn`), lombok
(`javac`/`ant`) fall to `unknown` — still capped + exit-coded, but no parsed diff. Expect
weaker gains on those three; two of them are also in the non-converting set.

**RISK 2 — ADOPTION. This is the one that sinks the plan if ignored.**
Measured verb uptake across all 49 eg sessions:

| verb | calls | sessions |
|---|---|---|
| grep | 44 | 34/49 |
| search | 34 | 33/49 |
| def | 24 | 19/49 |
| callers | 3 | 3/49 |
| **impact** | **0** | **0/49** |

**`impact` is named in all 49 prompts and was used zero times.** A capability line in the
affordance tail therefore has a documented **0% adoption precedent**. Shipping `verify` that way
would very likely produce no behaviour change at all.

**Mitigation — surface it where the agent is already looking, at the moment of need.** The
`VERIFY:` block already appears *inside search output*. Change it from a passive string the
agent must re-type into Bash:
```
VERIFY: vendor/bin/phpunit tests/CarbonInterval/TotalTest.php
```
into an executable affordance offered right after localization, e.g. a line stating that
`eg-q verify` runs exactly this and reports only the tests **this** edit changed. Tool output,
delivered at the point of relevance — strictly stronger than a prompt line.

**Sub-requirement:** VERIFY appeared in only **8 of 33** payloads. Coverage must rise toward
~100% or L1 reaches only a quarter of Class B. Raising it is work in
`internal/sem/search_verify.go`, and it is a hard prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.

Change set for L1:
1. `eg-q` gains a `verify` branch with auto-derived command + auto-managed baseline (kills RISK 1).
2. Search's VERIFY block advertises the executable path (kills RISK 2).
3. VERIFY derivation coverage raised from 8/33 (kills the coverage cap).
4. One capability line in the affordance tail — necessary but, on the `impact` evidence,
   nowhere near sufficient on its own.

*Fairness:* a **verb** is not an instruction — the baseline cannot invoke it. This is the same
class of difference as the search payload itself. The affordance line states capability only
(the existing tail was audited clean, see below).
*Scope honesty:* this measures "the tool as shipped, including its verification affordance",
not "the graph's marginal retrieval value". **Say which, in any writeup.**

### L2 — symmetric harness clamp — **REJECTED, modelled net-negative**

A clamp inside `published_exact_prompt()` (`run_3arm.sh:1227`, no arm argument → symmetric by
construction) was the obvious fair way to cut retries. **Modelled against measured runner counts
and per-call context, it makes the suite WORSE:**

| clamp K | winner group | loser group | combined 13 |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | +55.6% | −57.1% | **−2.7%** |
| 2 | +55.6% | −48.5% | **−9.7%** |
| 3 | +55.2% | −48.4% | **−9.6%** |
| 5 | +54.5% | −48.7% | **−9.7%** |

Losers improve (bat −79.6→−50.1, javaparser −145.1→−89.1) but winners pay more than losers gain:
`laravel-48636` **+50.6→+30.5**, `lombok-3674` **+71.0→+59.7**. In the winners it is the
**baseline** that flails (lombok baseline `javac`×68 vs eg ×23), so a symmetric clamp hands the
baseline the savings.

**Do not ship a shared frugality clamp.** The asymmetry that makes eg win is precisely that the
baseline over-runs the harness; suppressing that suppresses the win.

### L1-BLOCKER — the shipped binary has no `verify`

`./entire-graph verify` → **`unknown command`**. The checked-in binary (2026-08-04 21:41)
predates source HEAD `ecaba15` (2026-08-05). rep50 therefore ran a binary in which `verify`
does not exist at all, and `stats.verify_tier` is absent. **L1 requires a rebuild and a
provenance check before anything else.**

### L4 — the higher-value graph work the architecture review surfaced

Ranked by (turn impact ÷ build cost), all data already in the graph:

| # | change | data | turns | build |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R2** | a **working-tree `changed` verb** — "what did I just edit, and what else needs it" | yes | **3–5** | med |
| R4 | probe the VERIFY command; wire `verify --from-search` | mostly | 1–3 | **low** |
| R1 | warm the dirty-worktree index | yes | 0 direct, **unblocks R2–R4** | med |
| R3 | covering-test verb keyed on the diff | machinery yes, **edges weak** | 2–4 | med |
| R5 | co-change / CHANGE SET block | yes | 1–2 | low |

**R2 is the strongest and is genuinely missing:** `diff --base HEAD --head HEAD` returns
`{"files": null}` — **no verb can see an uncommitted edit.** Yet post-edit is where 97.7% of the
loss lives. `gitutil.ChangedFiles` (`git.go:379`), `dependents.go` (repo-wide reference counts)
and `search_related.go` (siblings/callers from an anchor) all exist; they just point at hit-1
instead of at the diff hunks.

**R1 is a hard prerequisite:** `worktreeSnapshotCacheable` (`search_cache.go:94`) returns false
on *any* dirty tree, so **every post-edit search re-indexes from scratch** — measured 1782 ms
vs 56 ms warm, and 8.9 s search / 22.4 s impact on real SWE-bench repos.

### Structural findings worth acting on regardless

- **`search` defaults to `--profile fast`**, which excludes `TESTS`, `SIMILAR_TO`, all type
  relations, `DATA_FLOWS` and `FILE_CHANGES_WITH` (`provider.go:462`). At the default the
  covering-test block, type card, signature types and half of RELATED SITES are *structurally
  empty*. eg-q sets `full`, so rep50 was fine — but the shipped default is misleading.
- **`TESTS` = 10 edges out of 36,114.** It is name-convention only (`provider.go:8875`) and is
  the covering-test block's advertised "strongest evidence". Fix the edge source before
  betting on R3.
- **`searchTestIntentWords` foot-gun** (`search.go:4402`): any query containing "test"/"spec"
  disables the −12 test demotion. Bug reports say "test" constantly; reproduced live returning
  a `_test.go` file at rank 1.
- **Signals computed but never used by search:** `DATA_FLOWS` (2,997), `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`
  (387), `HANDLES_ROUTE` (48), relation `Evidence` (exact call-site lines), `Confidence` (used
  only as a ≥0.7 gate, the value discarded), `dependents.go` counts, `SymbolRecord.Aliases`.

### ⚠️ FAIRNESS LANDMINE — `.entire/graph-agent.md`

It contains exactly the arm-asymmetric methodology the doctrine forbids: *"ONE search, then
act"*, *"Do NOT re-read what search already gave you"*, *"NEVER read a whole file"*, *"measured
to cut session tokens roughly in half"* — and it is `@`-included into `CLAUDE.md`.
**It did NOT leak into rep50** (`--safe-mode` disables CLAUDE.md for both arms; 0 injected files
verified in both checkouts). But any future cell run without `--safe-mode`, or on a machine
where that file is present, is invalid on arrival. **Add an explicit preflight assertion.**

### L3 — secondary fixes (cheap, independent)
- Deploy `b5473b0b` never-refuse to the VMs — **built and offline-verified, not yet deployed**
  (local eg-q `d1d115eb` vs VM `3878e23c`). Targets Class A, 9.12M burn.
- Checkout-layout leak: 2 instances spent 13–15 calls mining an *adjacent instance's* tree.
- Payload truncation at 4096/8192 B (10 of 33) — determine if the agent's stream truncated too.
- `O35_STRIP_ADVICE` eats the LOW CONFIDENCE notice (`eg-q:160` greps `verify before editing`).
- 6 flags inert (`EG_PREFETCH=0` kills all prefetch consumers; 0 `prefetch.payload` in 49

> *"That seems like cheating then? Why is baseline able to run the tests cheaper than eg is?"*

the same checkout with identical access (verified: only the eg `entire` shim differs on PATH).

9–19× vs baseline 4–10×). That is an eg behavioural regression, not a baseline advantage.

**Answer to the first: partly yes, on scope.** `verify` is cheap because of an *output
contract*, not privileged access — `cli/verify.go:31` returns an **adjudicated verdict, never
raw output**, capped at **2,048 B** (`:41`). The baseline could pipe `pytest` through `head`;
it doesn't. That is a genuine tool capability. **But** shipping it means we stop measuring
"does the code graph save tokens" and start measuring "does a bundle of dev tools save tokens".

**Consequence for this plan: L1 is demoted from PRIMARY to optional, and must be labelled.**
If run, report it as *graph + verify* against *no tools*, and report the graph-only number
beside it. Do not let it become the headline for entire-graph.

## ⛔ THE +35.06% NUMBER IS AN ARTIFACT — retracted

**eg's saving is a function of BASELINE WASTE, not of graph quality.**

| baseline cost tercile | median baseline | eg TOKEN | eg median |
|---|---|---|---|
| cheap | 0.99M | **−27.76%** | −28.0% |
| mid | 2.48M | −2.99% | +6.2% |
| expensive | 5.13M | **+8.07%** | +8.9% |

Below-median baselines: **−14.64%**. Above-median (78% of token mass): **+5.87%**.

**Why this kills the arithmetic:** the winner group's eg/base ratio of 0.604 was achieved on
instances whose baselines spent **2.64M median / 56 turns**. Applying that ratio to a 0.99M
baseline is impossible — there is no waste there to capture. "Convert every loser to
winner-quality" is not merely hard, it is **arithmetically unavailable** for the ~half of
losers whose baselines are already efficient.

The ceiling is therefore set by *how much the no-tool baseline wastes*, which the graph does
not control. On the 78% of token mass where waste is greatest, eg captures **+5.87%**.

**Empirical ceiling, all fair cells at n≥25: `opus xhigh` +17.21% (n=26).** That is the largest
honest number this project has produced.

- **Winner-ratio model (mine):** convert all 22 losers to the winner eg/base ratio → **+35.06%**.
  This is an *upper bound*: it assumes total conversion of every loser.
- **Mechanism model (architecture review):** removing N post-edit calls yields +2.8% at N=0,

The mechanism model is grounded in measured elasticity; mine assumes an outcome. **The honest
expected range is +18% to +25%, and 35% is the ceiling only under total conversion.** Say this
plainly rather than quoting +35.06%.

Running the tests for the agent makes eg cheaper at work **both arms do identically** — the
baseline is not cheaper per run, eg simply runs the harness 9–19× vs 4–10×. It would book a
subsidy for an eg regression as a graph win, and it changes the claim from "the code graph
saves tokens" to "our bundle does dev work cheaply". **Dropped. Do not run it.**

### L1′ — fix the VERIFY *derivation* so the first invocation works (REPLACEMENT)

Same target (post-edit waste), fair by construction: deriving the correct test command from
build files **plus the graph** is code intelligence. It makes the graph's answer better rather
than making eg cheaper at shared work.

The waste is not legitimate re-testing. From the transcripts it is failing to get the harness
running: `sleep 90/120/150` polling, `pkill` ×4, `--baseport` juggling, tailing its own
transcript to recover truncated Bash output, hand-built `/tmp` rigs.

1. **Wrong scope.** nushell (−141.2%): the manifest walk emitted `cargo test -p nu-cli` when the
   fix was in `nu-command`. **The graph knows which crate/package/module owns the symbol; the
   manifest walk cannot.** Use symbol→file→package to scope the command.
2. **No runnability check.** The only probe is `exec.LookPath` on the runner
   (`search_verify.go:1526`) — it confirms `pytest` is installed, never that the command runs.
   Add a collect-only probe (`pytest --collect-only`, `go test -run XXX -count=0`,
   `cargo test --no-run`) and drop to the next rung on failure.
3. **Coverage 8/33.** Most payloads carry no VERIFY line at all. Raise toward ~100% or this
   reaches only a quarter of Class B.

Fairness: the derived command is tool output computed from the repo, the same class as the
ranked hits. It ships no instruction and the baseline arm is untouched.

### L1-OLD — expose the executing `verify` verb (REMOVED — kept for the record)

**The capability already exists and was never wired up.** `internal/cli/verify.go:193` runs
`exec.CommandContext(ctx,"sh","-c",cmd)` + `CombinedOutput()` via `runVerifyCommands` (:158).
It has ecosystem-aware timeouts (`verifyCompiledCommand` :178 — cargo/go test/mvn/gradle/cmake/
ctest/make/bazel/dotnet/swift), **discards setup output** so install logs don't pollute test
parsing, returns exit code **separately** from error (a failing suite is normal), caps output via
`maxBytes`, and never mutates the tree.

But `tools/eg-q` exposes only `search|def|callers|impact|grep`. **No rep50 session could reach
it**, so every agent ran the harness by hand through Bash.

**VERIFIED (read-only, this session):**
- Reachable: `internal/cli/root.go:80  case "verify":`; tests drive it as
  `verify --repo R --test "sh run.sh"` (`verify_test.go:259`).
- **6 ecosystem parsers ship**: `cargo, ctest, gotest, jest, phpunit, pytest` + `unknown`
  fallback (`internal/cli/testdata/verify/`).

| verb | calls | sessions |
|---|---|---|

| search | 34 | 33/49 |
| def | 24 | 19/49 |
| callers | 3 | 3/49 |

agent must re-type into Bash:

```

~100% or L1 reaches only a quarter of Class B. Raising it is work in
`internal/sem/search_verify.go`, and it is a hard prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.

Change set for L1:
1. `eg-q` gains a `verify` branch with auto-derived command + auto-managed baseline (kills RISK 1).
2. Search's VERIFY block advertises the executable path (kills RISK 2).
3. VERIFY derivation coverage raised from 8/33 (kills the coverage cap).

class of difference as the search payload itself. The affordance line states capability only
(the existing tail was audited clean, see below).

| none | +55.6% | −57.1% | **−2.7%** |

**Do not ship a shared frugality clamp.** The asymmetry that makes eg win is precisely that the
baseline over-runs the harness; suppressing that suppresses the win.

does not exist at all, and `stats.verify_tier` is absent. **L1 requires a rebuild and a
provenance check before anything else.**

Ranked by (turn impact ÷ build cost), all data already in the graph:

| # | change | data | turns | build |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R2** | a **working-tree `changed` verb** — "what did I just edit, and what else needs it" | yes | **3–5** | med |
| R4 | probe the VERIFY command; wire `verify --from-search` | mostly | 1–3 | **low** |

It contains exactly the arm-asymmetric methodology the doctrine forbids: *"ONE search, then
act"*, *"Do NOT re-read what search already gave you"*, *"NEVER read a whole file"*, *"measured
to cut session tokens roughly in half"* — and it is `@`-included into `CLAUDE.md`.
**It did NOT leak into rep50** (`--safe-mode` disables CLAUDE.md for both arms; 0 injected files
verified in both checkouts). But any future cell run without `--safe-mode`, or on a machine
where that file is present, is invalid on arrival. **Add an explicit preflight assertion.**

### L3 — secondary fixes (cheap, independent)
- Deploy `b5473b0b` never-refuse to the VMs — **built and offline-verified, not yet deployed**
  (local eg-q `d1d115eb` vs VM `3878e23c`). Targets Class A, 9.12M burn.
- Checkout-layout leak: 2 instances spent 13–15 calls mining an *adjacent instance's* tree.
- Payload truncation at 4096/8192 B (10 of 33) — determine if the agent's stream truncated too.
- `O35_STRIP_ADVICE` eats the LOW CONFIDENCE notice (`eg-q:160` greps `verify before editing`).
- 6 flags inert (`EG_PREFETCH=0` kills all prefetch consumers; 0 `prefetch.payload` in 49
  sessions) and 15 knobs are inheritance-only, incl. `EG_VERIFY_PROBE` — bake into `eg-q.run`.

## ⛔ ADDRESSABLE-FRACTION AUDIT — the fix is worth +2.67%, not +24%

All **763** post-edit tool calls hand-classified across the 8 worst losers (counts reproduce
exactly: 442/321 tool calls, 370/248 API calls, +122).

| bucket | excess | addressable |
|---|---|---|
| F code reading/editing | +31 (26%) | **0** |
| A real test iteration | +30 (25%) | ~4 |
| E scratch harnesses | +26 (21%) | 5 strict |
| C output recovery | +18 (15%) | 7 |
| B polling/timeout | +13 (11%) | 6 |
| **D environment repair** | **+1** | — (eg 30 vs base 29: a **wash**) |

| | calls | tokens | suite |
|---|---|---|---|
| conservative | 17/122 (14%) | 1.92M | **+2.67%** |
| optimistic | 46/122 (38%) | 4.68M | **+4.57%** |

**14 of the 17 conservative calls are one instance.** Drop `bat-1892` → **2.5% addressable**.
In dollars it is ~$1.40 per 8 instances, because 97.8% of the removed tokens are cache reads.

**Strongest counter-evidence, and it is decisive:** the baseline was *not verifying at all* on
half these instances — baseline test-run counts: javaparser **0**, lombok **0**, bat-3108 2,
openlibrary 3. Cause is environmental:
```
base bat-1892 [9]  cargo build → netjail: no real 'cargo' found on PATH behind the guard
```
The baseline gave up and hand-rolled `rustc /tmp/mock_check.rs`; the eg agent found
`~/.cargo/bin/cargo` and ran the real suite. **Part of "eg waste" is eg doing verification the
baseline skipped.** Any tool that makes testing easy raises the *baseline's* count too.

Also: the agent re-ran commands whose output already fit (bat-3108 `cargo test --offline` ×3,
943–2,231 B, never truncated). An output cap cannot prevent that.

## MEASUREMENT-INTEGRITY DEFECTS (fix these regardless of any lever)

1. **Rust toolchain not persisted to the session PATH.** The 2026-08-04 toolchain-PATH fix is
   symmetric and covers ruby/node/python — **not cargo**. Both arms hunt for it; whether an arm
   finds it decides whether it runs real tests or a stub. Huge variance, not bias.
2. **Shipped binary predates source** — `./entire-graph verify` → `unknown command`;
   `stats.verify_tier` absent though the harness reads it.
3. **`.entire/graph-agent.md`** carries arm-asymmetric methodology (*"ONE search, then act"*,
   *"NEVER read a whole file"*) and is `@`-included into `CLAUDE.md`. Did **not** leak into rep50
   (`--safe-mode`, 0 injected files verified both arms) but voids any cell run without it.
4. **`_tee` fix and never-refuse fix are committed locally but NOT deployed to the VMs.**

## Arithmetic — each fix priced against the class it targets

Winner-group ratio eg/base = **0.604**. Suite base pool 145.6M.

| fix | targets | burn | → neutral | → winner-quality |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| never-refuse `b5473b0b` (**built, offline-verified**) | Class A, 8 inst | 9.12M | +7.62% | **+11.33%** |
| `verify` verb (**exists, needs wiring**) | Class B, 13 inst | 18.96M | +14.37% | **+24.49%** |
| **both** | 21 of 22 losers | 28.1M | +20.64% | **+34.46%** |
| + last loser (Class C) | 22 | 28.6M | +20.99% | **+35.06%** |

**Both fixes at winner quality = +34.46%; with the last loser, +35.06%.**
If Class B converts but A only neutralises: **+30.75%**.

Cross-check by a second route — driving post-edit call ratio to the winner's 0.474×: the 8
worst go **−57.1% → +40.7%** (30.3M recovered), suite **+22.17%**, and **+27.41%** with 70% of
the remaining burn. The two routes agree within a few points.

**`javaparser-4538` does not convert** (−145% → −59%; pre-edit dominant). Budget 1–3
non-converters — that is the difference between +31% and +35%, so **35% requires near-total
conversion and has no margin.**

## Gate ladder — escalate only on pass

Every gate: both arms, fresh, same instances, reporting **total + median + Δturns + harness-run
counts**.

**MEASURED NOISE FLOOR — this dictates the gate design.** 28 instances have been run in ≥2
independent cells. Same instance, same config:

| instance | cells | range | swing |
|---|---|---|---|
| fluentd-4655 | 7 | −263.6% .. +30.7% | **294pt** |
| ruff-15626 | 7 | −206.4% .. +47.3% | 254pt |
| caddy-5995 | 7 | −172.1% .. +63.7% | 236pt |
| hugo-12562 | 9 | −106.8% .. +62.4% | 169pt |

**Median same-instance swing 99.9pt, mean 118pt, max 294pt.**

Two consequences, both binding:
1. **No per-instance token delta can ever be a gate criterion.** A 30pt improvement is invisible.
2. **The identity of "the 22 losers" is itself unstable** — many would not be losers on a re-run.
   The fix is still valid because it is a *tool change applied to every instance*, not per-instance
   surgery. But do not treat the loser list as a fixed target set.

**Gates therefore read MECHANISM COUNTS (low noise, directly observable), not tokens.**

| gate | sample | n | pass criterion — mechanism, not tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| **G0** | offline, no model, $0 | 0 | `eg-q verify` returns a parsed result on cargo/pytest/phpunit/gotest/unknown repos; auto-baseline works; 0 regressions on existing verbs |
| **G1** | 4 losers + 2 winners | 6 | **`verify` is called in ≥4/6 sessions** (kills the `impact` 0/49 risk) and **raw harness invocations fall ≥50%** vs the rep50 run. **No token claim at this n.** |
| **G2** | 8 losers + 4 winners | 12 | median post-edit call count ≤ baseline; VERIFY block present in ≥80% of payloads; winners' harness counts unchanged |
| **G3** | all 22 losers + 10 winners | 32 | **first token claim**: loser group ≥ −5% and winner group ≥ +30%, both with bootstrap CI |
| **G4** | full rep50, both arms | 49 | **≥35%** with bootstrap CI; report total, median, Δturns |

`lombok-3674` (+71.0, 8.87M) and `fmt-2457` (+62.1, 3.18M) as the regression tripwire —
**lombok alone is worth more than the four losers gained.** Its role at G1/G2 is to confirm its
harness behaviour is *unchanged*, not to measure its tokens.

## Kill criteria

1. If G1 cannot flip ≥3 of 4 worst losers, this does not reach 35% — report and stop.
2. If any gate regresses a top winner >10pt, the fix is net-negative.
3. If losers land near 0% rather than winner-quality, ceiling is +20.99% — **snapshot that
   result** and continue only with a new mechanism, not a re-roll.
4. **No arm-asymmetric instruction, ever**, even if it would hit the number.
5. No claim from one cell: between-cell spread on identical config is ~20pt (opus max measured
   +1.35% / −4.65% / −25.04%).

n=49, all pairs. Shared block **byte-identical** after normalising the arm path. One eg-only

8	// WorktreeMatchesHEAD reports whether the working tree's indexable content is
9	// byte-identical to the committed HEAD tree.
10	//
11	// It is the precondition that lets a caller reuse a tree-keyed index cache for
12	// a working-tree query: when nothing is modified, staged, deleted or untracked,
13	// every file a working-tree walk can see is exactly the file HEAD records, so a

15	//
16	// The check is one `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` and is
17	// deliberately conservative:
18	//
19	//   - it reports FALSE on any output at all — modified, staged, deleted,
20	//     renamed, unmerged, untracked, or a dirty submodule;
21	//   - `--untracked-files=all` is required, not optional: a working-tree walk
22	//     indexes untracked-but-not-ignored files, so "no tracked modifications"
23	//     alone would not make the two views equal;
24	//   - files git ignores are excluded from BOTH sides (the provider's
25	//     working-tree walk honours .gitignore), so an ignored build artifact
26	//     changing cannot invalidate the equality. If the ignore rules themselves
27	//     change so that a file stops being ignored, that file becomes untracked
28	//     and this check turns false, which is the safe direction;
29	//   - any error (not a git repository, git missing) reports FALSE with the
30	//     error, never a hopeful TRUE.
31	//
32	// `--no-optional-locks` keeps this read-only probe from refreshing the index
33	// and so from contending with a concurrent git command in the same repo.
34	func WorktreeMatchesHEAD(ctx context.Context, repo string) (bool, error) {
35		// A repository with no commits has no HEAD tree to be equal to.
36		if _, err := RevParse(ctx, repo, "HEAD"); err != nil {
37			return false, err
38		}
39		out, err := run(ctx, repo, "git",
40			"--no-optional-locks", "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=all", "-z")
41		if err != nil {
42			return false, err
43		}
44		return strings.Trim(out, "\x00\n\r \t") == "", nil
45	}

content.text:
**R1 shipped** — `503a554`.

## What it does

A working-tree snapshot was cacheable only while the tree was byte-identical to HEAD, because the key *is* the tree hash. So the cache was refused **from the first edit onward** — every query an agent makes after it starts changing code, which is exactly where 97.7% of the token loss lives.

Now the dirty tree gets *named* instead of refused: `WorktreeContentDigest` folds the HEAD hash together with every differing path and its current bytes, threaded into the cache key as a separate component.

**Verified on a controlled repo:**

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| clean | miss → hit | miss → hit *(unchanged)* |
| **dirty** | **miss every time** | **miss → hit → hit** |
| content changed | — | **miss** → hit *(invalidates correctly)* |
| reverted to clean | — | **hit** *(reuses the pre-change entry)* |

That last row is the strongest correctness signal — existing on-disk caches keep their keys. Full suite green: 6 packages, 0 failures.

## One design trap worth recording

My first attempt folded the digest *into* the tree hash. That broke immediately with `HEAD changed while building search snapshot` — because `tree` is also the provenance a freshly built snapshot is checked against (`snapshot.Header.Tree`), so an augmented value makes a correct build look like a mid-flight HEAD change. The digest has to be its own key component.

It also stays conservative in every direction: deletions record absence rather than hashing (so deleted ≠ empty), renames record both paths, nested repositories get walked because the provider's walk sees their files, and >64 differing paths or any git error falls back to not caching exactly as before.

content.text:
Both levers from the plan are built, tested, and committed.

## What shipped

**`503a554` — R1: dirty working trees now cache.** The key was the tree hash, which can't name a dirty tree, so the cache was refused from the first edit onward — every query after the agent starts changing code. Now a content digest of exactly what differs is folded into the key.

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| clean | miss → hit | miss → hit *(unchanged)* |
| **dirty** | **miss every time** | **miss → hit → hit** |
| content changed | — | **miss** → hit |
| reverted to clean | — | **hit** *(reuses pre-change entry)* |

**`c500baa` — R2: `entire graph changed`.** The gap was total: `diff --base HEAD --head HEAD` returns no files, so no verb could see an uncommitted edit — while 97.7% of the measured loss lands post-edit. On this repo it surfaces `Run` with **54 callers** at the top of 322 changed definitions; on a fixture it finds the caller in a file the agent never opened, and picks up untracked files (which never appear in a diff but *are* indexed).

Both reuse existing machinery rather than adding a pipeline — R2 shares the snapshot cache R1 just fixed, which is why R1 was the prerequisite. Full suite green throughout: **6 packages, 0 failures**, vet clean.

## Two traps worth recording

**Don't fold the digest into the tree hash.** My first attempt did, and broke instantly with `HEAD changed while building search snapshot` — `tree` is also the provenance a fresh build is checked against, so an augmented value makes a correct build look like a mid-flight HEAD change.

**Readable output is part of the feature.** `changed` first emitted 38 paths dominated by untracked worktree dirs and docs, burying three Go edits. A verb that exists to save turns can't open with a wall of noise, so files with definitions are listed individually and the rest collapsed to a count.

## Where this leaves the goal

These are the two levers the plan identified as worth building, and I've built them. What they're worth is still bounded by what I measured before starting: the addressable post-edit waste is **+2.67–4.57%**, and six independent routes converge on **+15–21%** against a best-ever fair cell of **+17.21%**.

Neither commit changes that ceiling — they make the tool answer a question it couldn't answer at all, and they remove a latency wall that made post-edit querying impractical. Whether that converts into measured tokens is an empirical question I can't answer without a cell, and the plan's own G1 gate says to read *mechanism counts* (does the agent call `changed`? do harness invocations fall?) rather than token deltas, because same-instance swing is median 99.9pt.

Still outstanding from the plan: the stale binary on the VMs lacks both commits, and `.entire/graph-agent.md` still claims "cut session tokens roughly in half" while `AGENTS.md` withdraws exactly that number.

The full stack is deployed and verified on all three VMs — identical binary (`8daf183ee29d`) and `eg-q` (`9632e488`), with `changed` responding on each.

## Everything from the plan is now built and shipped

| item | state |
|---|---|
| **R1** — dirty working trees cache | ✅ `503a554`, 4 properties verified |
| **R2** — `entire graph changed` verb | ✅ `c500baa`, verified on a real SWE-bench checkout |
| **eg-q exposure** + affordance line | ✅ `0cf9cff9`, fairness-checked |
| never-refuse + `_tee` fixes | ✅ deployed earlier |
| Linux binary rebuilt from source | ✅ built on-VM, distributed to a/b/c |

The end-to-end proof is the one I'd point at: on `redis__redis-11510`'s leftover checkout, `eg-q changed` reports the edited `fcallCommandGeneric` at `:618` and both call sites — the post-edit question that previously had no answer at all, since `diff --base HEAD --head HEAD` returns nothing.

## What I won't claim

**None of this makes 35% reachable, and I'm not going to run a cell pretending otherwise.** The measurement stands: 97.7% of loss is post-edit, eg's savings are bounded by baseline waste (`corr = +0.305`; cheap baselines −27.76%), the directly addressable slice is **+2.67–4.57%**, and six routes converge on **+15–21%** against a best-ever fair cell of **+17.21%**.

What changed today is capability, not ceiling: the tool can now answer a post-edit question it structurally could not, and querying after an edit went from a 1782ms re-index to a 22ms cache hit.

**The honest next step is G1, not rep50** — 6 instances reading *mechanism counts*: does the agent call `changed`, and do raw harness invocations fall? Those are low-noise and directly observable. Token deltas at n=6 are meaningless when same-instance swing is median 99.9pt. If G1 shows uptake, G2 and G3 escalate; if it shows the `impact` 0/49 pattern repeating, the verb is unreachable in practice and I'd say so rather than escalate.

Two loose ends I'd still fix before any cell: `.entire/graph-agent.md` claims "cut session tokens roughly in half" while `AGENTS.md` withdraws that exact number, and Rust's toolchain still isn't on the session PATH — which is why one arm ran real `cargo test` and the other hand-rolled a mock.

## Hard rules (each violation costs real money)

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. ONE search, then act. Do not run a second search unless the first clearly missed.
3. Do NOT re-read what search already gave you. A `complete-symbol` hit is the whole function:
   edit it. Read a line range only for hits search returned as locators.
4. NEVER read a whole file; read at most ~120 lines around the reported line.
5. Impact question ("who calls X" / "what could this change break" / "where else needs this
   same change")? ONE targeted query:

   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change files, siblings)
6. ALWAYS verify your edit at least once before you finish: build/compile it, or run the nearest
   existing test. Pick the narrowest command that would still catch a syntax, type, name, or
   arity error (one package, one file, one test — not the whole suite).
7. VERIFY, DON'T CHASE. Verification is bounded: run it, read the error, fix exactly what the

Everything from the plan is now built, tested, deployed, and committed.

## Shipped this session

| commit | repo | what |
|---|---|---|
| `503a554` | entire-graph | **R1** — dirty working trees cache (1782ms → 22ms post-edit) |
| `c500baa` | entire-graph | **R2** — `entire graph changed` verb |
| `98d9a66` | entire-graph | agent doctrine: drop the withdrawn savings claim |
| `0cf9cff9` | graphmark | expose `changed` via `eg-q` + affordance |
| `681cb4c0` | graphmark | Rust/PHP toolchains handed to the session |
| earlier | graphmark | never-refuse + `_tee` fixes, deployed to all VMs |

All three VMs carry the identical rebuilt binary (`8daf183ee29d`) and `eg-q` (`9632e488`). Full Go suite green throughout — 6 packages, 0 failures, vet clean.

**The proof I'd point at:** on `redis__redis-11510`'s leftover checkout, `eg-q changed` reports the edited `fcallCommandGeneric` at `:618` and both call sites — a question that previously had *no answer*, since `diff --base HEAD --head HEAD` returns nothing.

**The one I'd flag hardest** is `681cb4c0`. On `bat-1892` the baseline hit `netjail: no real 'cargo' found`, gave up, and hand-rolled `rustc /tmp/mock_check.rs`, while eg found `~/.cargo/bin` and ran the real suite — 13 build/test invocations against 1. Baseline test-runs elsewhere: javaparser **0**, lombok **0**. So part of what I'd been scoring as "eg waste" was **eg verifying while the baseline faked it**. That's variance on exactly the measured axis, and every past cell carries it.

## On the goal, plainly

I can't tell you 35% is reachable, because six independent routes say +15–21% and the directly addressable post-edit waste is +2.67–4.57%. I retracted my own +35.06% when I found it assumed every loser could adopt a ratio earned on baselines spending 2.64M — impossible against a 0.99M baseline. eg's savings are bounded by baseline waste (`corr = +0.305`), which the graph doesn't control.

What I *can* tell you is that the tool is materially better than it was this morning, and that the next honest step is **G1 on 6 instances reading mechanism counts** — does the agent call `changed`, do harness invocations fall — because token deltas at n=6 are noise against a median same-instance swing of 99.9pt.

Two things I'd want before any cell: the `netjail`/toolchain fix means **past cells and future cells are no longer comparable**, so a fresh baseline is required rather than reusing rep50's; and the checked-in macOS binary is still stale (a git hook just failed on `unknown command "changed"`).

**G2 is running clean** — 8 drivers, 8 sessions, preflight passed, and I purged 8 stale `cc_out.json` files (4 per arm) that would otherwise have caused those instances to be silently skipped.

## What I caught in-flight

The rider shipped attached to `callers` and `impact`. Measured carrier frequency across rep50's 49 sessions:

```
grep 44   search 34   def 24   callers 3   impact 0
```

**Only 3 of 49 sessions ever touched `callers`/`impact`.** The rider would have reached ~6% of sessions, and G2 would have returned a null result for a reason having nothing to do with whether the rider works. I spotted it 9 minutes in — four eg payloads carried content, zero carried the rider, because the carrier verbs had been called zero times.

Fixed in `b59b5ca0`: the gate is now **tree state**, not a guess about which verb an agent reaches for. G1 already proved that guess is unreliable. Verified clean-tree silent / dirty-tree present on all three high-frequency verbs.

## Session ledger

| commit | what |
|---|---|
| `503a554` | R1 — dirty trees cache |
| `c500baa` | R2 — `changed` verb |
| `98d9a66` | doctrine — withdrawn claim removed |
| `0cf9cff9` | eg-q exposure |
| `681cb4c0` | Rust/PHP toolchain |
| `ff2c92e1` | post-edit rider |
| `b59b5ca0` | rider on all verbs (the G1+G2 fix) |

Two gates run, two useful negatives: **G1** — advertising a verb yields 0/5 adoption even when the agent is asking that verb's question; **G2 v1** — hanging delivery on rare verbs reaches 6% of sessions.

## On 35%

Unchanged and still not supported. Six routes converge on **+15–21%**; addressable post-edit waste is **+2.67–4.57%**; eg's saving is bounded by baseline waste (`corr = +0.305`), which the graph doesn't control. I retracted my own +35.06% when I found it assumed losers could adopt a ratio earned on 2.64M baselines — impossible against a 0.99M one.

G2 now measures the one thing that could move that: **do post-edit harness invocations fall** when the agent is handed what it changed. Delivery is no longer optional, so this is a clean test of the mechanism rather than of adoption. I'll report delivery rate, per-arm harness counts, and tokens-with-caveats when it lands.

VM C has been SSH-unresponsive for ~8 minutes across five retries. The G2 sessions are detached and still running — I simply can't observe them until load drops. This is the third wedge, always under 8 concurrent drivers, and it's now a known operational limit of these VMs.

## Where things stand

**Built, tested, committed, deployed — 7 commits this session:**

| commit | what | verified |
|---|---|---|
| `503a554` | R1 — dirty trees cache | 4 properties incl. correct invalidation |
| `c500baa` | R2 — `changed` verb | 5/5 languages + real SWE-bench checkout |
| `98d9a66` | doctrine — withdrawn claim removed | contradiction with AGENTS.md resolved |
| `0cf9cff9` | eg-q exposure + affordance | fairness-checked |
| `681cb4c0` | Rust/PHP toolchain to session | root-caused from `netjail` evidence |
| `ff2c92e1` | post-edit rider | clean/dirty behaviour proven |
| `b59b5ca0` | rider on all verbs | the G2-v1 fix |

**Three gates run, three useful negatives** — each cheap, each changing the next build:

1. **G0** ✅ 5/5 languages.
2. **G1** ❌ `changed` adoption **0/5**. The prompt advertised it; `bat-1892` called `callers` *twice* post-edit instead. Advertising a verb is not an adoption mechanism — now replicated against `impact`'s 0/49.
3. **G2 v1** ❌ caught in-flight: I'd hung the rider on `callers`/`impact`, which reach **3 of 49 sessions**. Would have produced a null result for the wrong reason. Rewired to gate on tree state.

**G2 v2 is in flight** and measures the one thing that could move tokens: whether post-edit harness invocations fall when the agent is handed what it changed.

## On the 35% goal — my honest position

I can't tell you it's reachable. Six independent routes converge on **+15–21%**; directly addressable post-edit waste is **+2.67–4.57%**; and eg's saving is bounded by *baseline waste* (`corr = +0.305`, cheap baselines −27.76%) — a variable the graph doesn't control. I retracted my own +35.06% when I found it assumed every loser could adopt a ratio earned on 2.64M baselines, which is arithmetically impossible against a 0.99M one.

I've also created a real constraint: the toolchain fix means **rep50's stored baseline is no longer comparable**, so any rep50 is now a full both-arms run, not a half one.

**What I'd need to change my mind:** G2 showing harness invocations falling materially. That would be the first evidence in this project that a build moved the mechanism, and it would justify the full cell. Until then, running rep50 would be spending ~$600 to re-measure a number I can already predict within a few points.

I'll report G2's delivery rate and per-arm harness counts as soon as the VM is reachable.

# TokensNotes.md — every idea tried on entire-graph token savings

Running ledger. **Struck ideas stay struck, with the reason** — the failure modes here repeat, and
re-proposing a dead lever has cost real money more than once.

Sign convention: **positive = the graph arm saved tokens.**

## 0. The one law everything else obeys

**Tokens are messages.** `log(tok) ~ log(msgs)`, elasticity **1.682**, r=**0.957**, n=536.
Message-adjusted residual saving is **0.000** in every model tested.

Consequences, and they are hard constraints not preferences:
- Nothing *inside* a message can move the metric. Only message **count** can.
- An extra tool call is an extra message is **~+1.7% tokens**, mechanically.
- Any lever must be expressed as "removes N messages/session" or it is not a lever.
- `−1% messages = −1.68% tokens`.

This is why eleven payload-quality metrics died. It was never about payload quality.

---

The graph pays when the code to change **already exists and is broken**; it costs when the task is

problem statement (cheap, and it would have to be applied to *both* arms' routing decision to stay
symmetric); or a structural signal — does the issue name an existing symbol that resolves in the
graph? The second is appealing because the graph itself can answer it.

### 3.2 Why does Fable win where Opus doesn't?
Fable pool **+19.1%** CI [+5.4, +30.0] n=26 (excludes zero); Opus pool **−1.4%** CI [−8.7, +5.6]
n=197 (null). Fable emits ~37.5K output tok/session vs Opus ~20K, so it has more to save per
message removed. **But** the within-instance model contrast on the 23 instances present in both a
Fable and an Opus cell is **+15.8pt [−3.0, +32.1] — spans zero.** Model × effort × cell ×
instance-set are perfectly confounded in FABLEMAX.

### 3.3 Is the ADD penalty avoidable rather than routable?
If the graph could say *"the thing you're describing does not exist here"* instead of returning a
plausible wrong hit, the ADD penalty might vanish without any routing. No verb does this today.

- **Adversarial refutation as standard.** Every finding gets N skeptics told to default to
  *refuted* unless they can independently reproduce it. In the two workflows run today this killed

## The mechanism, measured on all 49 pairs

| | baseline | eg |

| shell exploration calls | 995 | 905 |
| graph calls | 0 | 94 |

**One graph call displaces 0.96 shell calls.** It has to displace >1 just to break even on messages — which is why turns went *up* 38 and the headline sits at +1.35%. Nothing about payload quality or ranking was ever going to move that ratio.

The correlation confirms it's the governing variable: `corr(exploration eliminated, tokens saved) = +0.485`, slope 0.767, n=49. Instances where eg explored *more* (18/49): mean **−27.4%**. Instances in the 25–50% elimination band (n=9): mean **+28.4%**.

## Why the ratio is 1:1 — the surviving greps are capability gaps, not stubbornness

Phase split: `graph_pre=91 / grep_pre=232`, `graph_post=3 / grep_post=125`. Reading the 357 greps, four classes dominate and each maps to a verb the graph doesn't have:

| what the grep asks | example | graph today |
|---|---|---|
| **multi-symbol lookup in one call** | `grep -rn "calc_interval\|raw_interval\|calc_max_retry_timeout\|recalc_next_time\|naive_next_time"` | `def` takes **one** symbol — so grep wins on batching alone |
| **scoped search inside a known file/dir** | `grep -n "retry_wait\|backoff" test/plugin/test_output_as_buffered_retries.rb` | no `--path` scoping verb |
| **find the test covering X** | `grep -rn "greater than" tests/Validation/` | `TESTS` = **10 edges of 36,114**, name-convention only — dead |
| **who imports this module** | `grep -rn "from ansible.executor.play_iterator import"` | `IMPORTS` edges exist, **no verb exposes them** |

The agent batches 5–9 alternation patterns into one grep. A single-symbol `def` cannot compete with that, so the agent correctly prefers grep. That is a tool defect, and fixing it is pure tool output — no instructions, nothing the baseline could use.

35% needs 556 of 2671 turns removed. At 94 graph calls that requires a 7:1 displacement ratio; at 150 calls, 5:1. Today: 0.96:1. The band that already achieves ~2:1 measures +28.4%.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# G3 — do `search --path` and batched `def` actually DISPLACE shell exploration?
#
# The measurement this gate exists to move, from all 49 rep50 pairs:
#
#   baseline shell exploration calls   995
#   eg       shell exploration calls   905
#   eg       graph calls                94
#   => 0.96 shell calls displaced per graph call, and the arm's turns went UP 38.
#
# A graph call that removes one shell call is not a saving, it is a substitution. That is the
# whole reason the headline sat at +1.35% while every payload-quality lever measured zero.
#
# Classifying all 357 greps those sessions ran says what they were asking for:
#   scoped to a file or directory  233 (65%)   -> search --path   (did not exist)
#   batched multi-symbol            68 (19%)   -> def A B C       (existed, unreachable via eg-q)
#   free text                       36 (10%)
#   single symbol                   20 ( 6%)
#
# What G3 measures, in order of noise:
#   1. Are the new forms used at all?                     (count, zero noise)
#   2. Displacement ratio (base_expl - eg_expl)/graph_calls (count, low noise) -- THE criterion
#   3. Tokens                                             (reported, NOT a criterion at n=12)
#
# PASS: displacement ratio >= 2.0 (from 0.96) AND the winners' exploration counts do not rise.
# At n=12 the token MDE is ~30pt against a same-instance noise floor of ~100pt, so no token
# claim is made here regardless of which way it falls.
#
# Instances: the 12 with the highest BASELINE exploration volume -- where the mechanism operates.
# Deliberately spans +71.0% (lombok-3674) to -127.4% (valkey-790) so loser repair and winner
# regression are both tested in one cell.
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=$PATH:$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/local/go/bin
. "$HOME/.authenv"; export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
command -v claude >/dev/null || { echo "FATAL no claude on PATH"; exit 1; }
cd ~/work/graphmark/agentic-swebench

BIN="$PWD/bin/entire-graph-linux.r3"
# PREFLIGHT. Every withdrawn headline on this suite died of a harness bug, and the two most recent
# were capabilities that existed but were unreachable from the arm. Assert reachability, not
# presence -- through eg-q, the way a session gets it.
[ -x "$BIN" ] || { echo "FATAL missing $BIN"; exit 1; }
"$BIN" def --brief x --repo . >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL binary lacks --brief"; exit 1; }
"$BIN" search --query worktree --repo . --path internal >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FATAL binary lacks --path"; exit 1; }
grep -q '\-\-path) \[ "\$#" -ge 2 \]' tools/eg-q || { echo "FATAL eg-q lacks --path passthrough"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'EG_DEF_BRIEF_BYTES' tools/eg-q || { echo "FATAL eg-q lacks the batched def form"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'path <dir|file|glob>' tools/run_3arm.sh || { echo "FATAL affordance not updated"; exit 1; }
# Reachability through the wrapper on a real repo, not just the binary in isolation.
R="$PWD/$(ls -d repo-cache/* | head -1)"
WT="$R" EGI="$BIN" EG="$BIN" CACHE=/tmp/egq-g3pre timeout 240 ./tools/eg-q def foo bar 2>&1 | grep -q '== foo ==' \
  || { echo "FATAL batched def not reachable through eg-q"; exit 1; }
echo "[preflight] --path and batched def reachable through eg-q on $R"

export ENTIRE_GRAPH="$BIN"

python3 - <<'PY'

G3 is live — 6 drivers, both arms on binary `af18d641288a9135`, 12 instances spanning +71.0% to −127.4%.

**Where this stands:**

I was wrong about the ceiling, and the error was a denominator. I computed "addressable" on the *delta between arms*, which silently assumes eg's current behaviour is fixed. Measured against the baseline's own exploration pool instead:

| | baseline | eg |
|---|---|---|
| shell exploration calls | 995 | 905 |
| graph calls | 0 | 94 |

**0.96 shell calls displaced per graph call** — substitution, not saving, which is why turns rose 38 while tokens sat at +1.35%. `corr(exploration eliminated, tokens saved) = +0.485` across all 49 pairs, and the instances already achieving 25–50% elimination run +28.4% mean.

Classifying all 357 recorded greps found the tool simply couldn't answer them: 65% named a file or directory (**no path scoping existed**), 19% batched multiple symbols (**existed in the binary, unreachable through eg-q — it joined the names into one string and returned a no-match card**). Both are now fixed, committed (`607b2a4`, `8d6262ff`), 2210 tests green, and the byte economics inverted: for five names, batched grep 1,889 B vs `def --brief` **895 B**.

**Two results I owe you:**
- **G2 (post-edit rider): n=9, −14.48% total, median −24.82%, wins 3/9.** It lost. The rider fired 0/5 because 42/49 sessions make no post-edit graph call — that route is closed, as predicted.
- A and B were preempted; I stood up E as a build host to produce the linux binary.

G3 gates on displacement ratio (≥2.0, from 0.96), not tokens — at n=12 the token MDE is ~30pt against a ~100pt noise floor, so I won't make a token claim from it either way. If displacement moves, the population arithmetic reaches the mid-20s and 35% becomes a question of how much further the remaining classes go; if it doesn't, adoption is the wall and I'll say so.

- 42/49 eg sessions call the graph ONLY before their first edit; 7 call it after (8 calls total).

  grep 44 calls / 34 sessions | search 34 / 33 | def 24 / 19 | callers 3 / 3
  impact 0 / 0   (named in ALL 49 prompts, in the affordance tail)

  Displacement ratio 0.76 (gate was >=2.0, baseline 0.96). Graph calls ROSE 1.9 -> 3.1
  per session while displacement FELL. FAILED.

- The test: "would this sentence help an arm with no tool?" If yes, both arms or neither.

  ("never write a throwaway test script"; "no which, no ls vendor/, no find / -name php*").

13. Post-edit delivery gated on an agent-initiated call - unreachable by construction

            `If it claims not to, state exactly what makes it fire without agent initiative, and whether that ` +
            `mechanism was already tried (the post-edit rider fired 0/5 for exactly this reason). ` +
            `Default to refuted=true.`,
            { label: `refute-adopt:${c.name.slice(0, 22)}`, phase: 'Refute', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA }),

            `REFUTE IT ON FAIRNESS AND ON EFFECT SIZE. Apply the no-tool-arm test strictly. ` +

            `and against the noise floor (median same-instance swing 99.9pt). ` +
            `Is the claimed percentage even detectable? Is it double-counting a bucket another lever also claims? ` +
            `Default to refuted=true.`,

        ]).then((votes) => {
          const live = votes.filter(Boolean)
          const kills = live.filter((v) => v.refuted).length
          const revised = live

            .filter((n) => typeof n === 'number')
          return {
            ...c,
            survives: live.length > 0 && kills < 2,

            consensus_pct: revised.length ? revised.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / revised.length : c.expected_pct,
          }

    ).then((judged) => ({

# entire-graph → 35%: the route, the arithmetic, and the one intervention that reaches it

**Written 2026-08-08. Supersedes `PLAN-TO-35PCT.md`, whose gate ladder ran to completion and
failed at G1, G2 and G3.** Every number here is measured on the rep50 cell (49 gated pairs,
Claude Opus, SWE-bench Multilingual) unless marked as a projection.

Sign convention: **positive = the graph arm saved tokens.**

---

## 0. The problem, in one ratio

Across all 49 pairs:

| | count |
|---|---|
| graph calls made by the eg arm | **94** |
| shell-exploration calls eliminated | 72 |
| harness runs eliminated | 31 |
| **messages eliminated, total** | **103** |
| **net messages saved** (103 − 94) | **9** |

**Eliminations per graph call: 1.10.**

Nine messages out of 2,671 is 0.34% of the message count. Under the governing law
(`log tok ~ log msgs`, elasticity **1.682**, r=**0.957**, n=536) that predicts ≈ +0.6% tokens.
Measured headline: **+1.35%**. The model and the measurement agree.

**35% requires removing 556 of the 2,671 baseline turns.** At the current call volume that means
each graph call must eliminate **6.9 messages instead of 1.10** — a **6.3× move**. This single
number is the whole problem, and every proposal below is judged against it.

---

## 1. Where the removable turns actually are

Baseline, all 49 sessions, phase-split at the first `Edit`/`Write`:

| bucket | calls | share of 2,671 | eg's count | eliminated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shell exploration | **855** | 32.0% | 783 | 72 (8.4%) |
| harness runs (test/build) | **576** | 21.6% | 545 | 31 (5.4%) |
| other bash | 524 | 19.6% | 524 | 0 |
| edits | 397 | 14.9% | 414 | −17 |
| file reads | 240 | 9.0% | 238 | 2 |
| waits / kills | 62 | 2.3% | 62 | 0 |
| graph calls | 0 | — | 94 | −94 |

Shell exploration breakdown (baseline): `grep` 409, `ls` 263, `sed` 161, `cat` 107, `find` 36.

**Only two buckets are addressable by a code graph — exploration (855) and harness (576).**
Together they are 1,431 turns, so 556 is 39% of the addressable pool. It is not arithmetically
impossible. It is behaviourally hard, for the reason in §2.

---

## 2. The mechanism, measured — and a correction to the previous plan

Split the 49 pairs by outcome:

| | n | pts | eg shell | base shell | shell elim. | eg harness | base harness | harness elim. | graph calls |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **lift** | 24 | +21.21 | 370 | 440 | **+70** | 229 | 344 | **+115** | 50 |
| **drag** | 25 | −19.86 | **413** | **415** | **+2** | 316 | 232 | **−84** | 44 |

Three things follow, and two of them correct claims I previously made.

**2.1 — In the losing half the graph displaced nothing.** 413 vs 415 shell calls. Two out of 415.
The payload was delivered and the agent explored exactly as much as it would have without it.
Graph-call counts are near-identical between the halves (44 vs 50), so this is *not* a usage
difference. It is whether the answer landed.

**2.2 — CORRECTION: eg does not verify more than the baseline. It verifies less.**
Population: **eg 545 harness runs vs baseline 576**. Post-edit specifically: **eg 384 vs 422**.
The earlier claim ("eg runs `./runtest` 11× vs baseline 7×") was computed on the *8 worst
losers* — a set selected on the outcome. Over-verification is what a losing session looks like in
*either* arm:

| group | eg runs/session | base runs/session |
|---|---|---|
| eg won (24) | 6.3 | 10.0 |
| eg lost (25) | 9.3 | 7.3 |
| 8 worst losers | 12.4 | 7.9 |

`corr(Δharness runs, tokens saved) = −0.612`, n=49. Verification looping *is* the loss mechanism,
but eg's defect is **variance, not tendency**. Excluding three blow-up sessions the arm runs
**327 vs 402**. This also answers the external objection directly: the baseline is not cheaper at
testing, and eg is not running more tests.

**2.3 — The biggest win is the baseline blowing up, not eg being efficient.**
`lombok-3674` (+6.09 pts, +71.0%) — baseline ran `javac` **70 times**, eg ran it 23. Same
mechanism as the losses, opposite arm. The headline is the difference of two blow-up processes
that hit either arm at roughly a coin flip: drag −19.86, lift +21.21, net +1.35.

---

## 3. The ceiling of loser repair, computed exactly

The drag pool is **−19.86 points** spread over 25 instances; the top five carry **−11.42 (57%)**.

> **If every losing instance were made exactly neutral, the headline would be +21.21%.**

That is not a projection — it is the sum of the lift pool. **Loser repair cannot reach 35%
by definition.** Reaching 35% additionally requires the *winners* to improve by ~65% beyond what
they already deliver.

And loser repair is not even available at full strength: **~93% of losing instances flip sign
between cells** (median same-instance swing 99.9 pts, max 294). "The 22 losers" is not a stable
target set; only a change applied to every instance can work.

---

## 4. Why three built capabilities changed nothing

| capability | where advertised | adoption |
|---|---|---|
| `impact` | affordance tail | **0 / 49** |
| `changed` (G1) | affordance tail | **0 / 5** |
| `--path` scoping (G3) | affordance tail | **0 / 12** |
| `search` | primary instruction | 33 / 49 |
| `grep` | primary instruction | 34 / 49 |
| `def` | primary instruction | 19 / 49 |

**Everything named in the primary instruction gets used. Everything in the tail gets ~zero.**
G3 is the cleanest read: adding two genuinely useful capabilities moved graph calls *up*
(1.9 → 3.1 per session) and displacement *down* (0.96 → 0.76). More calls, less removed.

**Consequence, and it is binding on everything below: any proposal that requires the agent to
choose to reach for something new has a measured 0/66 track record. Do not build a fourth.**

---

## 5. The route: attack the ratio's two sides separately

`eliminations per call = messages_removed / calls_made`. There are exactly two ways up.

### R-A — Drive the denominator to zero: zero-toll delivery *(fair, cheap, untested on this metric)*

The graph's 94 calls are 94 messages of pure overhead. The tool already implements free delivery:
`internal/cli/search.go` — *"ZERO-TOLL DELIVERY. When the caller has already computed this
session's payload and handed it to the agent inside context the session pays for anyway, this
call must cost nothing: echo those bytes and return."* (`opts.Env.PresearchPath`.)

Compute the payload from the issue text before the session starts and place it in turn 0.

- **Effect:** removes 94 messages outright = 3.5% of messages ≈ **+5.9% tokens**.
- **Risk:** prefetched retrieval is worse than the agent's own distilled query — gold-visible@5
  **0.567 vs 0.715**. If eliminations fall 103 → ~70, net becomes 70 vs today's 9.
- **Projected headline: +5% to +9%.**
- **Why it was previously dismissed, and why that was wrong:** prefetch was struck on *retrieval
  quality*. Under the message law retrieval quality is not the metric — message count is. A
  worse payload delivered for free can beat a better payload that costs a turn. This has never
  been measured on tokens.
- **Fairness:** payload, not instruction. It ships no advice; the no-tool arm cannot produce it.
  Same class as the search result itself. **Fair.**

### R-B — Drive the numerator up: answer the command the agent already types *(reaches 35%, but changes the claim)*

The agent types `grep` **409 times** across 49 sessions and `entire` 94 times. Adoption of the
graph is 1.9 calls/session; adoption of grep is 8.3.

**Put the graph behind `grep` itself** — a PATH shim in the eg arm that answers a grep with the
enclosing symbol, its complete body and its callers, instead of matching lines.

- **Zero adoption cost.** This is the only proposal on the table that does not require the agent
  to learn anything, and it is the only one whose ceiling contains 35%.
- **Effect if each shimmed grep removes one follow-up read/grep:** ~400 messages = 15% of
  messages ≈ **+25% tokens**. Combined with R-A: **+30% to +35%**.
- **Fairness — this is the decision, and it is genuinely close to the line.**
  - *For:* it is tool output. No instruction is added; the agent is told nothing. The baseline
    has real grep, the tool arm has a code-aware grep — the same class of difference as having
    `entire graph search` at all, and the same mechanism as the existing `entire` PATH shim.
  - *Against:* it silently redefines a standard command, so the two arms no longer run the same
    program. That is environment divergence rather than tool provision, and the doctrine polices
    exactly this boundary.
  - **My assessment: defensible under the letter of the doctrine, but it changes the claim from
    "a code graph saves tokens" to "replacing grep with a code-aware grep saves tokens."** That
    is a legitimate — arguably more interesting — product claim, but it is a different one, and
    any writeup must say which was measured. This is the same treatment the executing `verify`
    verb got, and for the same reason.
  - **Risk of it backfiring:** the agent uses grep for logs, build files and changelogs, not only
    code. A shim that mangles those responses sends it straight back to `/usr/bin/grep` and costs
    a turn. Must degrade to real grep whenever the pattern or path is not code-like.

### R-C — Static post-edit consistency check *(fair, blocked)*

New capability: re-parse the working tree, report unresolved references, arity mismatches and
renamed symbols with live callers — without running anything. Attacks the 576-run harness pool,
which is where the drag group loses (+84 runs).

**Blocked by §4.** It is post-edit, and 42/49 sessions make no post-edit graph call. The rider
(G2) already tried to solve exactly this and delivered **0/5**, measuring **−12.19%**. Do not
build this until a delivery channel exists that does not need agent initiative — which means a
harness hook, which means `CC_NO_SAFE_MODE`, which alters every future cell.

---

## 6. Struck — do not re-propose

Each was measured and killed. Re-proposing any of these has already cost real money.

1. Eleven payload-quality metrics (completeness, gold coverage, byte width, rank) — all 0.
2. Retrieval/ranking quality — **anti-correlated**: gold at rank 1 in losers 6/8 vs winners 2/5.
3. Session-length routing · language/repo gating · confidence gating (abstention worse).
4. Per-loser repair — +0.0 pt; losers are not stable (93% flip sign).
5. Locate-call reduction as a token lever — corr +0.188 over 10 cells.
6. Raising the turn cap — both arms grow proportionally.
7. `EG_VERIFY_MODE=noworld` — +35.1% **worse**.
8. Symmetric frugality clamp — modelled net-negative: in the winners it is the *baseline* that
   flails (lombok baseline `javac`×70 vs eg ×23), so a shared clamp hands savings to the baseline.
9. More graph calls — G3: 1.9 → 3.1 calls, displacement 0.96 → 0.76.
10. Any new verb in the affordance tail — 0/66 across three attempts.

---

## 7. Gates

Mechanism counts only below n≈30. MDE is ~25–30 pts against a ~100-pt same-instance noise floor,
so **no token claim may be made from a small cell in either direction** — a discipline G3
violated in spirit by moving −37.7 → +9.8 → −1.2 across three polls of the same cell.

| gate | what | n | pass criterion |
|---|---|---|---|
| **H0** | offline, $0 | 0 | shim answers all 409 recorded grep commands; degrades to real grep on non-code patterns; zero regressions on existing verbs |
| **H1** | replay, $0 | 409 | for each recorded grep, does the shim's answer contain what the agent went on to read next? Target ≥60% |
| **H2** | live, both arms | 12 | **eliminations per graph call ≥ 3.0** (from 1.10). Mechanism count, not tokens |
| **H3** | live, both arms | 30 | ≥ 5.0 per call; report Δturns and harness counts |
| **H4** | full rep50 | 49 | first token claim, with bootstrap CI, total **and** median |

**Kill criteria.** If H1 lands under 40%, R-B does not reach 35% — stop and ship R-A alone.
If H2 lands under 2.0, stop entirely: the ratio cannot be moved by tool output, and the honest
number is the fair ceiling in §8.

---

## 8. What is true regardless of which route is taken

- **Fair ceiling from loser repair alone: +21.21%** (exact, = the lift pool).
- **Best fair cell ever measured: +17.21%** (opus xhigh, n=26).
- **Current: +1.35%** (n=49), median −4.2%, wins 24/49.
- R-A alone: projected **+5% to +9%**, fair without qualification.
- R-A + R-B: projected **+30% to +35%**, but measures a different claim and must be labelled.

**35% is not reachable by any intervention that leaves the agent's exploration behaviour intact**,
because the graph currently removes 8.4% of exploration and 5.4% of harness runs, and adding
capability made both worse. The only lever with 35% inside its range is the one that intercepts
behaviour the agent already has, rather than offering behaviour it must adopt.

---

## 9. Open defects to fix before the next cell

1. **`EMPTY PAYLOAD` detector is broken** — fires on sessions holding 7,757 payload bytes and
   3 graph calls. Corrupts any uptake metric computed from it. Seen 3× in G3.
2. **Gate admits junk patches** — `carbon-2981` baseline patch was **371,308 bytes** (vendor or
   build output) and passed as success. Add a size/содержание sanity bound, symmetric.
3. **VMs A and B are spot instances and were preempted**, freezing Gemini 300 at n=207 and
   leaving 52 rep30 sessions unfinished. Move long cells to non-preemptible (E/F) or checkpoint.
4. **`.entire/graph-agent.md` fairness landmine** — carries arm-asymmetric methodology and is
   `@`-included into `CLAUDE.md`. It did *not* leak into rep50 (`--safe-mode`, 0 injected files
   verified in both arms), but any cell run without `--safe-mode` is invalid on arrival. Add an
   explicit preflight assertion rather than relying on the flag.

SHELL=("grep","rg","ls","sed","cat","find","head","tail","awk")

    out=[]
    for cj in glob.glob(f"results/{tag}/{arm}/*/cc_out.json"):
        try: j=json.load(open(cj))
        except: continue
        if j.get("subtype")!="success": continue
        p=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(cj),"patch.diff")
        if not(os.path.exists(p) and os.path.getsize(p)>0): continue
        tf=IDX.get(j.get("session_id"))
        if not tf: continue
        calls=[]; res={}
        for line in open(tf,errors="ignore"):
            try: m=json.loads(line)
            except: continue
            msg=m.get("message") or {}
            if msg.get("role")=="assistant":
                for b in (msg.get("content") or []):
                    if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_use":
                        calls.append((b.get("id"),b.get("name"),(b.get("input") or {})))
            elif msg.get("role")=="user":
                for b in (msg.get("content") or []):
                    if isinstance(b,dict) and b.get("type")=="tool_result":
                        t=b.get("content")
                        if isinstance(t,list): t=" ".join(x.get("text","") for x in t if isinstance(x,dict))
                        res[b.get("tool_use_id")]=(t or "")[:20000]

PATH_RX=re.compile(r'([A-Za-z0-9_./\-]+\.(?:py|go|rb|php|rs|js|ts|tsx|java|c|cc|cpp|h|hpp|tcl|scala|kt|cs|swift))')
def analyse(sessions,lbl):
    nxt=collections.Counter(); tot=0; covered=0; grep_ret=collections.Counter()
    for calls,res in sessions:
        for i,(cid,name,inp) in enumerate(calls):
            if name!="Bash": continue
            cmd=(inp.get("command") or "").strip()
            h=os.path.basename(cmd.split()[0]) if cmd.split() else ""
            if h not in ("grep","rg"): continue
            tot+=1
            out=res.get(cid,"")
            files=set(PATH_RX.findall(out))
            grep_ret["files_"+("0" if not files else "1" if len(files)==1 else "2-5" if len(files)<=5 else "6+")]+=1

                if any(f in fp or fp.endswith(f) for f in files): covered+=1; nxt["Read-in-grep-output"]+=1
            elif n2 in ("Edit","Write","MultiEdit"):
                fp=str(i2.get("file_path",""))
                nxt["Edit"]+=1
                if any(f in fp or fp.endswith(f) for f in files): covered+=1; nxt["Edit-in-grep-output"]+=1
            elif n2=="Bash":
                c2=(i2.get("command") or "").strip()
                h2=os.path.basename(c2.split()[0]) if c2.split() else ""

Confounds checked — and the result strengthens rather than dissolves:

**1. Non-users are not easier instances.** Their baselines are *more expensive* (3.11M vs 2.31M median) and longer (61 vs 51 turns), identical shell counts. Since expensive baselines are known to *favour* eg (`corr = +0.305`), the confound runs against the effect.

**2. It holds inside every cost tercile:**

| tercile | uses `eg-q grep` | never uses | gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| cheap | −25.41% | −55.09% | 30 pts |
| mid | +5.78% | −17.93% | 24 pts |
| expensive | +18.16% | −7.09% | 25 pts |

**3. And it isolates to *which* verb — this is the new finding:**

| group | n | TOKEN | shell eliminated |
|---|---|---|---|
| any graph call | 46 | +0.64% | +10.3% |
| **`search` only, no grep** | 12 | **−15.72%** | **−7.3%** |
| `def` used | 19 | **+6.94%** | **+19.3%** |
| `grep` used | 34 | +8.38% | +15.9% |

`corr(eg-q grep calls, shell elimination) = +0.304`.

**Search-only sessions are the worst group in the cell** — they cost a turn and the agent explores *more* afterwards. The verbs that answer a *specific* question (`def <Symbol>`, `grep <literal>`) displace shell work; the verb that answers a *vague* one does not.

That contradicts the shipped doctrine, which makes `search` the mandatory first action (`.entire/graph-agent.md`: *"Your FIRST action must be ONE search"*). Changing which verb leads is a capability statement, not a frugality instruction — a no-tool arm can't invoke `def` either — so it's fair.

**Remaining confound, and it's the serious one:** using `def`/`grep` requires the issue to *name* a symbol. That's the ledger's live MOD-vs-ADD hypothesis — verb choice may be a *marker* of tractable tasks rather than a cause. Testing that now, since it decides whether this is a lever or a thermometer.

Found something material — the zero-toll implementation carries its own measurement base, from **178 pairs**, and it corrects my R-A estimate upward while dissolving the risk I flagged:

|---|---|
| graph calls per session are **invariant** (1.00 / 1.03 / 1.00 across exploration bands) | you cannot get more value by inducing more calls — consistent with G3 |
