# entire-graph on Opus — the final plan

## Context

The original goal was **35% token savings on rep50, on Opus, fairly measured**. That is refuted
and the reasons are in §1. You then relaxed it to the right target: **make the losers behave like
winners — a code graph should not make instances worse.** That is what this plan is built against.

The decisive discovery came last: **this is not an invention problem.** There are ~2,500 LOC of
measured, shipped, **default-off** capability in the tool, a `verify` verb documented nowhere, a
`changed` verb missing from `--help`, an `edges` filter the shipped guide says does not exist, and
a `capabilities` report that under-declares its own heuristics by ~20 relations. Every one was
built after a measurement and then never wired up.

**The bottleneck is the last 10 metres — defaults and the agent-facing guide.**

All numbers: rep50, Opus/max, 49 gated pairs. Sign: **positive = graph arm saved tokens.**

---

## 1. Where Opus actually stands

| estimator | value |
|---|---|
| total (the reported headline) | **+1.35%** |
| **leave-one-out: drop `lombok-3674`** | **−5.18%** |
| median | **−4.16%** |
| 10% trimmed mean | **−7.65%** |
| t-statistic | **−0.17 — indistinguishable from zero** |
| n to demonstrate +1.35% | 12,900 pairs ≈ $78k |
| n to demonstrate 35% | **11 pairs ≈ $88** |

**The headline is one instance.** Every robust estimator says eg loses. And 35% would have been
the cheapest result in the project to prove — it is not provable because it is not there.

**Do not quote +1.35% without the LOO range and the median.**

---

## 2. Why instances lose — three mechanisms, all measured

**Drag −19.86 pts over 25 instances (top five = −11.42, 57%). Lift +21.21 over 24.
`lombok-3674` alone is +6.09 = 29% of all lift.**

### 2.1 The call is paid for and removes nothing
Losers: eg shell exploration **413 vs baseline 415** — two calls displaced out of 415.
Winners: 370 vs 440. One graph call prices at **1.61 messages**, and a regression holding call
count fixed charges **+7.0% CI[1.9,13.2]** for merely having called.

### 2.2 ADD tasks get a confident wrong answer
Search always returns something. When the task is to *add* behaviour, the top hit is a plausible
sibling of the answer.

| | pooled |
|---|---|
| MOD (fix existing broken code) | **+14.35%** (n=36) |
| ADD (behaviour does not exist) | **−3.37%** (n=21) |

Same sign **4/4 cells**. Corroborated: gold at rank 2–3 measures **−85.3%**, *worse* than gold not
found at all (−25.6%). Forensics confirmed both `ansible-395e` and `prometheus-9248` are ADD, and
**80% / 64% of their surplus is PRE-edit** — the graph bled where it operates.

### 2.3 The verify-repair spiral, where the tool is absent
**91 of 94 graph calls are pre-edit; 42/49 sessions never call it again**, yet 97.7% of excess
cost lands after the first edit. Losers vs baseline: env-failures **+22**, throwaway scripts
**+16**, post-edit harness **+50**, post-edit exploration **+159**. Winners mirror it exactly
(−45, −48, −88, −81). `corr(Δharness, saving) = −0.612`; `corr(Δenv-failures) = −0.442`.

---

## 3. The economics that constrain every fix

`cache_read` is **95.5%** of billed tokens. A result injected at turn *i* is re-charged on every
later turn: cost ≈ `(bytes/4) × turns-remaining` — **~5 persist-tokens per byte** at 20 turns left.

**One default search payload is 10,822 B ≈ 54k persist ≈ 0.55 of the whole-file Read it replaces.**
That single number *is* the context-neutrality result (eg 38.5M vs baseline 38.6M).

| class | baseline share | calls | each |
|---|---|---|---|
| exploration | 45.1% | 1,206 | 14k |
| **whole-file `Read`** | **30.3%** | **119** | **98k (7×)** |
| harness | 11.2% | 576 | 7k |

**Break-even:** a block ≤2.8 KB pays for itself if it removes one grep/session; ≤19.6 KB if it
removes one whole-file Read; ≤1.4 KB if it removes one harness run.

**Corollary: bytes delivered at turn 1 are charged N times.** The tool spends its whole budget at
its most expensive moment and is absent from the phase where the money goes.

---

## 4. The plan — remove bytes and fix defaults, in this order

Every item is **tool output, not instruction**, and passes the no-tool-arm test. Ranked by
(turns removed) / (bytes added). **Items 4.1–4.4 all reduce or barely move payload size** — the
first proposals in this project with a positive byte ratio.

### 4.1 Fix `graph grep`: exclude vendored / minified / generated files *(NEGATIVE bytes)*
`internal/cli` grep path shells out to `grep -rInE` over the whole worktree and filters **only
tests**. On `prometheus-9248` it returned one hit inside minified vendored `d3.v3.js` where plain
grep returned a **clean zero** — and a clean zero is *actionable* ("pivot"), one noise hit is not.
Baseline pivoted to the issue's error string at call 2 and found `scalarBinop`; eg reached it at
calls 21–22. **~19 turns of delay, caused by the tool's opening answer.**

This is the only place measured where the graph is **demonstrably worse than no tool at all**, and
the fix removes bytes.

### 4.2 Ship FILE OUTLINE by default *(+1,421 B, ~8× return — best ratio of anything built)*
`internal/sem/search_outline.go` (217 LOC), flag `internal/cli/search.go:1637`. **Default OFF,
absent from `printHelp`.** Its own measurement: **77 targeted greps landed on a file the payload
had already named; 35 were immediately followed by a Read of that same file**, landing a median
109 lines from anything printed. Measured cost +1,421 B ≈ 7.1k persist against ~57k saved.

### 4.3 Cut complete bodies from rank 5 to rank 2 *(−76% payload bytes)*
`search_enclosure.go:41` (`searchEnclosureHeadRanks = 5`). Act-rate data in `search_outline.go:22`:
rank 1 read 62% / edited 54%; rank 2 27%/20%; **rank 3+ 0–11%.** Measured: `--body-head-ranks`
5→3 = 10,822→6,143 B; **5→2 = 10,822→2,590 B (−76%)**. Ranks 3–5 pay full persist for a ≤11% read
rate. Net is close (−41k certain saving vs ~29k probabilistic extra reads) but the saving is the
certain half.

### 4.4 Probe the VERIFY command instead of `LookPath` *(NEGATIVE bytes)*
`internal/sem/search_verify.go:135` checks only that the runner *binary exists* — `npx` exists,
so the command prints, then fails because deps were never installed. Replace with a collect-only
probe on the pristine tree (`pytest --collect-only -q`, `go test -run XXX -count=0`,
`cargo test --no-run`, `phpunit --list-tests`, `rspec --dry-run`); on failure **strip the block**.

Measured swing on this exact axis (rep30, baseline-matched): `VERIFY real` **+4.6 turns / +37.1%
USD**; `VERIFY runner-absent` **−6.0 turns / −11.8%**; no VERIFY line −4.7 turns. **An 11.4-turn
swing.** The previous response was to silence VERIFY entirely, which also discarded the good case.
A probe keeps the good case and kills the bad one.

**Note:** this makes the provider *execute* something for the first time. That is a real product
decision — latency, and a category change — and it should be taken deliberately.

### 4.5 Example-level VERIFY granularity *(+15 B, reaches 62% of the corpus)*
`search_covertest.go` already selects **exactly one** test method and its line, then the deriver
throws the name away for 5 of 8 ecosystems: Ruby, PHP, JS file-only; Java/Gradle class-only.
Python (`-k`), Go (`-run '^Name$'`) and Rust already do it right. Fix: emit
`rspec spec/foo_spec.rb:412`, `phpunit --filter testX`, `jest -t "…"`, `mvn -Dtest=Class#method`.
Targets Ruby 39 + PHP 32 + JS 23 + TS 8 + Java 31 = **133/213 instances**.

### 4.6 Ship R-A zero-toll delivery *(built, gated, deployed as `b669a57b`)*
`EG_PREFETCH=1` injected the payload at turn 0 and still let the agent re-derive it at full price.
`EG_PRESEARCH` makes the residual call an echo — 0.02 s vs 5.21 s, byte-identical.
Counterfactual on this cell **+4.3% to +6.0%** (CI spans zero at n=49).

### 4.7 Documentation and defaults that are simply wrong *(zero bytes)*
- `search` defaults to `--profile fast` (**9/30 relations**) while both agent guides mandate `full`.
  Under the default, TESTS, SIMILAR_TO, DATA_FLOWS, FILE_CHANGES_WITH and every type relation are
  **structurally empty**, so blocks depending on them cannot fire. `neighbors`/`impact` default to
  `full`; `search` is the odd one out.
- `AGENTS.md:72` states `edges --to/--from/--relation` **does not exist**. It does
  (`root.go:576-594`) — and it is the only route to 13 relation types. Delete that sentence.
- `capabilities --json` declares **7** heuristic relations; by the code **~27 of 30** are
  text-pattern derived, including **CALLS (35% of all edges), which is a regex name-set, not an
  AST call-site set.** Doctrine rule 7 says "feature-detect before you trust" — it is being fed a
  wrong answer.
- `TESTS` ships in the relation list at **10 edges of 36,354 on Go and 0 of 89,587 on a Python repo
  that has a pytest suite.** Either fix it (§4.8) or stop advertising it.
- `verify` and `changed` are in neither agent guide; `changed` is absent from `printHelp`.
- **The in-tree binary is stale vs source** — it rejects `verify`, `changed`, `--path`.
  Rebuild before anything ships.

### 4.8 TESTS from call-reachability rather than spelling *(zero payload bytes)*
`types.go:280-297` maps `TestFoo→Foo` by name only. Emit TESTS where a symbol in a test file
reaches the target within **≤2 CALLS hops**, restricted to ranked files. Uses edges that already
exist (12.6k–21.1k CALLS). CALLS is supported for Ruby/PHP/JS/TS/Python, so this is one of the few
upgrades that lands on the dynamic ~48% of the corpus. It is also the input to §4.4 and §4.5.

### 4.9 DO NOT BUILD
- **Post-edit consistency hook.** Stress-tested and rejected: its fair (symmetric) form's biggest
  beneficiary is the **baseline in `lombok-3674`**, i.e. it eats 29% of the lift. Cost −2% to −6%.
- Any new verb in the affordance tail — **0/66 adoption** measured.
- Anything requiring an agent-initiated post-edit call — 42/49 sessions make none.
- Better ranking; bigger payloads; graph-backed grep; the 12 dead payload metrics.

---

## 5. Integrity fixes — before any cell

1. **Sibling-checkout answer leak.** `bat-1892` (the worst loser, −2.81 pts) made **12 references
   into `bat-3108`, a later revision of the same repo containing the implemented feature.**
   Measured exposure: **2/49 eg sessions, 0/49 baseline** — small but **arm-asymmetric**. Fence
   checkouts so a session cannot read a sibling instance's tree.
2. **Shared `/tmp` between concurrent cells.** `prometheus-9248` found `/tmp/goyacc*` built by
   *other instances'* sessions and spent 2 calls auditing foreign binaries. eg 3/49, base 1/49.
   Give each session a private temp root.
3. **Junk-patch gate.** One baseline patch was 371,308 B of vendor/build output and passed as
   success. Add a symmetric size/content bound.
4. **`EMPTY PAYLOAD` detector is broken** — fires on sessions holding 7,757 payload bytes.
   Fix before any payload forensics.
5. **0-byte `cc_out.json`** — guard shipped; the sweep removed **90 corpses** across all cells.

**Validated clean:** 49/49 graphs present, **0 commit mismatches**, 0 of 310 under 50 KB, caches
small, prompt diff is 18 lines all of which are checkout paths.

---

## 6. Gates — mechanism counts, winners protected

MDE is ~25–30 pts against a ~100-pt same-instance noise floor; 93% of losers flip sign between
cells. **No token claim below n≈50, in either direction.**

| gate | n | criterion |
|---|---|---|
| **V0** offline, $0 | 0 | `mise run check` green; grep excludes vendored/minified on the prometheus query and returns a clean zero; outline/body-rank byte deltas reproduce (10,822 → 2,590 B) |
| **V1** replay, $0 | 49 | on recorded loser sessions, the probed VERIFY command would have run where the emitted one failed; ≥50% of the 22 env-failures avoided |
| **V2** live | 12 | mechanism only: payload bytes/session **down**, env-failures/session **down**, no rise in whole-file Reads. **No token claim.** |
| **V3** live | 50 | first token claim: bootstrap CI, and **total + median + trimmed + LOO reported together** |

**Winner-protection tripwire (per your instruction, abort at >10pt):** `lombok-3674`, `fmt-2457`,
`qutebrowser-c580`, `redis-11510` are in every sample from V2 on. If any regresses >10pt versus a
**same-wave** control, revert. Never compare against a previous cell — the noise floor forbids it.

---

## 7. Honest expected outcome

| item | effect | confidence |
|---|---|---|
| 4.1 grep vendor filter | removes a ~19-turn failure mode on ADD tasks | high — mechanism observed |
| 4.2 FILE OUTLINE default | ~8× return on 1,421 B | high — own measurement |
| 4.3 bodies rank 5→2 | −76% payload bytes | high on cost, medium on net |
| 4.4 VERIFY probe | up to 11.4-turn swing on that axis | medium |
| 4.5 VERIFY granularity | 133/213 instances | medium |
| 4.6 R-A zero-toll | +4.3% to +6.0% | medium, CI spans zero |

**Combined, realistically: high single digits to low teens, with the drag pool shrinking rather
than the lift pool growing.** The ceiling on loser repair is exactly **+21.21%** (the lift pool) —
arithmetic, not projection.

**35% is not reachable on Opus by any fair change.** The one intervention that would reach it is
an instruction telling the agent to explore and re-test less — which helps a no-tool arm equally
and is precisely what the withdrawn −35% contained.

**If §4.4 (executing a probe) is refused,** the honest recommendation is to stop optimising tokens
here: remove bytes (4.1–4.3, 4.7), and position entire-graph on correctness and latency, where it
is demonstrably good. It is not, on this corpus and this cost model, a token tool.

---

## 8. Verification

- `cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph && mise run check` (fmt + vet + race + build; CGO needed).
  **Rebuild the in-tree binary — it is stale.** Add unit tests beside `search_verify.go` and the
  grep filter.
- Offline replay: recorded queries at `results/<tag>/eg/<iid>/gq_calls.log`, payloads at the same
  path + `.payload`. Re-run against the binary at zero model cost; assert both that the change
  fires and that nothing else moved.
- Harness deploys to VMs by temp path + atomic `mv` with a live-session guard — never overwrite a
  script a running session is reading.
- Every gate reports total **and** median **and** trimmed **and** LOO **and** Δturns **and**
  env-failure counts.

---

# APPENDIX A — Subagent findings log

## A1 — Post-edit hook stress test — **REJECTED**
Fair (symmetric) form's biggest beneficiary is the baseline in `lombok-3674` = 29% of all lift;
cost −2% to −6%; ~48% of corpus is dynamically typed where arity checks are unreliable.
Also surfaced: `claude --settings '<json>' --setting-sources ''` avoids writing
`.claude/settings.json` into the worktree, removing the patch-pollution blocker.

## A2 — Loser forensics: `bat-1892`, `valkey-790` — **graph INNOCENT**
Payload was correct in both; top hit was the exact function to edit; eg used *fewer* localization
calls than baseline (10 vs 15; 15 vs 17). Losses were environment, answer-leak and a hung pty test.
`valkey`: ~13–15 pre-edit calls were graph-shaped (test invocation, tcl `proc` sites — **no `.tcl`
symbols are indexed**).

## A3 — Loser forensics: `ansible-395e`, `prometheus-9248` — **graph GUILTY on prometheus**
Both ADD tasks; 80%/64% of surplus is PRE-edit. `graph grep` returned a minified-vendor false
positive where plain grep returned a clean zero → ~19 turns of delay. `ansible` innocent
(environment). **`EG_LITERALS` — the error-string→symbol index that would have collapsed
prometheus's delay — is built and was switched OFF in this cell.**

## A4 — Capability inventory — **the decisive result**
~2,500 LOC shipped default-off; `verify`/`changed`/`def` undocumented; `AGENTS.md:72` denies a
real feature; `capabilities` under-declares heuristics 7 vs ~27; **CALLS is a regex name-set, not
AST**; TESTS 10/36,354 on Go and **0/89,587 on a Python repo with pytest**; Ruby 5/30 relations,
C 4/30 (61/213 instances where the graph is barely a symbol index).

## A5 — Claims I made and then RETRACTED
- "eg verifies more than baseline" — **false**, eg 545 vs base 576. Came from the 8 worst losers,
  a set selected on the outcome.
- "eg loses 14.49% when both arms build" — **regex artifact**; stricter definition gives n=17 and
  **−0.89%**.
- "the metric rewards failing to provision" — real on `bat-1892`, but only **2/25 losers**, worth
  −1.06 pts. Refuted as a driver.
- "+35.06% is reachable by loser repair" — arithmetic artifact; the lift pool caps it at +21.21%.
- ×0.54 persist calibration — wrong; the validated figure is the regression **slope 0.822**
  (corr +0.916, R² 0.839).

content.text:
That workflow is the most consequential yet — **all three proposals killed**, and it invalidates two sections of the plan I just wrote. The findings:

## R-A (my leading lever) — mispriced by 5.2×

The first graph search lands at **assistant turn 2 of a median 85-turn session**, where `cache_read` is **12,231 tokens against a session mean of 63,137**. The call is the *cheapest message in the session*. My +4.3–6.0% priced the removed message at session-mean cost.

| | |
|---|---|
| my estimate | +4.3% to +6.0% |
| **corrected** | **+0.96%**, CI [+0.53, +1.38] |
| n to demonstrate it | **19,504 pairs** |

Worse — it's aimed the wrong way. Only 33/49 sessions call `search`; the other **16 never do, and those are the losing cohort** (non-callers pooled −1.02%, median −24.94%; callers **+6.30%**, median +12.61%). Universal injection charges the non-callers ~45k tokens for nothing.

**`displace & win` = 19/21 (90.5%); `no-displace & win` = 6/28 (21.4%), AUC 0.838.** Calling is the *winning* behaviour. R-A removes the call in exactly the cohort where calling works.

It also found two genuine bugs: `echoPresearchPayload` has **no length check** (zero-byte payload → 0 bytes, exit 0 — the "announced but never shipped" failure), and the echo is **query-blind and header-less**, so any later search returns the turn-0 payload verbatim — an absorbing state.

## ADD tasks — real, and far bigger than I said

An independent gold-patch labeller: **gold-MOD n=36 +13.59%; gold-ADD n=13 −23.19%** (median −18.03%). **Gold-ADD is 8 of the 25 drag instances and −10.68 of the −19.86 drag points — 54% of all drag.**

But the fix is refuted: the structural signal ("does the issue name a symbol that resolves") was tested offline and doesn't separate, and the `exact-symbol` signal is *already printed to the agent* with rank-1 exactness identical on ADD and MOD (0.36 vs 0.36). And **GEM300 inverts the effect** (MOD −14.13%, ADD +0.86%), so it isn't universal.

## VERIFY probe — already shipped and already on

`run_REP50.sh:141` sets `EG_VERIFY_PROBE=1`. It was on in rep50. And **21 of 25 losers got no VERIFY line at all**, so it's a no-op on 84% of the drag.

---

My plan's §4.4 and §4.6 are now wrong, and §2.2's sizing was understated. I'm not rewriting it until the last audit lands — that one is specifically tasked with finding errors in my documents, and on this evidence it will find more.

const BASE = `

Caveman-ultra compressed output. Numbers and file:line. Use RTK where it saves tokens.

entire-graph: local deterministic code-graph CLI (Go, tree-sitter). Benchmarked vs a no-tool
baseline on SWE-bench Multilingual through Claude Code. Metric: tokens.
Sign: POSITIVE = graph arm SAVED tokens.

=== THE OBJECTIVE (this is what you are optimising, not "tokens" in the abstract) ===
Measured on rep50 (49 gated pairs, Opus): DISPLACEMENT is the discriminator.
  label a session "displaced" if eg's shell-exploration call count < its paired baseline's.
    displaced & won  = 19/21  (90.5%)
    not-displaced & won = 6/28 (21.4%)
    AUC(no-displacement -> loss) = 0.838
  Sessions that CALL the graph: pooled +6.30%, median +12.61%.
  Sessions that never call it (16/49): pooled -1.02%, median -24.94%.
  => CALLING AND DISPLACING IS THE WINNING BEHAVIOUR. The goal is to raise the fraction of
     sessions that displace, WITHOUT adding payload bytes and WITHOUT an instruction.

=== HEADLINE STATE ===
total +1.35% | median -4.16% | 10% trimmed -7.65% | t=-0.17 | LOO drop lombok-3674 -> -5.18%
drag -19.86 pts over 25 instances; lift +21.21 over 24; lombok-3674 alone +6.09 (29% of lift).

gold-MOD n=36: +13.59% (median +12.67%)
gold-ADD n=13: -23.19% (median -18.03%)

=== COST MODEL ===
cache_read = 94.6-95.5% of billed tokens. A result at turn i is re-charged every later turn:
cost ~ (bytes/4) x turns-remaining. BUT turn cost is NOT uniform: the first graph search lands at
assistant turn median 2 of a median 85-turn session, where cache_read is 12,231 tokens vs the

One default search payload = 10,822 B ~ 54k persist ~ 0.55 of the whole-file Read it replaces.
Baseline cost by class: exploration 45.1% (1,206 calls x 14k), whole-file Read 30.3% (119 x 98k),

=== KILLED THIS WEEK — do not re-propose, and do not propose anything that reduces to these ===
- R-A zero-toll pre-delivery: repriced +0.96% CI[+0.53,+1.38] (was +4.3-6.0%, a 5.2x overcharge

  never call search ARE the losing cohort, and universal injection charges them ~45k for nothing.

- Post-edit consistency hook: its fair symmetric form's biggest beneficiary is the BASELINE in

- New verb in the prompt's affordance tail: 0/66 adoption (impact 0/49, changed 0/5, --path 0/12).
- Anything needing an agent-initiated POST-EDIT call: 42/49 sessions make none.
- Better ranking (gold-at-rank-1 sessions LOST more often); bigger payloads; graph-backed grep

  frugality clamp (helps the baseline more in exactly the instances eg wins).

=== CONFIRMED, UNEXPLOITED, AND CHEAP (these are real and nobody has shipped them) ===
1. `graph grep` has NO vendor/minified/generated filtering — it shells to `grep -rInE` over the
   worktree and filters ONLY tests. On prometheus-9248 it returned one hit inside minified
   vendored d3.v3.js where plain grep returned a CLEAN ZERO. A clean zero is actionable; one

   any new symbol returns the turn-0 payload verbatim with no indication it answered a different

6. search defaults to --profile fast (9/30 relations) while both agent guides mandate full; under

8. AGENTS.md:72 states `edges --to/--from/--relation` does not exist. It does (root.go:576-594),

9. capabilities --json declares 7 heuristic relations; by the code ~27 of 30 are text-pattern
   derived, INCLUDING CALLS (35% of all edges) which is a regex name-set, not AST call sites.
10. The in-tree binary is STALE vs source (rejects verify, changed, --path). Rebuild before ship.

=== FAIRNESS (binding) ===

Test: "would this sentence or change help an arm with NO tool?" yes -> both arms or neither.

=== NOISE FLOOR ===

const TRACKS = [
  { key: 'bytes', brief: `TRACK A — REMOVE BYTES WITHOUT LOSING ANSWERS.
Items 1,2,3,6 in the CONFIRMED list are byte-level changes with measured act-rates. Design the
combined change: grep vendor/minified exclusion + FILE OUTLINE default + body ranks 5->2 +
the profile default. Price the NET byte delta and the NET persist delta, and say which of the
1,206 baseline exploration calls or 119 whole-file Reads specifically stop happening.` },
  { key: 'displace', brief: `TRACK B — RAISE THE DISPLACEMENT RATE.
19/21 displaced sessions won; 6/28 non-displaced won; AUC 0.838. 16/49 sessions never call the
graph at all and they are the losing cohort. Design a change that makes MORE sessions displace.
Constraints: no new verb (0/66), no instruction, no post-edit agent call. You may change what
EXISTING verbs return, what the DEFAULT behaviour is, or how the harness exposes the tool —
provided it is output/capability, not advice.` },
  { key: 'add', brief: `TRACK C — THE ADD-TASK DRAG (54% of all drag, 8 instances, -10.68 pts).
The router and the abstention affordance are both refuted (see KILLED). exact-symbol is already
printed and does not separate (0.36 vs 0.36). GEM300 inverts the MOD/ADD sign. Given all that:
is there ANY tool-output change that reduces the ADD penalty, or is the honest answer that the
penalty is a property of the task and the correct action is to STOP claiming the tool helps on
ADD tasks? Argue it out and commit to one.` },
]

const SPEC = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['track', 'proposal', 'mechanism', 'net_bytes', 'expected_low', 'expected_high', 'fair', 'survives_known_kills'],
  properties: {
    track: { type: 'string' },
    proposal: { type: 'string', description: 'Concrete change with file:line' },
    mechanism: { type: 'string', description: 'Which specific calls stop happening, and why' },
    net_bytes: { type: 'number', description: 'Net payload byte delta, negative is good' },
    expected_low: { type: 'number' },
    expected_high: { type: 'number' },
    fair: { type: 'boolean' },
    fairness_argument: { type: 'string' },
    survives_known_kills: { type: 'string', description: 'Explicitly: why this is not a restatement of any KILLED item' },
    offline_test: { type: 'string', description: 'The $0 test that would confirm or kill it' },
  },
}

const VERDICT = {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['refuted', 'reason'],
  properties: {
    refuted: { type: 'boolean' },
    reason: { type: 'string' },
    what_would_fix_it: { type: 'string', description: 'If refuted: the specific change that would make it survive, or "nothing" if unsalvageable' },
  },
}

function refute(spec, round) {
  return parallel([
    () => agent(`${BASE}\n\nROUND ${round} PROPOSAL:\n${JSON.stringify(spec, null, 1)}\n\n` +
      `REFUTE ON MECHANISM AND COST. eg is context-neutral — no slack. Price every added byte at ` +
      `(bytes/4) x turns-remaining, and remember early turns are CHEAP (turn 2 = 12,231 cache_read ` +
      `vs 63,137 session mean). Can you trace the specific calls that stop happening? Twelve ` +
      `payload-quality levers died by changing content without changing behaviour. ` +
      `If refuted, you MUST say what specific change would make it survive, or "nothing".`,
      { label: `r${round}-cost:${spec.track}`, phase: `Round${round}`, schema: VERDICT, effort: 'high' }),
    () => agent(`${BASE}\n\nROUND ${round} PROPOSAL:\n${JSON.stringify(spec, null, 1)}\n\n` +
      `REFUTE ON FAIRNESS AND WINNER REGRESSION. Apply the no-tool-arm test literally, and look for ` +
      `DISGUISED instructions. Then: winners win by converging, and lombok-3674 alone is 29% of all ` +
      `lift where the BASELINE ran javac 70x vs eg 23x. Could this help the baseline more than eg, ` +
      `or make winners do more? If refuted, say what change would make it survive, or "nothing".`,
      { label: `r${round}-fair:${spec.track}`, phase: `Round${round}`, schema: VERDICT, effort: 'high' }),
    () => agent(`${BASE}\n\nROUND ${round} PROPOSAL:\n${JSON.stringify(spec, null, 1)}\n\n` +
      `REFUTE ON PRIOR ART AND MEASURABILITY. Open TokensNotes.md and the harness runners and check ` +
      `whether this is ALREADY SHIPPED or ALREADY ON — EG_VERIFY_PROBE was already set in ` +
      `run_REP50.sh:141 and that killed a whole proposal last round. Then: is the effect bigger than ` +
      `the ~100pt same-instance noise floor, and what n demonstrates it? ` +
      `If refuted, say what change would make it survive, or "nothing".`,
      { label: `r${round}-prior:${spec.track}`, phase: `Round${round}`, schema: VERDICT, effort: 'high' }),
  ]).then((votes) => {
    const live = votes.filter(Boolean)
    const kills = live.filter((v) => v.refuted)
    return {
      survives: live.length > 0 && kills.length < 2,
      kills: kills.length,
      reasons: kills.map((v) => v.reason),
      fixes: kills.map((v) => v.what_would_fix_it).filter((x) => x && x !== 'nothing'),
      unsalvageable: kills.length >= 2 && kills.every((v) => !v.what_would_fix_it || v.what_would_fix_it === 'nothing'),
    }
  })
}

// Three rounds: propose -> refute -> REVISE USING THE REFUTATION -> refute -> revise -> final.
const results = await pipeline(
  TRACKS,
  async (t) => {
    let spec = await agent(`${BASE}\n\n${t.brief}\n\nPropose ONE concrete change. It must survive the ` +
      `KILLED list — say explicitly why it is not a restatement of any of them.`,
      { label: `propose:${t.key}`, phase: 'Round1', schema: SPEC, effort: 'high' })
    if (!spec) return null
    let history = []
    for (let round = 1; round <= 3; round++) {
      const v = await refute(spec, round)
      history.push({ round, kills: v.kills, reasons: v.reasons })
      if (v.survives) return { track: t.key, spec, survived_at_round: round, history }
      if (v.unsalvageable || round === 3) return { track: t.key, spec, survived_at_round: null, history, dead: true }
      // REVISE using why it died — this is what the previous workflow lacked
      const revised = await agent(`${BASE}\n\n${t.brief}\n\nYour previous proposal was REFUTED.\n\n` +
        `PROPOSAL:\n${JSON.stringify(spec, null, 1)}\n\n` +
        `WHY IT WAS KILLED:\n${v.reasons.map((r, i) => `(${i + 1}) ${r}`).join('\n\n')}\n\n` +
        `SUGGESTED REPAIRS FROM THE REFUTERS:\n${v.fixes.join('\n') || '(none offered)'}\n\n` +
        `Produce a REVISED proposal that specifically answers every refutation above. If the ` +
        `refutations are correct and the idea is unsalvageable, say so in `proposal` beginning ` +
        `with "ABANDON:" and propose the best remaining alternative on this track instead.`,
        { label: `revise${round}:${t.key}`, phase: `Round${round + 1}`, schema: SPEC, effort: 'high' })
      if (!revised) return { track: t.key, spec, survived_at_round: null, history, dead: true }
      spec = revised
    }
    return { track: t.key, spec, survived_at_round: null, history, dead: true }
  },
)

const all = results.filter(Boolean)
const survivors = all.filter((r) => r.survived_at_round)
log(`${survivors.length}/${all.length} tracks produced a surviving proposal`)

phase('Ship')

const ship = await agent(
  `${BASE}\n\n` +
  `Three tracks each ran up to 3 rounds of propose -> adversarial refute -> revise-using-the-refutation.\n\n` +
  `RESULTS:\n${JSON.stringify(all, null, 1)}\n\n` +
  `Write the shipping decision. For each SURVIVING proposal: exact files and functions with ` +
  `file:line, the change stated precisely enough to implement, the $0 offline test that must pass ` +
  `first, honest expected effect WITH an interval, the n required to demonstrate it, and the ` +
  `fairness argument.\n\n` +
  `For each DEAD track: state plainly that it is dead and why, so nobody retries it.\n\n` +
  `Then answer the user's actual question: does the surviving set reduce the -19.86 pt drag pool, ` +
  `and by roughly how much? If the honest answer is "not measurably", say that. Do not manufacture ` +
  `a number. Note explicitly that the gold-ADD cohort is 54% of the drag and whether anything here ` +
  `touches it.`,
  { label: 'ship-decision', phase: 'Ship', effort: 'high' },
)

return { survivors: survivors.length, tracks: all.map((r) => ({ track: r.track, survived_at_round: r.survived_at_round, dead: !!r.dead })), ship }

**No — and the data is unusually clean about it.**

**By language, R² = 0.153** — language explains 15% of the variance, and the groups contradict themselves:

| lang | n | TOTAL | median | wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Java | 5 | **+29.64%** | **−30.18%** | **1/5** |
| C | 6 | +10.15% | +46.18% | 3/6 |
| Ruby | 6 | +22.83% | +24.50% | **6/6** |
| Rust | 5 | −42.58% | −33.52% | 2/5 |
| Python | 10 | −8.47% | −6.31% | 4/10 |
| PHP | 6 | −14.45% | −5.03% | 2/6 |
| Go | 6 | −15.20% | −4.16% | 2/6 |

Java is the tell: **+29.64% total but 1 win in 5 and a median of −30.18%.** That's `lombok-3674` (+6.09 pts alone) making the whole language look good while four of five Java instances lose. Any per-language config tuned on that number would be tuned on one instance.

**By repo it's worse — the same repo doesn't agree with itself.** Only **5 of 14** repos with more than one instance are internally consistent:

```
laravel   n=5  MIXED   [+51, −5, −59, −124, +39]
tokio-rs  n=2  MIXED   [−114, +33]
lombok    n=2  MIXED   [−19, +71]
fmtlib    n=2  MIXED   [+62, −23]
prometheus n=2 MIXED   [+17, −75]
```

Same repo, same language, same tool, same config — swings of 175 points between two instances.

**So there is no repo type or language type that reliably wins.** That's the measured basis for the ledger already striking language/repo gating, and it's why I advised against the grouping workflow. The only grouping with real signal is **task kind** (gold-ADD = 54% of all drag), and even that inverts on GEM300.

Ruby 6/6 is the one clean-looking cell — but at n=6 against a ~100-point same-instance noise floor, that's what a coin flip looks like six times.

# entire-graph on Opus — final plan

## Context

The goal was **35% token savings on rep50, Opus, fairly measured**. You later relaxed it to the
right target: **stop the tool making instances worse** — a code graph should not lose. This plan
is built against that, after five investigations (two loser dissections, a capability inventory,
a 4-lens artifact audit, and an iterative fix workflow) totalling ~4.5M subagent tokens.

**The headline finding is not about the tool.** It is that the measurement has ~287 recoverable
sessions, an arm-skewed censoring rule, a content-blind gate, and four eg-favouring leaks — and
that the one payload block designed to answer the question losing tasks actually ask **could not
fire in the headline cell at all**.

Sign convention: **positive = graph arm saved tokens.** All figures rep50, Opus/max, 49 gated pairs.

---

## 1. What is true on Opus

| estimator | value |
|---|---|
| total (the reported headline) | +1.35% |
| **leave-one-out: drop `lombok-3674`** | **−5.18%** |
| median | **−4.16%** |
| 10% trimmed mean | **−7.65%** |
| t | **−0.17 — indistinguishable from zero** |

**The headline is one instance.** Every robust estimator says eg loses. Never quote +1.35% without
the LOO range and the median beside it.

**And the fair number is bounded ABOVE by this one.** Four eg-favouring leaks are recorded and
unfixed (§5). Closing them moves the headline **down**, not up.

---

## 2. Corrections to my own work — the full list

Recorded so they are not re-derived, and because most are mine.

1. **"eg verifies more than baseline"** — false. eg 545 harness runs vs baseline 576. The claim
   came from the 8 worst losers, a set selected on the outcome.
2. **"eg loses 14.49% when both arms build"** — regex artifact. A stricter definition gives n=17
   and **−0.89%**.
3. **"the metric rewards failing to provision"** — real on `bat-1892` only; **2 of 25 losers**,
   worth −1.06 pts. Refuted as a driver.
4. **"+35.06% reachable by loser repair"** — arithmetic artifact; the lift pool caps it at +21.21%.
5. **×0.54 persist calibration** — wrong; the validated figure is the regression **slope 0.822**
   (corr +0.916, R² 0.839). **This one moved projections UP by ~52%.**
6. **"Five consecutive corrections, every one downward… nothing has moved the other way"** —
   **false, by item 5 above.** It was four downward and one upward. That sentence was rhetorical
   overreach and is withdrawn.
7. **R-A zero-toll at +4.3% to +6.0%** — mispriced by **5.2×**. The first search lands at assistant
   turn median 2 of a median 85-turn session where `cache_read` is 12,231 vs a session mean of
   63,137. Correct value **+0.96%**, CI [+0.53, +1.38]; n to demonstrate ≈ **19,504 pairs**.
   It was also priced in the message model that §1 of my own document retires.
8. **The VERIFY collect-only probe as a new fix** — `EG_VERIFY_PROBE=1` was **already set in
   `run_REP50.sh:141`** and live during rep50. Also a no-op on 84% of drag (21/25 losers got no
   VERIFY line).
9. **"Retrieval/ranking is anti-correlated (gold at rank 1: losers 6/8 vs winners 2/5)"** — this is
   **n=13, p≈0.29**. It cannot support closing a lever, and it was load-bearing in two sections.
   Demoted to **not tested**.
10. **Context-budget arithmetic** — three inconsistent totals in one section; **3.59M (9.3%) of the
    budget was unlisted**, and the real reconciliation is that the 1.57M classified saving is
    offset by **+1.50M growth in that unlisted bucket**. That offset, not the headline, is the fact.

---

## 3. Why instances lose

**Drag −19.86 pts over 25 instances; lift +21.21 over 24; `lombok-3674` alone +6.09 (29% of lift).**

| | losers (25) | winners (24) |
|---|---|---|
| **pre-edit exploration** | **−46** | **−58** |
| post-edit exploration | +159 | −81 |
| post-edit harness | +50 | −88 |
| turns | +296 | −258 |

**The graph works pre-edit in BOTH groups.** Localization is not the discriminator.

**The discriminator is displacement:** label a session displaced if eg's shell-exploration count is
below its paired baseline. **Displaced & won 19/21 (90.5%); not-displaced & won 6/28 (21.4%);
AUC 0.838.** Sessions that call the graph: pooled **+6.30%**, median +12.61%. The 16 that never
call it: pooled −1.02%, median **−24.94%**. **Calling and displacing is the winning behaviour.**

**Task kind is the largest single concentration:** independent gold-patch labeller gives
gold-MOD n=36 **+13.59%**, gold-ADD n=13 **−23.19%**. **Gold-ADD is 8 of 25 drag instances and
−10.68 of the −19.86 drag points — 54% of all drag.** Caveat: **GEM300 inverts the sign**
(MOD −14.13%, ADD +0.86%), and the MOD/ADD pools have **never been LOO-tested** — the same test
that killed the headline. Do that first, offline, before spending anything on it.

**Neither repo nor language predicts outcome.** Language R² = **0.153**; only **5 of 14** repos
with >1 instance are internally consistent (`laravel` = [+51, −5, −59, −124, +39]). Per-repo or
per-language configs are not viable, which is why the ledger already struck that lever.

---

## 4. What to actually do — ranked

Every item is tool output or harness hygiene. None adds an instruction.

### 4.1 `EG_TOPK` 5 → 8 *(harness one-liner, no rebuild)* — **highest value**
**RELATED SITES — the only payload block that names "the other places this change has to land" —
cannot be emitted at all when `--top-k <= 5`.** rep50 ran `EG_TOPK=5`. So the block designed to
answer the completeness question that ADD tasks actually ask **never fired in the headline cell**.
This is not ranking, not a new verb, and not a payload-quality metric; it is a block that was
switched off by a numeric floor.

### 4.2 Fix `graph grep`: exclude vendored / minified / generated *(NEGATIVE bytes)*
It shells to `grep -rInE` over the worktree and filters **only tests**. On `prometheus-9248` it
returned one hit inside minified vendored `d3.v3.js` where plain grep returned a **clean zero** —
and a clean zero is actionable, one noise hit is not. Baseline pivoted on move 2 and found the fix
site; eg reached it at call 21. **~19 turns lost. The only measured case of the graph being worse
than no tool at all**, and the fix removes bytes.

### 4.3 Recover the 287 dropped sessions *($0, and it is the only free power on the table)*
**287 of ~1,560 arm-sessions produce no usage data and are dropped WITH THEIR PAIR — but their
token counts survive verbatim in the Claude Code transcripts.** 132 of 133 zero-byte `cc_out.json`
have an **empty** `cc_err.log`. Recovering them is a scoring change, not a cell.

### 4.4 Fix two gate defects that currently flatter eg
- **Turn-cap censoring is arm-skewed:** eg hits `error_max_turns` **2.75× more often** than
  baseline, and every such pair is deleted. Those are eg's *worst* sessions. Report censoring per
  arm beside every headline; treat a truncated session as a loss at the cap rather than deleting it.
- **The patch gate is a byte count**, so it admits junk: 20 patches over 100 KB passed, worst
  2.95 MB; eg shipped **1,892,106 B across 1,708 files** on `gson-2479`. Add `*.class/*.o/*.jar/
  *.pyc/build/dist/target` excludes.
- *(Verified NOT a problem: gate strictness is not inflating the headline — removing it entirely
  moves the pooled total by −0.15 pt.)*

### 4.5 Ship FILE OUTLINE by default *(+1,421 B, ~8× return)*
`internal/sem/search_outline.go` (217 LOC), flag `cli/search.go:1637` — **default OFF, absent from
`printHelp`**. Its own measurement: 77 targeted greps landed on a file the payload had already
named; 35 were immediately followed by a Read of that same file.

### 4.6 `search --format` default json → text *(1.79× byte reduction for real users)*
The parser defaults to `json`, which is **1.79× the text payload**, and the doctrine file agents
actually read prescribes the command **without** `--format`. Every real (non-benchmark) invocation
gets the fat form. Zero risk: `json` stays available explicitly.

### 4.7 Binary and default hygiene *(preflight, not a lever)*
- **`run_3arm.sh`'s default binary is missing every payload feature added in recent releases** —
  any cell without an explicit `ENTIRE_GRAPH` override measures a tool that no longer exists.
- **`entire graph verify` was not in the binary the headline cell executed.**
- The in-tree binary is **stale** (rejects `verify`, `changed`, `--path`). Rebuild before anything.
- Add a hard preflight gate on `entire graph capabilities --json` that aborts when the binary lacks
  the features the cell assumes.

### 4.8 Move the advice switch into the binary
The binary **hard-codes arm-asymmetric generic methodology advice** into the payload, and the only
way to remove it is a 9-pattern literal grep in the harness whose default is OFF. rep50 happened to
have it on. Fairness must not depend on a grep list in another repo — add `--no-advice`, defaulted
off for measurement builds.

### 4.9 DO NOT BUILD — all refuted this session
| | why |
|---|---|
| R-A zero-toll as a token lever | +0.96%, needs 19,504 pairs; and it removes the call in the cohort where calling *wins* |
| VERIFY collect-only probe | already shipped and ON in rep50; no-op on 84% of drag |
| MOD/ADD structural router | doesn't separate offline; `exact-symbol` already printed, identical on ADD and MOD (0.36 vs 0.36) |
| post-edit consistency hook | its fair form's biggest beneficiary is the *baseline* in `lombok-3674` = 29% of lift |
| new verb in the affordance tail | 0/66 adoption |
| anything needing a post-edit agent call | 42/49 sessions make none |
| better ranking · bigger payloads · graph-backed grep · renderer byte-trimming | closed; payload is 79.9% source, ~0.6% of session spend |

---

## 5. Integrity — before any cell

1. **Four eg-favouring answer leaks** are recorded in memory and unfixed. `bat-1892` (worst loser,
   −2.81 pts) made **12 references into `bat-3108`**, a later revision of the same repo containing
   the implemented feature. Measured: **2/49 eg sessions, 0/49 baseline.** Direction matters —
   closing these moves the headline **down**.
2. **Shared `/tmp` between concurrent cells** — `prometheus-9248` audited `/tmp/goyacc*` built by
   other instances' sessions. eg 3/49, base 1/49. Give each session a private temp root.
3. **`EMPTY PAYLOAD` detector is broken** — fires on sessions holding 7,757 payload bytes.
4. **`CC_TIMEOUT`** may have censored the right tail; if rep50 ran at 1400 s the paired sd of 0.494
   is an **underestimate** and every power calculation here is optimistic.
5. **`echoPresearchPayload` has no length check** (`cli/search.go:286`) — a zero-byte payload gives
   0 bytes on stdout with exit 0, the "announced but never shipped" failure class. The guard exists
   on another branch and is not on this tree.

**Validated clean:** 49/49 graphs present, 0 commit mismatches, 0 of 310 under 50 KB, caches small,
prompt diff 18 lines all of which are checkout paths.

---

## 6. Gates

MDE ~25–30 pts against a ~100-pt same-instance noise floor; 93% of losers flip sign between cells.
**No token claim below n≈50 in either direction.**

| gate | n | criterion |
|---|---|---|
| **V0** offline $0 | 0 | `mise run check` green; RELATED SITES fires at TOPK=8 on recorded queries; grep returns a clean zero on the prometheus query; 287 sessions recovered and re-scored |
| **V1** offline $0 | 49 | LOO / winsorised / trimmed re-score of the MOD and ADD pools — does MOD survive the test that killed the headline? |
| **V2** live | 12 | mechanism only: **displacement rate** (eg shell calls < paired baseline) up from 21/49; RELATED SITES present in payloads; no rise in whole-file Reads. **No token claim.** |
| **V3** live | 50+ | first token claim: bootstrap CI, and **total + median + trimmed + LOO reported together**, plus per-arm censoring counts |

**Winner tripwire (your instruction: abort at >10pt):** `lombok-3674`, `fmt-2457`,
`qutebrowser-c580`, `redis-11510` in every sample from V2. Compare only against a **same-wave**
control — never a previous cell.

---

## 7. Honest expected outcome

**No number is promised.** The two items with a real mechanism and no prior art are §4.1 (RELATED
SITES was structurally off) and §4.2 (grep noise where a clean zero existed). Both are cheap, both
are fair, and neither has been measured. Everything else in §4 is hygiene that makes the *next*
measurement trustworthy rather than moving the current one.

**The ceiling on loser repair is +21.21%** — arithmetic (the lift pool), not projection.
**35% is not reachable on Opus by any fair change**; the only intervention that would reach it is
an instruction to explore and re-test less, which helps a no-tool arm equally and is exactly what
the withdrawn −35% contained.

**If §4.1 and §4.2 do not move the displacement rate at V2, the honest conclusion is that
entire-graph is not a token tool on this corpus** — and the defensible claim becomes correctness
and latency, plus whole-file-read suppression (119 → 105 calls, median 5,125 → 4,081 B), which is
measurable at n=49 today.

---

## 8. Verification

- `cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph && mise run check` (fmt + vet + race + build; CGO for
  tree-sitter). **Rebuild the binary — it is stale.** Unit tests beside the grep filter.
- Offline replay: `results/<tag>/eg/<iid>/gq_calls.log` + `.payload`; re-run against the binary at
  zero model cost; assert the change fires **and** that nothing else moved.
- Harness deploys by temp path + atomic `mv` with a live-session guard — never overwrite a script
  a running session is reading.
- Every gate reports total **and** median **and** trimmed **and** LOO **and** Δturns **and**
  per-arm censoring counts.

Tested it properly, and the answer is **no — and this kills the last surviving lever**.

**Task kind (MOD vs ADD), put through the same leave-one-out test that killed the headline:**

| | n | TOTAL | median | **10% trimmed** | wins | **LOO** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOD | 32 | +4.38% | +8.90% | **−3.44%** | 16/32 | −0.18% … +10.52% — **spans zero** |
| ADD | 17 | −1.44% | −16.82% | −18.14% | 8/17 | −15.76% … +4.25% — **spans zero** |

Three things break it:

1. **Drop ADD's single worst instance and ADD flips to +0.60%.** The penalty is not a property of the group.
2. **`lombok-3674` is an ADD task that eg won by +71%** — dropping it makes ADD *worse* (−15.76%). The same instance that carries the headline also carries this.
3. **The labeller decides the answer.** The workflow's labeller gave MOD +13.59% / ADD −23.19% at n=36/13; mine gives **+4.38% / −1.44% at n=32/17**. A 36.8-point gap became 5.8 points on a labelling choice. That is researcher degrees of freedom, not a finding.

**Prompt/ask features predict nothing:**

| feature | corr with outcome |
|---|---|
| quoted error strings | −0.278 |
| traceback present | −0.229 |
| distinct identifiers | +0.150 |
| file paths named | −0.135 |
| code fences | +0.089 |
| prompt length | −0.027 |
| backticked spans | +0.013 |

So: **not repo, not language (R² 0.153), not task kind (fails LOO), not prompt text.** Nothing knowable in advance predicts whether the tool helps. That's the eleventh correction, and it retires the ledger's ⭐ "best current idea."

What survives is only what's *structurally* broken — RELATED SITES never firing at `TOPK=5`, `graph grep` returning noise where plain grep returns a clean zero, 287 recoverable sessions, and the arm-skewed censoring that currently flatters eg.

# entire-graph on Opus — final plan

## Context

The goal was **35% token savings on rep50, Opus, fairly measured**. You later relaxed it to the
right target: **stop the tool making instances worse** — a code graph should not lose. This plan
is built against that, after five investigations (two loser dissections, a capability inventory,
a 4-lens artifact audit, and an iterative fix workflow) totalling ~4.5M subagent tokens.

**The headline finding is not about the tool.** It is that the measurement has ~287 recoverable
sessions, an arm-skewed censoring rule, a content-blind gate, and four eg-favouring leaks — and
that the one payload block designed to answer the question losing tasks actually ask **could not
fire in the headline cell at all**.

Sign convention: **positive = graph arm saved tokens.** All figures rep50, Opus/max, 49 gated pairs.

---

## 1. What is true on Opus

| estimator | value |
|---|---|
| total (the reported headline) | +1.35% |
| **leave-one-out: drop `lombok-3674`** | **−5.18%** |
| median | **−4.16%** |
| 10% trimmed mean | **−7.65%** |
| t | **−0.17 — indistinguishable from zero** |

**The headline is one instance.** Every robust estimator says eg loses. Never quote +1.35% without
the LOO range and the median beside it.

**And the fair number is bounded ABOVE by this one.** Four eg-favouring leaks are recorded and
unfixed (§5). Closing them moves the headline **down**, not up.

---

## 2. Corrections to my own work — the full list

Recorded so they are not re-derived, and because most are mine.

1. **"eg verifies more than baseline"** — false. eg 545 harness runs vs baseline 576. The claim
   came from the 8 worst losers, a set selected on the outcome.
2. **"eg loses 14.49% when both arms build"** — regex artifact. A stricter definition gives n=17
   and **−0.89%**.
3. **"the metric rewards failing to provision"** — real on `bat-1892` only; **2 of 25 losers**,
   worth −1.06 pts. Refuted as a driver.
4. **"+35.06% reachable by loser repair"** — arithmetic artifact; the lift pool caps it at +21.21%.
5. **×0.54 persist calibration** — wrong; the validated figure is the regression **slope 0.822**
   (corr +0.916, R² 0.839). **This one moved projections UP by ~52%.**
6. **"Five consecutive corrections, every one downward… nothing has moved the other way"** —
   **false, by item 5 above.** It was four downward and one upward. That sentence was rhetorical
   overreach and is withdrawn.
7. **R-A zero-toll at +4.3% to +6.0%** — mispriced by **5.2×**. The first search lands at assistant
   turn median 2 of a median 85-turn session where `cache_read` is 12,231 vs a session mean of
   63,137. Correct value **+0.96%**, CI [+0.53, +1.38]; n to demonstrate ≈ **19,504 pairs**.
   It was also priced in the message model that §1 of my own document retires.
8. **The VERIFY collect-only probe as a new fix** — `EG_VERIFY_PROBE=1` was **already set in
   `run_REP50.sh:141`** and live during rep50. Also a no-op on 84% of drag (21/25 losers got no
   VERIFY line).
9. **"Retrieval/ranking is anti-correlated (gold at rank 1: losers 6/8 vs winners 2/5)"** — this is
   **n=13, p≈0.29**. It cannot support closing a lever, and it was load-bearing in two sections.
   Demoted to **not tested**.
10. **Context-budget arithmetic** — three inconsistent totals in one section; **3.59M (9.3%) of the
    budget was unlisted**, and the real reconciliation is that the 1.57M classified saving is
    offset by **+1.50M growth in that unlisted bucket**. That offset, not the headline, is the fact.
11. **"gold-ADD is 54% of all drag"** — does not survive leave-one-out, and is labeller-dependent
    (36.8-pt gap between two labellers). Task kind is **not** a usable predictor. Retracted, and
    with it the ledger's §1.1 "best current idea".

---

## 3. Why instances lose

**Drag −19.86 pts over 25 instances; lift +21.21 over 24; `lombok-3674` alone +6.09 (29% of lift).**

| | losers (25) | winners (24) |
|---|---|---|
| **pre-edit exploration** | **−46** | **−58** |
| post-edit exploration | +159 | −81 |
| post-edit harness | +50 | −88 |
| turns | +296 | −258 |

**The graph works pre-edit in BOTH groups.** Localization is not the discriminator.

**The discriminator is displacement:** label a session displaced if eg's shell-exploration count is
below its paired baseline. **Displaced & won 19/21 (90.5%); not-displaced & won 6/28 (21.4%);
AUC 0.838.** Sessions that call the graph: pooled **+6.30%**, median +12.61%. The 16 that never
call it: pooled −1.02%, median **−24.94%**. **Calling and displacing is the winning behaviour.**

**Task kind does NOT predict outcome — this retires the ledger's best remaining idea.**
Put through the same leave-one-out test that killed the headline:

| | n | TOTAL | median | 10% trimmed | wins | LOO range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOD | 32 | +4.38% | +8.90% | **−3.44%** | 16/32 | −0.18% … +10.52% — **spans zero** |
| ADD | 17 | −1.44% | −16.82% | −18.14% | 8/17 | −15.76% … +4.25% — **spans zero** |

Three independent breaks: (a) dropping ADD's worst instance flips ADD to **+0.60%**;
(b) `lombok-3674` is an **ADD** task eg won by +71%, so dropping it makes ADD *worse* — the same
instance carries both the headline and this; (c) **the labeller decides the answer** — one
labeller gives MOD +13.59% / ADD −23.19% (n=36/13), mine gives +4.38% / −1.44% (n=32/17). A
36.8-pt gap collapses to 5.8 pt on a labelling choice. GEM300 also inverts the sign.
**Do not build a MOD/ADD router or spend on a classifier.**

**No prompt/ask feature predicts the outcome either:** quoted error strings −0.278, traceback
−0.229, distinct identifiers +0.150, file paths named −0.135, code fences +0.089, prompt length
−0.027, backticked spans +0.013.

**Neither repo nor language predicts outcome.** Language R² = **0.153**; only **5 of 14** repos
with >1 instance are internally consistent (`laravel` = [+51, −5, −59, −124, +39]). Per-repo or
per-language configs are not viable, which is why the ledger already struck that lever.

---

## 4. What to actually do — ranked

Every item is tool output or harness hygiene. None adds an instruction.

### 4.1 `EG_TOPK` 5 → 8 *(harness one-liner, no rebuild)* — **highest value**
**RELATED SITES — the only payload block that names "the other places this change has to land" —
cannot be emitted at all when `--top-k <= 5`.** rep50 ran `EG_TOPK=5`. So the block designed to
answer the completeness question that ADD tasks actually ask **never fired in the headline cell**.
This is not ranking, not a new verb, and not a payload-quality metric; it is a block that was
switched off by a numeric floor.

### 4.2 Fix `graph grep`: exclude vendored / minified / generated *(NEGATIVE bytes)*
It shells to `grep -rInE` over the worktree and filters **only tests**. On `prometheus-9248` it
returned one hit inside minified vendored `d3.v3.js` where plain grep returned a **clean zero** —
and a clean zero is actionable, one noise hit is not. Baseline pivoted on move 2 and found the fix
site; eg reached it at call 21. **~19 turns lost. The only measured case of the graph being worse
than no tool at all**, and the fix removes bytes.

### 4.3 Recover the 287 dropped sessions *($0, and it is the only free power on the table)*
**287 of ~1,560 arm-sessions produce no usage data and are dropped WITH THEIR PAIR — but their
token counts survive verbatim in the Claude Code transcripts.** 132 of 133 zero-byte `cc_out.json`
have an **empty** `cc_err.log`. Recovering them is a scoring change, not a cell.

### 4.4 Fix two gate defects that currently flatter eg
- **Turn-cap censoring is arm-skewed:** eg hits `error_max_turns` **2.75× more often** than
  baseline, and every such pair is deleted. Those are eg's *worst* sessions. Report censoring per
  arm beside every headline; treat a truncated session as a loss at the cap rather than deleting it.
- **The patch gate is a byte count**, so it admits junk: 20 patches over 100 KB passed, worst
  2.95 MB; eg shipped **1,892,106 B across 1,708 files** on `gson-2479`. Add `*.class/*.o/*.jar/
  *.pyc/build/dist/target` excludes.
- *(Verified NOT a problem: gate strictness is not inflating the headline — removing it entirely
  moves the pooled total by −0.15 pt.)*

### 4.5 Ship FILE OUTLINE by default *(+1,421 B, ~8× return)*
`internal/sem/search_outline.go` (217 LOC), flag `cli/search.go:1637` — **default OFF, absent from
`printHelp`**. Its own measurement: 77 targeted greps landed on a file the payload had already
named; 35 were immediately followed by a Read of that same file.

### 4.6 `search --format` default json → text *(1.79× byte reduction for real users)*
The parser defaults to `json`, which is **1.79× the text payload**, and the doctrine file agents
actually read prescribes the command **without** `--format`. Every real (non-benchmark) invocation
gets the fat form. Zero risk: `json` stays available explicitly.

### 4.7 Binary and default hygiene *(preflight, not a lever)*
- **`run_3arm.sh`'s default binary is missing every payload feature added in recent releases** —
  any cell without an explicit `ENTIRE_GRAPH` override measures a tool that no longer exists.
- **`entire graph verify` was not in the binary the headline cell executed.**
- The in-tree binary is **stale** (rejects `verify`, `changed`, `--path`). Rebuild before anything.
- Add a hard preflight gate on `entire graph capabilities --json` that aborts when the binary lacks
  the features the cell assumes.

### 4.8 Move the advice switch into the binary
The binary **hard-codes arm-asymmetric generic methodology advice** into the payload, and the only
way to remove it is a 9-pattern literal grep in the harness whose default is OFF. rep50 happened to
have it on. Fairness must not depend on a grep list in another repo — add `--no-advice`, defaulted
off for measurement builds.

### 4.9 DO NOT BUILD — all refuted this session
| | why |
|---|---|
| R-A zero-toll as a token lever | +0.96%, needs 19,504 pairs; and it removes the call in the cohort where calling *wins* |
| VERIFY collect-only probe | already shipped and ON in rep50; no-op on 84% of drag |
| MOD/ADD structural router | doesn't separate offline; `exact-symbol` already printed, identical on ADD and MOD (0.36 vs 0.36) |
| post-edit consistency hook | its fair form's biggest beneficiary is the *baseline* in `lombok-3674` = 29% of lift |
| new verb in the affordance tail | 0/66 adoption |
| anything needing a post-edit agent call | 42/49 sessions make none |
| better ranking · bigger payloads · graph-backed grep · renderer byte-trimming | closed; payload is 79.9% source, ~0.6% of session spend |

---

## 5. Integrity — before any cell

1. **Four eg-favouring answer leaks** are recorded in memory and unfixed. `bat-1892` (worst loser,
   −2.81 pts) made **12 references into `bat-3108`**, a later revision of the same repo containing
   the implemented feature. Measured: **2/49 eg sessions, 0/49 baseline.** Direction matters —
   closing these moves the headline **down**.
2. **Shared `/tmp` between concurrent cells** — `prometheus-9248` audited `/tmp/goyacc*` built by
   other instances' sessions. eg 3/49, base 1/49. Give each session a private temp root.
3. **`EMPTY PAYLOAD` detector is broken** — fires on sessions holding 7,757 payload bytes.
4. **`CC_TIMEOUT`** may have censored the right tail; if rep50 ran at 1400 s the paired sd of 0.494
   is an **underestimate** and every power calculation here is optimistic.
5. **`echoPresearchPayload` has no length check** (`cli/search.go:286`) — a zero-byte payload gives
   0 bytes on stdout with exit 0, the "announced but never shipped" failure class. The guard exists
   on another branch and is not on this tree.

**Validated clean:** 49/49 graphs present, 0 commit mismatches, 0 of 310 under 50 KB, caches small,
prompt diff 18 lines all of which are checkout paths.

---

## 6. Gates

MDE ~25–30 pts against a ~100-pt same-instance noise floor; 93% of losers flip sign between cells.
**No token claim below n≈50 in either direction.**

| gate | n | criterion |
|---|---|---|
| **V0** offline $0 | 0 | `mise run check` green; RELATED SITES fires at TOPK=8 on recorded queries; grep returns a clean zero on the prometheus query; 287 sessions recovered and re-scored |
| ~~V1~~ | — | **Already run: MOD/ADD fails LOO and is labeller-dependent. Lever closed.** |
| **V2** live | 12 | mechanism only: **displacement rate** (eg shell calls < paired baseline) up from 21/49; RELATED SITES present in payloads; no rise in whole-file Reads. **No token claim.** |
| **V3** live | 50+ | first token claim: bootstrap CI, and **total + median + trimmed + LOO reported together**, plus per-arm censoring counts |

**Winner tripwire (your instruction: abort at >10pt):** `lombok-3674`, `fmt-2457`,
`qutebrowser-c580`, `redis-11510` in every sample from V2. Compare only against a **same-wave**
control — never a previous cell.

---

## 7. Honest expected outcome

**No number is promised.** The two items with a real mechanism and no prior art are §4.1 (RELATED
SITES was structurally off) and §4.2 (grep noise where a clean zero existed). Both are cheap, both
are fair, and neither has been measured. Everything else in §4 is hygiene that makes the *next*
measurement trustworthy rather than moving the current one.

**The ceiling on loser repair is +21.21%** — arithmetic (the lift pool), not projection.
**35% is not reachable on Opus by any fair change**; the only intervention that would reach it is
an instruction to explore and re-test less, which helps a no-tool arm equally and is exactly what
the withdrawn −35% contained.

**If §4.1 and §4.2 do not move the displacement rate at V2, the honest conclusion is that
entire-graph is not a token tool on this corpus** — and the defensible claim becomes correctness
and latency, plus whole-file-read suppression (119 → 105 calls, median 5,125 → 4,081 B), which is
measurable at n=49 today.

---

## 8. Verification

- `cd /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph && mise run check` (fmt + vet + race + build; CGO for

- Every gate reports total **and** median **and** trimmed **and** LOO **and** Δturns **and**
  per-arm censoring counts.

exploration falls in BOTH winners and losers. It is exploring because one search answers *where
is it*, and it then has to discover **what calls it**, **what tests it**, **how to run that test**,
and **what else must change**.

| the agent's next question | eg has the answer | why it never arrives |
|---|---|---|
| what else must change? | RELATED SITES block | **cannot emit at `--top-k ≤ 5`**; cell ran 5 |

| what test covers this? | covering-test selection | present in only **8 of 33** payloads |
| how do I run it? | derived VERIFY command | same 8/33; and 21/25 losers got none |

|---|---|---|

| `graph grep`: exclude vendored/minified/generated | grep path | **negative bytes**, and fixes the only measured case of the graph being *worse than no tool* (prometheus: one hit in minified `d3.v3.js` where plain grep gave a clean zero → **~19 turns lost**) |

### 4.2 Spend it on answers

| change | file | delta |
|---|---|---|
| `EG_TOPK` 5 → 8 so RELATED SITES can emit | harness one-liner, no rebuild | +~600 B |
| FILE OUTLINE on by default | `search_outline.go`, flag `cli/search.go:1637` | +1,421 B — its own measurement: 77 targeted greps landed on a file the payload already named, 35 immediately followed by a Read of it |

answers*.

  (`root.go:576-594`) and is the only route to 13 relation types.
- Document `verify`, `changed`, `def` — 971 LOC of `def` is in neither agent guide.

  on a 9-pattern literal grep in another repo whose default is OFF.

Fair challenge, and it's the same one ashtom raised. There are two different things called "verify" and only one of them is arguably cheating.

**1. The `VERIFY:` line in the payload** — a *derived string*, e.g. `VERIFY: bundle exec rspec spec/foo_spec.rb:412`. The agent still runs it through Bash, gets full raw output, pays full price. That's what I just touched.

**2. The `entire graph verify` verb** — actually *executes* the suite and returns an adjudicated verdict capped at 2,048 B with pre-existing failures labelled. **That one I already ruled out of scope**, for exactly your reason: it changes the claim from "does a code graph save tokens" to "does a bundle of dev tools save tokens."

**Is #1 cheating?** Apply the doctrine test literally — "would this help an arm with no tool?" — and the answer is *yes*. But that test disqualifies **every** payload, including a ranked search hit. If "would it help the baseline" were the bar, no tool output would ever be fair, and the benchmark would be unrunnable.

The real line is **advice vs computed fact**:
- *"Verify once and stop chasing"* → behavioural instruction → **unfair** (this is what the withdrawn −35% contained)
- *"The test covering this symbol is `spec/foo_spec.rb:412`"* → a fact derived from graph edges → **fair**

**Where I think it genuinely gets uncomfortable:** the derivation is two halves. *Which test covers this symbol* is code intelligence — graph edges, legitimately the tool's job. *Which runner and what invocation syntax* comes from parsing `Gemfile`/`package.json`/`pom.xml` — that's build-system knowledge, not a code graph. That second half is the part that smells like a bundle.

**But here's what makes the reorder specifically clean:** it adds nothing. It moves an existing block above the agent's truncation cut. **If VERIFY is cheating, it was already cheating in rep50** — in 8 of 33 payloads — and the remedy isn't to leave it buried at line 80 where it's accidentally invisible. That's not fairness, it's a bug that happens to look like fairness.

So the decision is cleanly separable, and it's yours: ship the VERIFY block or don't. My change only determines whether the thing you already ship actually arrives. I'll finish the reorder so it's testable either way, and gate it default-off so shipping it stays a deliberate choice.

r"""Vendored / minified / generated path predicate for the tool-arm grep verb.

WHY THIS EXISTS (measured, prometheus__prometheus-9248):

The task was to make `atan2` a first-class binary operator — an ADD task, so the identifier does
not exist in the repo yet. Both arms opened with the same query:

    baseline   grep -rn "atan2\|ATAN2" --include=*.go --include=*.y .
               -> 31 B: "(Bash completed with no output)"

    eg         entire graph grep "atan2|ATAN2"
               -> 165 B: web/ui/static/vendor/rickshaw/vendor/d3.v3.js:1 | d3=function(){...
                  "(1 matches)"

`entire graph grep` shells out to `grep -rInE` over the whole worktree and filters ONLY test
paths, so it manufactured a hit inside a minified vendored copy of d3 where plain grep returned a
clean zero.

That inversion is the defect, and the direction matters: **a clean zero is actionable** — it says
"this identifier does not exist here, stop looking for it and pivot" — while one hit in minified
vendored JS is not. Baseline pivoted on its very next call to the error string from the issue text
and pinned `promql/engine.go:2089 scalarBinop` (a gold edit site) at call 2. eg never grepped the
error string; it spent calls 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 re-confirming atan2's absence — call 7 re-derived
this same d3.js hit — and reached `scalarBinop` at calls 21-22. **~19 turns, seeded by the tool's
opening answer.**

This is the only case measured in the rep50 corpus where the graph arm's output was WORSE than
having no tool at all, and the fix REMOVES bytes rather than adding them.

DESIGN, mirroring tools/_istest.py:
  * every directory alternative is anchored at a path-component boundary `(?:^|/)`, so it fires on
    repo-relative paths and never mid-word — "vendored_test.go", "my_vendor_api.py" and
    "distributed/" do NOT match;
  * only HIGH-CONFIDENCE vendoring is listed. `dist/` and `build/` are deliberately NOT here:
    they are product source in enough repos (and are the edit target in some) that excluding them
    would suppress real hits. The cost of a missed exclusion is one noisy line; the cost of a
    wrong exclusion is hiding the answer;
  * `vendor/` IS included: it is Go's standard vendoring directory and PHP's Composer target. Note
    the predicate is applied to grep RESULT paths only, never to commands, so filtering it cannot
    hide `vendor/bin/phpunit` from anything that needs to run it;
  * minified files are matched on the `.min.` infix and on source maps, both of which are
    unambiguous;
  * lockfiles are excluded: they contain every dependency name in the tree and match almost any
    identifier query, which is exactly the noise mode this predicate exists to stop.
"""

import re

# Directory components that mean "this subtree is not this repo's source".
_VENDOR_DIR = (
    r"(?:vendor|vendored|node_modules|third_party|third-party|thirdparty"
    r"|bower_components|jspm_packages|Godeps|site-packages|\.venv|venv"
    r"|\.yarn|\.pnpm-store|eggs|\.eggs)"
)

# Lockfiles: every dependency name in the tree, so they match nearly any identifier query.
_LOCKFILES = (
    r"(?:package-lock\.json|yarn\.lock|pnpm-lock\.yaml|Gemfile\.lock|composer\.lock"
    r"|Cargo\.lock|poetry\.lock|Pipfile\.lock|go\.sum|mix\.lock|pubspec\.lock)"
)

_RX = re.compile(
    # --- vendored subtree, anchored at a path-component boundary ---------------------------
    r"(?:^|/)" + _VENDOR_DIR + r"/"
    # --- minified bundles and source maps --------------------------------------------------
    r"|\.min\.(?:js|mjs|cjs|css)$"
    r"|\.map$"
    # --- lockfiles, anchored so a repo-relative or nested path both match -------------------
    r"|(?:^|/)" + _LOCKFILES + r"$"
)


def isvendor(path: str) -> bool:
    """True when a grep hit at this path is vendored, minified or a lockfile.

    `path` is repo-relative, matching how tools/_istest.py is called.
    """
    if not path:
        return False
    return _RX.search(path.replace("\\", "/")) is not None


# A single physical line this long with no whitespace is minified regardless of its path — this
# catches generated bundles that live outside any vendor directory. Deliberately generous: real
# source lines run long (URLs, base64 fixtures, long string literals), and a false positive here
# suppresses a hit, so the bar is set where only machine-generated output clears it.
_MINIFIED_LINE_CHARS = 400


def isminified_line(text: str) -> bool:
    """True when the matched LINE itself looks machine-generated rather than authored."""
    if len(text) < _MINIFIED_LINE_CHARS:
        return False
    # Authored code of this length still breaks into words; minified output does not.
    return (text.count(" ") / len(text)) < 0.02
